# WasmGC backend campaign: summary for Matt (internal)

Written 2026-10-01 evening, finalised 20:30. **Skunkworks: nothing pushed, no PR, no issue.**
Everything is local commits on joint `main` under `dev/lower-wasm/`
(≈45 commits since the plan). Ground truth: `dev/lower-wasm/STATUS.md`,
`DECISIONS.md` (D1–D120), `checks/items.tsv`, `FINDINGS.md`.

## Headline

**The plan's finish line is reached.** xsofy's real `main.lg`, compiled by
a new WasmGC backend walking let-go's IR, boots in the unmodified
`xsofy-shell.html` and renders a byte-identical screen to the stock-Go
lane at seed 424242 (settle-based scripted walk, identical on 4 consecutive
runs). Measured on the same loaded laptop (2026-10-01):

| lane | bundle raw | brotli | time to title | time to map |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **emitted WasmGC (lane 5)** | 497 KB | 140 KB | ~5.0 s | ~7.2 s |
| stock Go `lg -w` | 9.13 MB | 6.64 MB | ~10.9 s | ~16.4 s |
| TinyGo (2026-09-20 memory) | 2.3 MB | 1.27 MB | 8.7 s | 12.6 s |

No cross-origin isolation needed (JSPI sleep and read-key instead of the
SharedArrayBuffer ring). World generation plus 60 turns is byte-identical to
native lg on 20 seeds, plus 200-turn runs with exploration, descent to
floor 2 and player death. Module alone: 1.84 MB emitted → 409 KB after
wasm-opt → 109 KB brotli. fib(32) runs at 1.37× the hand-written probe
with checked arithmetic kept.

## Gates

| phase | state | evidence |
|---|---|---|
| 1 backend complete on scalar code | PASSED (D62), review fixes landed (D92–D96) | 7 rows + 148-probe adversarial review, all 11 bugs fixed or refused by name; tail calls via `return_call` |
| 2 runtime + collections | PASSED with one named limit (D127): 13/14 rows; core tests **265/273 (97%)** under the backend, 14/14 oracle programs, map-order 14/14, hash parity 0 misses, native tier 116 tests / 37.8k assertions, fuzz 2300 seeds clean; the red row is one `to-array` deftest | `corpus/wasm`, `corpus/review2`, `corpus/core-tests-report.md` |
| 3 xsofy headless world-gen | PASSED (D113) | `checks/world-parity.sh 20` 20/20 |
| 4 xsofy in the browser | PASSED (D120) | `checks/gate.sh 4`; lane 5 identical |
| 5 legmacs | not started, by design | new decision |

## What was built (dev/lower-wasm)

- `src/`: `lower_wasm.lg` (the backend), `driver.lg` (multi-namespace,
  `-source-paths`), `lw_rt.lg` (compiles the runtime through the backend
  into a content-addressed rtlib cache, tree-shakes), `lw_ext.lg`,
  `testshim.lg`, `run.mjs`.
- `rt/wasm/`: the runtime written in the constrained lg dialect over 43
  intrinsics: pvec, HAMT map/set mirroring let-go's array-map/HAMT
  (iteration order parity incl. its bugs), seqs with chunk parity, strings
  with exact Go float formatting, EDN reader, core natives, arrays, math,
  canonical XXH3, host/term. Runs natively under reference intrinsics too.
- `host/`: browser/node/wasmtime host, JSPI, the import ABI (`ABI.md`),
  an adapter that loads the real shell unmodified.
- `checks/` + `corpus/`: one match relation (`oracle.sh`), every item a row
  with a runnable check, corpora as files (op matrix, hash vectors from
  `vm.HashValue`, map-order oracle, 14 oracle programs, world dump), two
  adversarial reviews, perf report.

## Decisions you should know about

- D4/D24: runtime in lg over intrinsics, not deftype, not WAT. It paid off:
  the backend compiles its own runtime, and the runtime was tested natively
  before the backend could run it.
- D19/D30/D79: parity INCLUDING let-go's quirks (hash of `[]` vs `()`,
  the collision-bucket dissoc bug, ArrayVector vs PersistentVector rules).
- D91: no COI for the JSPI lane. D99: xsofy's deepest stack is 20 frames.
- D106: check speedups adopted (slot pool, parallel corpus/census/tier,
  no sleep-polling); attestation reuse deferred.
- D83/D109: variadics were not optional; landed as a `$FnV` subtype.

## Upstream-worthy findings (generic phrasing, not yet filed)

`docs/project_incoming/letgo-upstream-findings-from-lower-wasm-2026-10-01.md`
plus D94/D101/D116: checked arithmetic marked pure in the op catalog (DCE
drops throwing ops, LICM hoists them), constfold identities on non-numbers,
`free-vars` scope bug in ir.build (closures capturing same-named locals),
name-only self-call typing in typeinfer, LICM validate failures, the
collision-bucket dissoc bug, `()`/`[]` hash split, -0.0 hash, the reader's
empty-list meta leak, `require` silently truncating on an unclosed form.

## Open items and honest gaps

- Closed since the draft: P2.14 landed at 265/273; P0.1 landed (checks run
  2–3× faster, byte-identical); P2.GATE recorded (D127).
- `with-meta` on a variadic fn drops the variadic arity; identity hash of
  atoms/fns is per-kind; printing a fn is refused; `sort` incomparable-pair
  error may name a different pair; `*out*` rebinding is lexical.
- Perf per turn is 1.3–1.5× native lg on a loaded host; untuned.
- Everything was measured on a laptop at load 10–45; absolute times are soft,
  byte-identity results are not.

## What to decide tomorrow

1. Whether and how to surface this upstream (the backend itself is not
   secret: structurize's header anticipates it; the public why is size and
   speed). The upstream-findings dossier can go first, as plain bugs.
2. Phase 5 (legmacs: reflection, live compiler, regex, go blocks) as its
   own plan, or not.
3. Where the code lives long-term (D7 said out-of-tree first).

1+# IR pipeline coverage: xsofy and legmacs (2026-09-30)
2+
3+Prep for the WasmGC backend plan. Question: how much of two real programs
4+does the IR pipeline (`expand-all -> ir.build/build-fn -> optimize-fn ->
5+ir.structurize`) handle today, since a wasm backend walking the structurize
6+tree has no bytecode fallback.
7+
8+let-go `main` @ `4e769212`, lg binary `~/projects-new/3p/lg-bin/lg-4e76921230`.
9+Nothing in the let-go tree was modified. Scripts + raw TSVs live in this
10+directory (`census.lg`, `probe-dump.lg`, `summarize.py`, `*-lower*.tsv`,
11+`*-census.tsv`, `*-summary.md`).
12+
13+## Headline
14+
15+| | xsofy (72 files: main + xsofy/*.lg + xsofy/test/*.lg) | legmacs (30 files: main + legmacs/**/*.lg, examples excluded) |
16+|---|---|---|
17+| ir-stress `lower` (IR -> bytecode) | 823/1040 defns, **79.1%** (program files alone 68.1%) | 640/802, **79.8%** |
18+| ir-stress `lower-go` (IR -> Go bridge) | 1036/1040, **99.6%** | 802/802, **100%** |
19+| census: build + optimize + structurize, 0 fallbacks | 1032/1064 top-level units, **97.0%** (1008/1040 defns, 96.9%) | 783/816 units, **96.0%** (769/802 defns) |
20+| build-fn errors | 0 | 0 |
21+| optimize-fn errors | 2 (both `validate after licm`) | 0 |
22+| structurize fallbacks>0 | 30 units (31 fallbacks, all `:multi`-exit loops, 0 `[:goto]`) | 33 units (34 fallbacks, all `:multi`, 0 `[:goto]`) |
23+| nested fn* bodies (inner templates, optimize+structurize run here) | 392 units: 392 ok | 333 units: 331 ok, 2 fallback |
24+| arithmetic/comparison insts typed int/float/bool | 1192/2203 = **54%** | 657/1024 = **64%** |
25+| live IR values typed int/float/bool (all values) | 10.5% (`:unknown` 68.6%) | 4.5% (`:unknown` 72.4%) |
26+
27+So the front half of the pipeline the backend would sit on (build + optimize
28++ structurize) already covers ~96-97% of top-level fns and ~100% of nested
29+fn bodies in both programs. The ~3% gap is one shape, and the 79% `lower`
30+numbers are a bytecode-lowerer problem (`lower.lg` stack-position
31+materialization, `:try`, `:div`), not an IR problem; the same IR lowers to Go
32+at 99.6-100%.
33+
34+## What the gap is
35+
36+**Every structurize fallback in both corpora is a loop with two or more exit
37+blocks** (`structure-loop`'s `(= exit :multi)` branch; `count-gotos` found
38+zero `[:goto]` nodes). The canonical shape, `legmacs.buffer/row-col-of`
39+(dump via `probe-dump.lg`):
40+
41+```clojure
42+(loop [row 0, remaining offset]
43+ (if (>= row (count lens))
44+ [row remaining] ; exit 1 -> b2 -> b4
45+ (let [len (nth lens row)]
46+ (if (<= remaining len)
47+ [row remaining] ; exit 2 -> b5 -> b7 -> b4
48+ (recur (inc row) (- remaining len 1))))))
49+```
50+
51+The two exit edges leave the loop set through two different blocks (b2, b5)
52+that only rejoin at b4, so `loop-exit-of` reports `:multi` and the node is
53+emitted with `cont nil` plus a fallback tick. Other examples: `dag/walk-parents`
54+(`cond` with two non-recur arms inside `loop`), `fov/reveal-line`,
55+`check/shrink-failure`, `completion/fuzzy-score`, `dispatch/lookup-layers`.
56+This is a structurize limitation, not a wasm one: wasm's `block $exit (loop
57+$head ...)` admits any number of `br $exit` sites, so the backend can either
58+(a) teach structurize to accept multiple exits to a common post-dominator
59+(each exit edge becomes `[:break]` into a shared continuation), or (b) treat
60+the `:multi` case itself as "break to the loop's ipdom". Either closes 100% of
61+the observed fallbacks.
62+
63+**The two optimize-fn failures** are pipeline bugs, not coverage gaps, and
64+they show up identically in `lower-go`:
65+
66+- `xsofy.main/read-dismiss-key!`: `validate after licm: block #0 branch to b1 passes 0 args but b1 has 1 params`
67+- `xsofy.world/bfs-path`: `validate after licm: Inst #185 (op=:call, block=3) has cross-block ref 240`
68+
69+Both are LICM leaving the IR invalid; worth a let-go issue (search first).
70+
71+**`lower-go` timeouts**: `render/render-vfx-frame`, `terrain/place-lake!`
72+and (in an isolated rerun) `terrain/generate-level` exceed the harness's 5 s
73+per-defn cap in `lower-go` mode. All three complete under the census's 10 s
74+cap (build + optimize + structurize), so the time is in optimize or the Go
75+emission, not build. Not a correctness gap, but a backend that runs the full
76+pass list at load time would feel these.
77+
78+## What the backend has to emit
79+
80+Op histogram (both corpora, top-level + inner units, live values after
81+optimize): the working set is **const, load-arg, load-var, load-closed,
82+block-arg, call, add/sub/mul/inc/dec, lt/lte/gt/gte/eq, return,
83+branch/branch-if, make-closure/push-closed, try**, plus a tail of bit ops,
84+quot/div and unchecked-* in xsofy only. Never seen in either program:
85+`set-var`, `tail-call`, `bit-and-not`, `bit-not`, `pop`, `dot`, `def`
86+(`recur-fn` appears in exactly one xsofy fn, 17 insts). So `set!`, interop
87+`.` and in-fn `def` can be left out of a first backend without losing a
88+single fn in these two programs.
89+
90+Feature use (units using the op):
91+
92+| | xsofy | legmacs |
93+|---|---|---|
94+| `:make-closure` | 204/1456 (14%) | 165/1149 (14%) |
95+| `:try` | 32 (2.2%) | 36 (3.1%) |
96+| `:recur-fn` | 1 | 0 |
97+| `:dot` / `:set-var` / `:tail-call` / `:def` | 0 | 0 |
98+
99+`:call` is in 96-97% of units, and almost all of them go through `load-var`
100+of a core fn (`count`, `nth`, `vector`, `get`, ...): the runtime surface, not
101+the instruction set, is the real cost (see `reach.lg` for that census).
102+
103+**block-arg dominates the value count** (xsofy 116k of 158k live values,
104+legmacs 35k of 60k) because `build.lg` threads every live local through
105+every block as a parameter: a 0-arg `let` with two locals (`legmacs.main/
106+term-size`) produces blocks with 3-4 params each. For a wasm backend that is
107+just locals plus parallel copies on edges, but it is why the all-values type
108+split looks worse than the arithmetic split, and why `cleanup.lg`'s
109+compact-dead-params matters for emitted code size.
110+
111+## Types: what runs unboxed
112+
113+Over all live values, `:unknown` is ~68-72% and `:int/:float/:bool` is
114+4.5-10.5%, but that includes the block-arg flood and the control ops. The
115+numbers that matter for an unboxed fast path:
116+
117+- arithmetic + comparison insts typed `:int/:float/:bool`: **xsofy 54%,
118+ legmacs 64%**. The rest are boxed generic `+`/`<`/`=` on values typeinfer
119+ could not pin (map lookups, fn results).
120+- value-producing insts only (no block-arg/branch/return/push-closed):
121+ `:unknown` ~67-70%, int/float/bool 6-10%, other known types (`:nil`,
122+ `:any`, `:string`, `:map`, `:true/:false`, const-int, unions) ~23%.
123+- 60-68% of units have zero typed values at all: they are glue (calls into
124+ core, map/vector construction) with nothing numeric to unbox.
125+- `:float` barely exists (0 in legmacs; 661 values in xsofy).
126+
127+So a first backend can be "everything is `(ref null eq)` except typed
128+int/bool locals", and the typed arithmetic that exists is already roughly
129+half to two-thirds of all arithmetic.
130+
131+## Caveats
132+
133+- `census.lg` censuses what `ir.passes.pipeline/analyze-ns-forms` harvests:
134+ top-level `defn`/`defn-`/`(def NAME (fn ...))` after macroexpansion,
135+ macros excluded, one unit per arity. For test files that includes
136+ `deftest` bodies, so xsofy's 372 test units are mostly trivial; the
137+ program-only line is reported separately (95.4% units ok).
138+- Nested fn bodies are built by `build-fn` as `:fn-template` consts and
139+ `ir.lower` lowers them *without* `optimize-fn`; the census runs
140+ `optimize-fn` + structurize on them because a wasm backend would. All of
141+ them optimize cleanly, so that is not adding risk.
142+- `lower-go` for xsofy ran concurrently with the census (65 s wall); the
143+ isolated rerun of render.lg + terrain.lg reproduced the timeouts plus one
144+ more (`generate-level`), so treat those three as ~5 s borderline, not as
145+ load artefacts.
146+- Both xsofy and legmacs resolve `term`, `os`, `js`, `io` natives at
147+ `require` time; nothing was evaluated, so no terminal was touched.
148+- Numbers are as of 2026-09-30 on let-go `4e769212`; rerun with the
149+ commands below rather than trusting them later.
150+

1+# emit-wasm probe: host-capability extensions (2026-09-30)
2+
3+Companion to `../README.md`. Answers five questions for the WasmGC-backend plan:
4+overflow-check cost, wasmtime WasmGC, wasm EH, JSPI, boxing representation.
5+Report: `docs/project_incoming/` (emit-wasm prep measurements).
6+
7+`../lower_wasm.lg` grew four dynamic knobs (`*checked*`, `*trap*`, `*box*`,
8+`*guard-calls*`); with defaults it emits exactly what it did before.
9+
10+```sh
11+# from the probe dir (../), lg = let-go main 4e769212
12+lg -source-paths . ext/gen-ext.lg # writes ext/*.wat variants
13+cd ext && for m in fib fibl fib-chk fibl-chk fib-chki fibl-chki fib-chkt fibl-chkt fib-try fib-i31; do
14+ wasm-tools parse $m.wat -o $m.wasm; done
15+./bench-all.sh # Node: median of 3 processes x median of 5 reps
16+node chk-test.mjs # overflow helpers vs let-go's checkedXxxInt boundaries
17+node mk-wasmtime-bench.mjs && wasm-tools parse wasmtime-bench.wat -o wasmtime-bench.wasm
18+wasmtime run --invoke bench_fib wasmtime-bench.wasm # prints ns (WASI clock inside the module)
19+wasm-tools parse eh.wat -o eh.wasm && node eh-test.mjs eh.wasm # try_table / exnref
20+node eh-legacy.mjs # hand-assembled legacy try/catch binary
21+wasm-tools parse jspi.wat -o jspi.wasm && node jspi.mjs # Suspending / promising
22+wasm-tools parse ss.wat -o ss.wasm # core stack-switching (wasmtime check)
23+```
24+
25+Variants: `-chk` = checks via `$add_chk`/`$sub_chk`/`$mul_chk` calls that `throw $overflow`;
26+`-chki` = add/sub/inc/dec checks inlined at the use site; `-chkt` = inlined, `unreachable`
27+instead of throw (no tag); `-try` = every self-call inside a rethrowing `try_table`;
28+`-i31` = `ref.i31` boxing (31-bit range only). Generated `.wat`/`.wasm` are gitignored scratch.

@@ -0,0 +1,188 @@
1+# emit-wasm prep measurements: host capabilities and costs (2026-09-30)
2+
3+Probe: `dev/emit-wasm-probe/` + new `ext/` (see `ext/README.md`). lg = let-go main
4+4e769212. Hosts: node v25.2.0 (V8 14.1), wasmtime 47.0.3, wasm-tools 1.256.0,
5+deno 2.8.2 (V8 14.9), bun 1.3.13 (JSC), binaryen wasm-opt.
6+
7+**Measurement caveat.** The machine (8 cores, 4 performance) sat at load average
8+25-38 from ~22:10 onward (other sessions: Erlang beams, a headless Chromium, a
9+sibling `lg` job). The Node pass below was taken at ~22:05 while the box was quiet
10+and matches the README's baseline shape; a second 15-rep pass under load ran
11+~2.2x slower across the board but with the *same ratios* (fib ≈ chk ≈ try, i31 =
12+0.34x, checked fibl = 2.4x), so the ratios are solid even where absolute numbers
13+are not. wasmtime timings were only obtainable under load; min-of-7 is quoted.
14+
15+Harness: `ext/bench-all.sh` = 3 node processes x (3 warm-ups + 5 timed reps),
16+median of per-process medians. Baseline today: fib(32) boxed 21.6 ms, fibl(90)x1e6
17+27.3 ms (README said 28/68; the 68 was a slower day or an older lg output).
18+
19+## 1. Overflow-check cost
20+
21+Checks mirror `pkg/vm/numbers.go` `checkedAddInt`/`checkedSubInt`/`checkedMulInt`
22+(sign-xor for add/sub; half-width fast path + MIN*-1 guard + divide-back for
23+mul; `i64.div_s` traps on MIN/-1 so the guard must precede it). `inc`/`dec` are
24+checked too (OP_INC uses checkedAddInt). Three emission shapes, selected by
25+`lower-wasm/*checked*` / `*trap*`:
26+
27+| variant | mechanism | fib(32) boxed, Node | fibl(90)x1e6, Node | fib(32) wasmtime (loaded, min) | fibl wasmtime (loaded, min) |
28+|---|---|---|---|---|---|
29+| unchecked (control) | `i64.add` | **21.6 ms** | **27.3 ms** | 86.5 ms | 123 ms |
30+| `-chk`: helper calls, `throw $overflow` | `call $add_chk` | 21.5 ms | 64.6 ms | — | — |
31+| `-chki`: inline checks, `throw` | xor/and/lt_s + `(if (then (throw)))` | 21.6 ms | 65.0 ms | 240 ms (2.8x) | 195 ms (1.6x) |
32+| `-chkt`: inline checks, `unreachable` | same, trap instead of throw | 21.6 ms | 63.8 ms | 91.7 ms (1.06x) | 187 ms (1.5x) |
33+
34+Correctness (`ext/chk-test.mjs`): MAX+1, MIN-1, MIN-1 (sub), 0-MIN, MIN*-1,
35+-1*MIN, 2^32*2^31, 3037000500^2 all throw `WebAssembly.Exception` with
36+`e.is($overflow)`; MAX+0, MAX-MAX, 2^31*2^31, 3037000499^2, 0*MIN, (-2^31)^2 return
37+the right value. `fibl(91)` = 4660046610375530309 in both wasm and lg; `fibl(92)`
38+throws in wasm and raises `ExecutionError: integer overflow` in lg (the loop
39+computes fib(93) one step ahead), and the unchecked module silently wraps
40+`fibl(93)` to -6246583658587674878.
41+
42+Findings:
43+- **Node: zero cost on the boxed recursive path** (allocation dominates), **2.4x
44+ on the tight unboxed loop**: fibl runs at ~1 cycle/iteration unchecked (27 ns
45+ per 90-iteration call), so two extra ALU ops + a branch on the loop-carried
46+ chain really do cost ~1.3 cycles each. Helper-call vs inline vs trap are
47+ indistinguishable in V8 (TurboFan inlines the helpers).
48+- **wasmtime: the `throw` itself is expensive, not the check.** Inline checks
49+ with `unreachable` cost ~6% on fib; the same checks with `throw` cost 2.8x.
50+ The checked fibl loop costs 1.5x either way. If a wasmtime target matters,
51+ route overflow through a trap or a host call rather than a wasm `throw` in
52+ hot functions.
53+- Throwing used tag `$overflow` (no payload). EH was not a problem in Node;
54+ under wasmtime it validates and runs but see Q3 for the uncaught form.
55+
56+## 2. wasmtime 47 and WasmGC
57+
58+| run | command | result |
59+|---|---|---|
60+| fibl(90), plain | `wasmtime run --invoke fibl fibl.wasm 90` | `2880067194370816120` (warns `--invoke` with args/returns is experimental) |
61+| fib(20), plain | `wasmtime run --invoke fib fib.wasm 20` | prints `<anyref>` (can't print a GC ref; module validates and runs) |
62+| `-W gc=y` | same + flag | identical; **gc is on by default in 47** |
63+| `-W gc=n` | | `failed to parse WebAssembly module` (struct types rejected) |
64+| i64 args via `--invoke` | | **work** (`90`, `20` parsed as i64) |
65+
66+Timing used `ext/mk-wasmtime-bench.mjs`, which splices the generated `$self`
67+functions into a module with `wasi_snapshot_preview1.clock_time_get`, so
68+`--invoke bench_fib` / `bench_fibl` print elapsed ns from inside wasm (no host
69+timer, no GC-ref returns). Same module run in Node with a `clock_time_get` shim.
70+
71+| | wasmtime (quiet, 3 runs) | wasmtime (loaded, min of 7) | Node, same module (quiet) |
72+|---|---|---|---|
73+| fib(32) boxed | 53.3 / 54.9 / 68.4 ms | 86.5 ms | 25.0 / 25.3 ms |
74+| fibl(90)x1e6 | 79.9 / 83.1 / 89.8 ms | 123 ms | 27.7 / 29.6 ms |
75+| fib(32) i31 | — | 35.1 ms | 17.3 ms (loaded) |
76+
77+wasmtime is ~2-3x slower than V8 on both shapes (Cranelift struct allocation and
78+the `ref.cast` per unbox; no inlining of `$rt_add`). WasmGC validates and runs
79+without flags; `--invoke` is enough for i64-arg functions.
80+
81+## 3. Wasm exception handling
82+
83+`ext/eh.wat`: `(tag $e (param i64))`, `$inner` throws when x<0, `$mid` is an
84+untouched middle frame, exports catch in the outer frame via `try_table`:
85+`run` uses `(catch $e $h)` (payload on stack, returns 1000+x), `run_ref` uses
86+`(catch_all_ref $h)` + `throw_ref` to rethrow for x<-100.
87+
88+| host | current EH (`try_table`/exnref) | legacy `try`/`catch` |
89+|---|---|---|
90+| wasm-tools 1.256 | parses + validates, no flags | **text form no longer parses** (`(do` rejected); binary validates only with `-f legacy-exceptions` |
91+| Node 25, no flags | `run(5)=11 run(-3)=997 run_ref(5)=11 run_ref(-3)=7 run_ref(-500)` rethrows as `WebAssembly.Exception` | **accepted** (hand-assembled binary, `ext/eh-legacy.mjs`): `run(5)=10 run(-3)=997`; `--experimental-wasm-legacy-eh` defaults to true |
92+| wasmtime 47 | **runs with no flag** (exceptions on by default); `-W exceptions=n` rejects the module; an uncaught throw surfaces as `error while executing at wasm backtrace` | **rejected**: `failed to compile ... WebAssembly translation error`; no `legacy-exceptions` -W option exists |
93+
94+Cost of a `try_table` around a non-throwing hot call (`*guard-calls*`: every
95+`fib` self-call wrapped in `(block $done (throw_ref (block $caught (result exnref)
96+(br $done (try_table (catch_all_ref $caught) (call $self ...))))))`):
97+
98+| | fib(32) Node |
99+|---|---|
100+| no try | 21.6 ms |
101+| try_table around both self-calls | 22.1 ms (quiet) / 49.0 vs 50.8 ms (loaded) |
102+
103+Within noise: V8 does not charge for an installed handler. Not measured under
104+wasmtime (Q1 suggests the throw site, not the handler, is where Cranelift pays).
105+
106+## 4. JSPI / async sleep
107+
108+`ext/jspi.wat` imports `env.sleep(ms)`; `run(x)` calls `d3 -> d2 -> d1 -> sleep`
109+with a live local at every level (`run(x) = (x+100) + 10x + 1`), and `loop_sum`
110+sleeps inside each loop iteration. `ext/jspi.mjs` wraps the import in
111+`new WebAssembly.Suspending(ms => new Promise(...))` and the exports in
112+`WebAssembly.promising`.
113+
114+| host | flag | result |
115+|---|---|---|
116+| Node 25.2 | **none** | `run(5)` returns a Promise synchronously after 1 sleep; resolves to 156 after 6.1 ms (5 ms sleep); `Promise.all([run(1), loop_sum(10)])` interleaves two suspended stacks -> 112 and 45, 12 sleeps total; calling the raw export without `promising` throws `SuspendError: trying to suspend without WebAssembly.promising` |
117+| Deno 2.8 (V8 14.9) | none | same results |
118+| Bun 1.3 (JSC) | none | same results |
119+| wasmtime 47, `-W stack-switching=y` | | module with `cont`/`cont.new`/`resume`/`suspend` (`ext/ss.wat`, validates with `wasm-tools validate -f stack-switching`): **`the wasm_stack_switching feature is not supported on this compiler configuration`** (Cranelift on aarch64-apple-darwin); without the flag `failed to parse WebAssembly module`. Core stack switching is not usable in this wasmtime; its async path is the component-model one |
120+| Node, core stack-switching | `--experimental-wasm-wasmfx` | compiles the type section but my `(on $yield $on_yield)` handler shape failed validation in V8 (`handler generates 1 operand, target block returns 2`) where wasm-tools accepted it; not pursued, JSPI is the shipping API |
121+
122+JSPI is the answer for `(<!! (timeout ms))`: no flags on any JS host, nested
123+depth 3 and loop state survive, multiple suspended stacks coexist.
124+
125+## 5. Boxing representation
126+
127+`lower-wasm/*box*` selects `(struct.new $Int)` vs `(i32.wrap_i64) (ref.i31)` /
128+`(ref.cast (ref i31)) (i31.get_s) (i64.extend_i32_s)`.
129+
130+| representation | fib(32) Node (quiet) | fib(32) Node (loaded, 15 reps, median/min) | fib(32) wasmtime (loaded, min) | after `wasm-opt -O3` (loaded) |
131+|---|---|---|---|---|
132+| `(struct.new $Int)` boxed | **21.6 ms** | 50.8 / 46.0 ms | 86.5 ms | 49.2 / 42.0 ms |
133+| `i31ref` boxed | **7.5 ms** (0.35x) | 17.4 / 15.5 ms | 35.1 ms | 16.6 / 14.7 ms |
134+| i64 unboxed (fibl path, different algorithm) | 27.3 ms per 1e6 calls of a 90-iteration loop, i.e. ~0.3 ns/iteration | | | |
135+
136+`i31ref` is 2.9x faster than struct boxing in V8 and 2.5x in wasmtime, with the
137+range limit: 31-bit signed (-2^30..2^30-1); fib(32)=2178309 fits, fib(90) does
138+not. A real backend wants the Clojure/Java-style hybrid: `i31` when the value
139+fits, `$Int` struct otherwise, with `ref.test (ref i31)` on unbox. The unboxed
140+path is the actual target for `^long`-typed code; boxing only matters at the
141+boundary. `wasm-opt -O3` changed nothing on either shape (it can't elide the
142+allocation across the recursive call).
143+
144+## Exact commands
145+
146+```sh
147+cd ~/projects-new/3p/joint-xsofy/dev/emit-wasm-probe
148+LG=~/projects-new/3p/lg-bin/lg-4e76921230
149+$LG -source-paths . gen.lg && for m in fib fibl; do wasm-tools parse $m.wat -o $m.wasm; done && node run.mjs
150+$LG -source-paths . ext/gen-ext.lg
151+cd ext && for m in fib fibl fib-chk fibl-chk fib-chki fibl-chki fib-chkt fibl-chkt fib-try fib-i31; do wasm-tools parse $m.wat -o $m.wasm; done
152+./bench-all.sh # Q1, Q3 (fib-try), Q5 (fib-i31); REPS=15 for the loaded pass
153+node chk-test.mjs # Q1 boundary checks (exports $add_chk etc. from fibl-chk.wat)
154+node mk-wasmtime-bench.mjs && wasm-tools parse wasmtime-bench.wat -o wasmtime-bench.wasm
155+node mk-wasmtime-bench.mjs fib-chki.wat fibl-chki.wat wasmtime-bench-chk.wat
156+node mk-wasmtime-bench.mjs fib-chkt.wat fibl-chkt.wat wasmtime-bench-chkt.wat
157+node mk-wasmtime-bench.mjs fib-i31.wat fibl.wat wasmtime-bench-i31.wat
158+wasmtime run --invoke fibl fibl.wasm 90; wasmtime run --invoke fib fib.wasm 20
159+wasmtime run --invoke bench_fib wasmtime-bench.wasm # ns; also bench_fibl, -W gc=y|n
160+wasm-tools parse eh.wat -o eh.wasm && wasm-tools validate eh.wasm && node eh-test.mjs eh.wasm
161+wasmtime run --invoke run eh.wasm -3; wasmtime run --invoke run_ref eh.wasm -500; wasmtime run -W exceptions=n --invoke run eh.wasm 5
162+node eh-legacy.mjs; wasm-tools validate -f legacy-exceptions eh-legacy.wasm; wasmtime run --invoke run eh-legacy.wasm 5
163+wasm-tools parse jspi.wat -o jspi.wasm && node jspi.mjs && deno run --allow-read jspi.mjs && bun jspi.mjs
164+wasm-tools parse ss.wat -o ss.wasm && wasm-tools validate -f stack-switching,exceptions,function-references,gc ss.wasm
165+wasmtime run -W stack-switching=y --invoke run ss.wasm
166+/opt/homebrew/opt/binaryen/bin/wasm-opt --enable-gc --enable-reference-types -O3 fib.wasm -o fib-opt.wasm
167+```
168+
169+## Surprises / workarounds
170+
171+- wasm-tools 1.256 dropped the legacy `try`/`do`/`catch` *text* syntax; to test
172+ host acceptance I hand-assembled the binary (`ext/eh-legacy.mjs`). Node still
173+ accepts legacy EH by default; wasmtime 47 does not at all.
174+- wasmtime 47 has gc and exceptions enabled by default; `-W gc=y` is a no-op.
175+ `--invoke` takes i64 args fine but prints GC refs as `<anyref>`, hence the
176+ WASI-clock bench module.
177+- wasmtime `-W stack-switching=y` fails with "not supported on this compiler
178+ configuration" on aarch64-apple-darwin, so Q4's wasmtime half is a dead end.
179+- Under wasmtime a `throw` site in a hot function costs 2.8x (fib) while the
180+ identical check ending in `unreachable` costs 6%; V8 shows no difference.
181+- The README's stated baseline (28 / 68 ms) did not reproduce: today's quiet
182+ numbers are 21.6 / 27.3 ms on the unchanged probe output.
183+- The probe's `*.wat`/`*.wasm` at the probe root are *not* gitignored (they show
184+ as untracked); `ext/.gitignore` covers the ext ones. Edited:
185+ `lower_wasm.lg` (four dynamic knobs, defaults unchanged, control output verified
186+ semantically identical); new: `ext/{README.md,.gitignore,gen-ext.lg,bench.mjs,

1+# Brief for every agent on the lower-wasm campaign
2+
3+Read in this order: this file, `README.md`, `checks/items.tsv`, your item's
4+row, then the plan (`../../docs/project_incoming/letgo-emit-wasm-plan-2026-09-30.md`,
5+sections 3 and 4) and `DECISIONS.md`. Then read the probe you are extending:
6+`../emit-wasm-probe/lower_wasm.lg` and `ext/README.md`.
7+
8+Rules (not negotiable):
9+1. **Skunkworks.** Nothing leaves this machine: no `git push`, no `gh`, no
10+ issue, no PR, no comment anywhere. Do not commit; the orchestrator commits.
11+2. **Write only under `dev/lower-wasm/`** (and your scratch dir). The let-go
12+ checkout at `~/projects-new/3p/let-go` is read-only reference; the xsofy
13+ and legmacs checkouts too. Never modify them.
14+3. **Toolchain:** lg = `~/projects-new/3p/lg-bin/lg-4e76921230` (let-go main
15+ 4e769212; older lgs lack the `ir.*` API). node 25, wasm-tools 1.256,
16+ wasmtime 47, `/opt/homebrew/opt/binaryen/bin/wasm-opt`. Install nothing.
17+4. **Done means `checks/run.sh <your-id>` exits 0.** If the check script in
18+ your row does not exist, writing it is part of your item. A check must be
19+ able to FAIL: before you finish, break the feature once and watch the check
20+ go red, then fix it (record this in your report).
21+5. **Match means `checks/oracle.sh`.** Never compare by eye.
22+6. Shell is zsh in interactive use but scripts are bash: no word-splitting
23+ of unquoted vars in zsh; `mv`/`cp` are `-i` aliased interactively, use
24+ `command mv`. Background nothing that outlives you.
25+7. **Report** = what you built (files), the check command and its output,
26+ the falsification step, anything you could not do, and any decision you
27+ had to make that is not in DECISIONS.md (propose it; do not edit that
28+ file). Keep it under a page. No subagents.
29+8. **Never poll a long check with `until … sleep` loops.** The harness caps a
30+ foreground command at 10 min; a check that can exceed that (gate, census,
31+ native tier, corpus runs) is started with `run_in_background` and you act
32+ on its completion notification, or you split it (`checks/run.sh <one id>`).
33+ Measured 2026-10-01: 6.1 of 13.7 agent-hours were spent in sleep loops.
34+ Also: wrap any lg/node-heavy command in `checks/sem.sh` (a machine-wide
35+ slot pool, `LW_SLOTS=4`) so three agents' gates queue instead of
36+ oversubscribing the 8-core laptop (native tier: 90 s at load 10, 525 s at
37+ load 30+). Before running the full gate, `checks/affected.sh` tells you
38+ which rows your diff actually touches; run those first, the gate once.

1+# DECISIONS (orchestrator-owned; D1–D9 are in the plan, section 3)
2+
3+- 2026-09-30 D10. Module layout: one wasm module per program; the runtime WAT is prepended as text by the driver (as the probe does) until Phase 2 turns it into generated sections. Exports: `_main` (runs top-level forms in order) plus every defn by name.
4+- 2026-09-30 D11. Host imports for Phase 1 are exactly: `env.print_i64`, `env.print_str` (utf-8 ptr+len or array ref), `env.print_nl`; everything a scalar program prints goes through them. Phase 2 replaces them with `str`/`pr-str` in the runtime and one `env.write` import.
5+- 2026-09-30 D12. The runner `checks/wasm-run.sh <prog.lg>` compiles with the driver, assembles with wasm-tools, runs under node, and mirrors lg's observable behaviour: program stdout to stdout, exit 0 on success, non-zero with an `error: <message>` first line on an uncaught exception (so oracle.sh's normalised comparison works).
6+- 2026-09-30 D13. `.expected` files beside corpus programs are snapshots of native lg's stdout; `run-corpus.sh` fails STALE-EXPECTED if native lg no longer produces them, THEN calls oracle.sh. oracle.sh itself never reads them. Catches hand edits and lg drift the oracle would silently follow.
7+- 2026-09-30 D14. run-corpus.sh exit precedence: any MISMATCH or STALE → 1; otherwise anything short of all-MATCH (NOT IMPLEMENTED) → 2; all MATCH → 0.
8+- 2026-09-30 D15. `/` on ints yields ratios and, for MinInt64/-1, a bigint. Those are runtime value types (Phase 2). The div-*.lg op-matrix programs are skipped by P1.1 (run-corpus.sh honours a `SKIP` file in the corpus dir listing basenames) and re-enter at P2.7. `quot` stays in Phase 1.
9+- 2026-09-30 D16. Native quirks the backend must reproduce, not fix: (quot MinInt64 -1) = MinInt64; (- MinInt64) = MinInt64 while (- MinInt64 1) and (dec MinInt64) throw; shift counts ≥ 64 or negative follow Go (0 or sign), never throw; overflow message carries an `ExecutionError:` prefix, divide-by-zero does not.
10+- 2026-09-30 D17. P1.1's programs wrap every application in try/catch, so P1.1 cannot go green before P1.2 lands `:try`. Order within Phase 1 is therefore P1.0 → P1.2 → P1.1 ∥ P1.3 ∥ P1.4.
11+- 2026-09-30 D18. Hash hook contract: `checks/wasm-hash.sh <edn> <kind>` prints one decimal uint32. `<kind>` is required because `[]` hashes differently as ArrayVector vs PersistentVector. Non-finite floats are spelled `##NaN` `##Inf` `##-Inf` in vectors.tsv.
12+- 2026-09-30 D19. The wasm port reproduces let-go's hashing bit for bit INCLUDING its quirks (see FINDINGS.md H1–H5): empty-seq/[] split, -0.0 ≠ 0.0 hash, map entry hash = hash(k) ^ hash(v), the shared 64-bit finalizer across Int/Char/Float/BigInt, keyword = symbol + 0x9e3779b9. Parity first; fixing them is an upstream conversation after the campaign, phrased as plain hashing bugs.
13+- 2026-09-30 D20. Macroexpansion leaves qualified heads (`core/<`, `core/inc`); ir.build keeps them as var calls. The backend lowers calls whose target var is one of `#'< <= > >= + - * inc dec` as the matching IR op. `=` stays a call (polymorphic).
14+- 2026-09-30 D21. Legalize threads `:load-var` through blocks as block-args; values `ir/resolve-single-source` resolves to a var get no local and no edge copy and lower only in callee position; dead `:invalid` block params get no copy. A var used as a VALUE is an error until P1.3 (var table).
15+- 2026-09-30 D22. Booleans box to two `$Bool` singleton globals. Ints still box to `$Int` structs; the hybrid i31 of D2 is an explicit P1.1/P1.3 follow-up, not done in P1.0.
16+- 2026-09-30 D23. Driver: every defn body goes through `ir.passes.pipeline/expand-all` before `build-fn` (build-fn does not macroexpand). `ns`/`defn` forms are eval'd in a `user` ns so vars resolve; other `def*` heads are a named error; remaining top-level forms run in order in `_main`.
17+- 2026-10-01 D24. Intrinsics (`rt/wasm/intrinsics.lg`, ns `wasm.intrinsics`, 42 fns + `defstruct`/`defarray`/`deffunc`): the wasm instruction and typeinfer signature live in `:wasm`/`:type` var metadata so the backend and the coverage test read them mechanically. Operands/results are lg types (`:int`=i64, `:bool`=i32, `:any`=(ref null eq)); i32/i8 are storage only and each intrinsic's expansion carries its own wrap/extend. Mutable fields are `[:mut t]`. `new`/`call-ref` arity is fixed by the declaration.
18+- 2026-10-01 D25. No `wasm/throw`/`wasm/try`: lg `try` + `core/throw` (P1.2) for catchable errors; `wasm/trap` (uncatchable) for internal invariants. All runtime types go in ONE `(rec ...)` group so same-shaped structs stay distinct under `ref.test`.
19+- 2026-10-01 D26. Reference impl is stricter than wasm where wasm is silent (out-of-range i31, index ≥ 2^32, raw lg value in a :ref slot, out-of-range :i32 all throw). OPEN for the backend: bounds-check indices in i64 or accept the i32-wrap divergence; decide at P2.1-backend.
20+- 2026-10-01 D27. Host calls in the reference are deterministic (virtual clock advanced only by host-sleep; env from `*host-env*`). `bytes-of-string` is literal-only in wasm (`array.new_data`).
21+- 2026-10-01 D28. Gap: float hashing needs `f64-bits` (`i64.reinterpret_f64`), absent from the set and not computable in native lg without interop. P2.2-wasm adds the intrinsic; the reference impl may use a Go-side helper via a tiny native, or skip float rows under `--native`.
22+- 2026-10-01 D29. Map order spec = `corpus/maporder/SPEC.md` (let-go 4e769212): insertion-ordered array-map up to 8 entries (`arrayMapMaxEntries`, persistent_map.go:601) incl. `hash-map`; 9th key promotes to a 32-way HAMT (bitmap + collision nodes only, low 5 bits first, seq walks slots 0..31 depth-first); never demotes; sets are hash-ordered at every size. The port implements the node algorithms literally; collision-bucket order is history-dependent.
23+- 2026-10-01 D30. Parity includes the bucket 2→1 dissoc bug (FINDINGS M1). Go-map-sourced maps (json, transit, bencode, boxing) are out of the oracle's scope. maporder rows above 100 keys print head 16, tail 16 and a checksum.
24+- 2026-10-01 D31. Exceptions: try regions are lambda-lifted wasm functions; ONE tag `$lgex (param (ref null eq))` carries the thrown lg value; runtime errors are `$Err` kind 1 (uncaught message) reified to kind 2 on catch (`ex-message` then carries the `ExecutionError: ` prefix for overflow, none for divide-by-zero, as native); finally = catch_all_ref + throw_ref. Catch class table is strict (Throwable, Exception, ExceptionInfo, String + java./clojure.lang. spellings); other classes are compile errors.
25+- 2026-10-01 D32. The structurize gate rejects only trees containing a `:goto` node; `:multi`-exit loops are complete and lower (`:break` finds its loop by exit block). P1.6's metric is therefore `:goto` count, and `:switch` nodes (keyword cond chains) are P1.6's remaining work.
26+- 2026-10-01 D33. run.mjs runs the module on a worker thread with a 256 MB stack (native lg recurses past 3M frames; 100k-deep int recursion must not die). P1.GATE's timing compares like with like.
27+- 2026-10-01 D34. CONFLICT TO RESOLVE at P2.1-backend: P1.2 emits every wasm type as its own rec group (relying on structural distinctness); D25 requires ONE rec group. 28+- 2026-10-01 D35. Unary minus: build.lg turns `(- x)` into `(sub 0 x)` so `(- MinInt64)` throws in the IR path while native bytecode wraps (D16). Not distinguishable after build. 29+- 2026-10-01 D36. Closure ABI (adopted from P2.5's proposal; P1.3 implements it): a closure is an `Fn` struct with one funcref per arity (0, 1, 2, … as needed, plus a variadic slot later) and an env field; each funcref takes the closure itself as first argument. The runtime calls closures only through `invoke0/1/2…` helpers.

31+- 2026-10-01 D38. Value-model stand-ins are UNIFIED NOW, not at P2.2: boxed values are structs in the single rec group (D25): `Int{i64}`, `Bool` singletons, `Float{f64}`, `Str{bytes, cached-hash}`, `Kw{ns name hash}` and `Sym{…}` interned, `Char{i32}`, `Nil` = ref.null. `rt/wasm/seq.lg`'s Int/Bool boxes are the reference; phm's `vstub` HostVal side table is a test-only shim to be removed when P2.4-hamt lands (its author gets this message). 1+# FINDINGS (things learned that are not decisions; candidates for later, generic upstream reports)
2+
3+## Hashing (from corpus/hash/SPEC.md, let-go 4e769212, 2026-09-30)
4+- H1. `hashOrdered` counts EmptyList as one nil element, so `()`, `(nil)`, `[nil]` and an empty PersistentVector all hash alike, while an empty ArrayVector hashes differently: `(= [] ())` is true but `(contains? #{[]} ())` is false. Looks like a real bug.
5+- H2. Float hashing does not fold -0.0 into 0.0: `(= 0.0 -0.0)` is true, hashes differ, `(get {0.0 :z} -0.0)` depends on map size. Looks like a real bug.
6+- H3. Map entries hash as `hash(k) ^ hash(v)`; a map whose keys equal their values hashes to 0, same as `{}`, `#{}`, nil, false, 0, 0.0. Weak, not wrong.
7+- H4. Int/Char/Float/in-range BigInt share one finalizer: `97` = `\a`, `1` = `1N`, `MinInt64` = `-0.0`; `0.1M` = `0.1`; keyword hash = symbol hash + 0x9e3779b9.
8+- H5. `hashUnordered` has no callers; legacy `vm.Map` has no Hash() and falls back to FNV of its printed form (Go map order). Not reader-producible.
9+
10+## Arithmetic (from corpus/opmatrix, D16)
11+- A1. `(quot MinInt64 -1)` and `(- MinInt64)` wrap silently while sibling forms throw; overflow and divide-by-zero error strings are inconsistently prefixed. Parity for now.
12+
13+## IR pipeline (from the 2a census)
14+- I1. Two LICM validation failures on xsofy (`read-dismiss-key!`, `bfs-path`).
15+- I2. Every structurize fallback on both corpora is the multi-exit loop case.
16+- I3. lower-go reports "unsupported function body shape" on the probe's `fibl` loop.
17+
18+## let-go runtime oddities met while writing the reference intrinsics (2026-10-01)
19+- R1. `(not= ##NaN ##NaN)` is false, so `not=` is not `(not (= …))` for NaN.
20+- R2. `ns-resolve` returns nil even for public vars; core vars carry no `:ns` meta.
21+- R3. `bit-or` takes exactly 2 args.
22+- R4. Shifts follow Go (count not masked): `(bit-shift-right -8 64)` = -1. The wasm backend masks mod 64; the reference intrinsics mirror wasm, lg's own ops mirror lg (D16).
23+
24+## Maps (from corpus/maporder/SPEC.md, let-go 4e769212, 2026-10-01)
25+- M1. **Real bug:** when a 2-entry collision bucket loses one key, the survivor is rebuilt at shift 0 regardless of depth (persistent_map.go:552-562): `seq` still shows it, `get` misses it, a re-assoc inserts a duplicate key, `(= c (dissoc a \a))` is false. Pinned by `collide-map.lg` bucket-* rows. Generic upstream report after the campaign.
26+- M2. With ≤8 keys, `read-json`/transit/bencode-sourced maps take Go map iteration order: native lg is nondeterministic there (2 orders in 3 runs). Not on xsofy's path.
27+- M3. 11 constructed hash-colliding key pairs incl. an FNV-1a string preimage ("xe2tiazy" collides with 97, \a, 4.8e-322).
28+
29+## IR build quirks met in P1.0/P1.2 review (2026-10-01)
30+- I4. build.lg: `(- x)` → `(sub 0 x)` makes `(- MinInt64)` throw where native wraps; lower-go inherits it.
31+- I5. build.lg: unary comparison `(< x)` is treated as identity, so `(defn f [x] (< x))` returns x, not true. Silent.
32+- I6. `ir/resolve-single-source` stops at a loop header param fed by the entry value and its own back-edge copy; the backend replaced it with a cycle-following `src-of`.
33+- I7. structurize's `:fallbacks` counter counts `:multi`-exit loops although their trees are complete (no `:goto`); the 2a census's "3% fallback" is therefore an over-count of real gaps.
34+
35+## Seqs (rt/wasm/SEQ.md, 2026-10-01)
36+- S1. Range, InfiniteRange, Repeat and the vector seq do not implement Hashable; `hash` falls back to FNV over the printed form, so `(hash (range 3))` ≠ `(hash '(0 1 2))` although they are `=`. Reproduced.
37+- S2. `(count (seq (map inc (range 3))))` throws (ChunkedCons has no count); `(peek (cons 1 nil))` throws; a throwing lazy-seq thunk is NOT re-run natively (error cached). Reproduced except the last (needs ex-info, P2.7).
38+- I8. `optimize-fn` DCEs an unused op that would throw (`(+ (id MaxInt64) 1)` at top level exits 0 under wasm, native throws); `quot` is kept. The pass treats checked arithmetic as pure; lower-go likely inherits it. Parity gap, recorded not fixed.
39+- I9. The oracle reports MATCH when both sides fail identically (e.g. a reader error in the program); check line counts when a new corpus program "passes" first time.
40+
41+## From P2.7 (2026-10-01)
42+- R5. A map's or set's `seq` hashes over its printed form natively (450139980 vs the ordered-seq hash 21852162); the runtime still hashes it as an ordered seq. Open seam in phm.
43+- R6. Native bug: `with-meta` on `'()` breaks the empty list: `(= (with-meta '() m) '())` is false and `(vec …)` gives `[nil]`. Not mirrored.
44+- R7. Possible lg bug: an unclosed form makes `require` skip the rest of the file silently (9 deftests failed to register with no error).
45+- R8. Native reader stamps `{:line :column}` meta on a process-global empty-list singleton, so `(meta '())` is whatever was read last. Upstream candidate.
46+- R9. Native reader quirks reproduced: `0x-5` = -5, `018` = 18, `1_000` = 1000.0, `4/2` = Int 2, `\u-041` = rune -65, radix overflow is `invalid number` never BigInt.
47+- R10. Native: an exception thrown while `=` realises a lazy seq escapes try/catch; so does one raised inside a `try` placed in a vector literal. `(lazy-seq (lazy-seq (throw …)))` reads as `()` on the second access. Upstream candidates.
48+- I10. ir.build resolves later `loop*` initialisers in the OUTER scope (phm_test's shuffle-lcg shape); typeinfer does not fold `cond`'s `:else`, so every cond result joins with nil and boxes. Both worked around in the backend; upstream IR candidates.
49+
50+## Backend bugs from the oracle corpus (corpus/wasm/README.md, 2026-10-01) → P2.11
51+- F1 silent: closures capturing same-named locals in different scopes share the captured value (`[104 104 104]` vs `[100 101 102]`).
52+- F2 silent: the constant pool interns literals by `=` so `[]`/`()` and `0.0`/`-0.0` collapse to whichever was seen first.
53+- F3 silent: compiled `=` on maps/sets treats vector and list members as equal (native: false).
54+- F4 trap: `compare`/`==`/`sort`/`reduce +` with a float operand overflows the stack (boxed runtime calls re-enter).
55+- F5 silent: vector `=` short-circuits on identical elements, so `(= [nan] [nan])` is true.
56+- F6 trap: HOF twins (`map`, `some`, `mapv`) reject keyword/set/map callables (`(map :id ents)` is xsofy's shape).
57+- F7 trap: a wrong-arity closure inside `reduce`/lazy `map` null-derefs uncatchably.
58+- F8 trap: `max`/`min` or closures with float operands `illegal cast`.
59+- F9 compile error: a float literal where typeinfer chose i64 fails the program (`unsupported coercion {:from :float, :to :int}`).

1+# lower-wasm inventory (written 2026-10-01 21:00, end of the campaign)
2+
3+Everything here is on joint `main` (ADR-017: joint does not branch), local
4+only, never pushed. Skunkworks rule: `AGENTS.md` and memory
5+`feedback-emit-wasm-is-skunkworks`. Read with: `README.md` (scaffold),
6+`ORCHESTRATOR-HANDOFF.md` (how the campaign was run), `STATUS.md`,
7+`DECISIONS.md` D1–D127, `FINDINGS.md`, and the summary at
8+`docs/project_incoming/letgo-emit-wasm-campaign-summary-2026-10-01.md`.
9+
10+## Try it first (what Matt will want)
11+
12+```sh
13+cd ~/projects-new/3p/joint-xsofy/dev/lower-wasm
14+# 1. xsofy in the browser from the emitted module, real shell, Playwright-driven
15+checks/browser-boot.sh --xsofy # title + map, prints timings
16+checks/lane5.sh # byte-identical to the stock lane at seed 424242
17+# 2. open it yourself: build the serve dir and serve it (no COI needed)
18+host/build-xsofy-module.sh # compiles xsofy main.lg (~80 s) + wasm-opt (~2.5 min), cached
19+host/build-xsofy-serve.sh /tmp/lw-serve # real xsofy-shell.html + adapter + module
20+python3 -m http.server 8260 -d /tmp/lw-serve # then http://localhost:8260/xsofy.html?seed=424242
21+# 3. a plain program through the backend vs native lg
22+WASM_RUN=checks/wasm-run.sh checks/oracle.sh corpus/wasm/maps.lg
23+# 4. the whole board
24+checks/gate.sh 1 ; checks/gate.sh 2 ; checks/gate.sh 3 ; checks/gate.sh 4
25+```
26+
27+The first compile after any `src/` or `rt/` change rebuilds the runtime
28+library (~90 s, `src/.rtlib/` or `$LW_RTLIB_DIR`); later compiles take 6–15 s.
29+
30+## Layout
31+
32+| path | what | owner during the campaign |
33+|---|---|---|
34+| `src/lower_wasm.lg` | the backend: IR → WasmGC text; one rec group; intrinsics; closures `$Fn`/`$FnV`; var table; EH; tail calls; purity pins | P1.x, P2.1b, P2.11, P2.12 |
35+| `src/driver.lg` | file/multi-namespace driver, `-source-paths`, `--test`, var/namespace symbols | P1.0, P3.2, P2.14 |
36+| `src/lw_rt.lg` | loads `rt/wasm/*.lg` in README order, lg-defined let-go stdlib on demand (core, string, zip, data, set, walk…) from let-go at 4e769212, twins, ext-twins, rtlib cache | P2.1b, P2.14 |
37+| `src/lw_ext.lg` | backend-owned lg fills: variadic natives, regex engine (RE2 subset), format, json, dot interop, host seams | P2.12, P2.14, P4.1 |
38+| `src/testshim.lg`, `src/run.mjs` | minimal `test` ns for compiled test files; Node runner (worker, 256 MB stack, imports) | P2.1b, P1.2 |
39+| `rt/wasm/*.lg` | the runtime in the constrained dialect: intrinsics (43), pvec, seq (owns all boxes + kinds 0–37), phm/phs (array-map/HAMT parity), str (exact Go float format), core, reader (EDN), math, xxhash (canonical XXH3), arrays, host, term, lang; `README.md` has load order and the kind table | P2.x, P3.x, P4.1 |
40+| `host/` | browser/node/wasmtime host, JSPI sleep + read_key, key coalescing, `ABI.md`, shell adapter, build scripts | P4.0, P4.1 |
41+| `checks/` | `oracle.sh` (THE match relation), `items.tsv` (definition of done per row), `run.sh`/`gate.sh`, `run-corpus.sh`, `run-tests.sh`, `census.sh`, `world-parity.sh`, `lane5.sh`, `browser-boot.sh`, `hash-parity.sh`+`wasm-hash.sh`, `native-twins.sh`, `sem.sh`, `affected.sh`, `bench-fib.sh` | all |
42+| `corpus/` | every oracle as files: scalar, opmatrix, typed, control, closure, review, review2 (fuzz), wasm (14 programs + pending/), intrinsics (native tests), hash, maporder, natives, edn, floats, census, depth, host, xsofy (repros + size-boot), examples, seqs, core-tests | all |
43+| `tools/` | native inventory, twin manifest, reach wrapper | P2.8 |
44+
45+## Knobs (all optional)
46+
47+`LG` (native lg, default `~/projects-new/3p/lg-bin/lg-4e76921230`), `LG_ARGS`
48+(e.g. `-source-paths …`, oracle passes it to both sides), `WASM_RUN`,
49+`LW_PAR` (corpus 3 / native tier 4), `LW_GATE_J` (2), `CENSUS_SHARDS` (4),
50+`FRESH=1` (census), `LW_SLOTS` (4) + `LW_SEM`, `LW_RTLIB_DIR`, `LW_RT_DIR`
51+(overlay an rt/ copy to test a patch), `LW_MODULE_CACHE`, `SLOW=1` (native
52+tier full), `KEEP=1` (keep temp dirs), `LW_SETTLE`/`LW_MIN_MS` (lane 5).
53+
54+## Things that bit us (keep)
55+
56+- A `coverage/` directory anywhere is hidden by the global gitignore; we use `census/`.
57+- lg at main is required (`just lg-at 4e769212`); the `smoke: boot budget` step is flaky cold, rerun.
58+- `oracle.sh`: lg prints its error REPORT to stdout with ANSI; on failure the oracle compares the normalised first error line, not bytes. MATCH when both sides fail identically is possible (check line counts on a new program).
59+- `.expected` files are snapshots checked BEFORE the oracle (STALE-EXPECTED); `oracle.sh` never reads them. `SKIP` files take `# reason` comments.
60+- Committing while an agent edits `src/` can capture half a change: the backend REFUSES to load an rt intrinsic without an emitter (coupled changes land together; see f64-neg, D108).
61+- let-go's `examples/server.lg` and `mandelbrot.lg` hang/run for minutes natively: the examples corpus SKIPs them.
62+- The stock-Go lane drops/merges keys under load; lane 5 is settle-based (D119).
63+- Timings in this tree were taken at load 5–45; byte-identity results are the signal, times are soft.
64+- `LW_MODULE_CACHE` once produced two keys for identical inputs (unexplained; costs a recompile).
65+- The native tier is budgeted 120 s at load ≤ 10 (D81); do not trim tests to meet it.
66+
67+## Known gaps (named limits, all recorded in DECISIONS/FINDINGS)
68+
69+Ratio/BigInt/BigDecimal (D15); `defprotocol`/`deftype`/go blocks/`future`
70+(Phase 5); dynamic `binding` of user vars only via the var table, `*out*`
71+lexical; `with-meta` on a variadic fn drops the variadic arity; identity hash
72+of atoms/fns per kind; printing a fn refused; `sort` incomparable-pair message
73+may name a different pair; `slurp`/`open`/host file I/O; `sorted-map`/`sorted-set`;
74+`to-array`; regex outside the RE2 subset; `*ns*` rebinding.
75+
76+## What is NOT here
77+
78+Nothing was pushed, no PR/issue was opened, the let-go/xsofy checkouts were
79+never modified. The upstream-worthy findings are collected, generically
80+phrased, in `docs/project_incoming/letgo-upstream-findings-from-lower-wasm-2026-10-01.md`.

2+

8+ item, with the exact command whose exit 0 means done. `checks/run.sh <id>`
9+ runs one; `checks/gate.sh <phase>` runs a phase. Exit 2 = the check is not
10+ built yet, which is the implementer's job alongside the feature.
11+- `checks/oracle.sh` — the single match relation (stdout bytes + exit class +
12+ normalised first error line). Every "MATCH" in items.tsv means this script.
13+- Check speed (D106): `checks/sem.sh <cmd>` is a machine-wide pool of
14+ `LW_SLOTS` (default 4) heavy-process slots under `${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/lw-sem`
15+ (set `LW_SEM` to one path if agents' TMPDIRs differ); wrap leaves, not

23+ (advisory; gates stay full). `LW_RTLIB_DIR=<absolute dir>` moves the runtime
24+ library cache off `src/.rtlib` so tree copies on the same sources share one

1+# P2.3 / P2.GATE measurement: let-go core tests through the backend
2+
3+Measured 2026-10-01 on a frozen snapshot of the tree (git HEAD 1a65573 plus other agents'
4+uncommitted `src/` edits; md5 of `src rt checks` excluding `.rtlib` = `75daf80d25389c948ae06cae84d71697`).
5+The live tree moved during the run (a first pass on it differed on 2 files: `transducer_test`, `string_split_test`),
6+so these numbers are for that snapshot only. let-go test files at 4e769212 (`corpus/core-tests.txt`).
7+Per-file rows: `corpus/core-tests-results.tsv`. Nothing under `src/` or `rt/` was changed.
8+
9+## Totals
10+
11+| measure | value |
12+|---|---|
13+| files MATCH / run (oracle = `run-tests.sh` summary + FAIL/ERROR lines equal) | **20 / 44** as `run-tests.sh` runs them; 21 / 44 counting `chunked_seq_test` via an ns-named scratch copy |
14+| deftests passing under the backend (no FAIL/ERROR line) | **133 / 273 = 48.7%** as run; **144 / 273 = 52.7%** with the chunked_seq workaround |
15+| P2.GATE bar (>= 90%) | 246 / 273. **Not met**: short by 113 as run (102 with the workaround counted) |
16+| assertions | native 870 evaluated; backend 680 evaluated in the 39 files that printed a summary, 522 of them passed (no native failures anywhere) |
17+| timeouts | 0 (wall per file 11-21 s at machine load ~20, includes `sem.sh` queue wait; 7-14 s at load 3) |
18+
19+`chunked_seq_test.lg` declares `test.chunked-seq`, so native `require` looks for `test/chunked_seq.lg` and the
20+native side prints no summary. Run from a copy at that name it passes 11/11. This is a harness gap, not a backend one.
21+
22+## Failure taxonomy
23+
24+By file (23 non-passing files with the chunked_seq workaround, 24 as run; string_replace_fn appears in two rows, so file counts sum to 24 with it counted twice):
25+
26+| class | files | deftests lost | detail |
27+|---|---|---|---|
28+| missing native / stdlib twin (`TypeError: nil is not a function`, an unlinked extern; the message carries no var name, names below come from the `$ext_*` globals in the emitted WAT) | 14 | 70 | zip 20, data/diff 15, `.getBytes` 8, walk 6, set_ns 5, persistent_set 4 (disj, meta, set/difference, set/intersection), transient 3, math 2, update-keys/vals 2 (`core/meta`), lazy-seq? 1, map-entry? 1, with-out-str* 1, sorted-map/set 1, replace-literal-fn 1 (`str-replace-first`) |
29+| Phase-2 constant (compiles, throws when evaluated) | 3 (string_replace_fn shared) | 10 | `let-go.lang.Regex`: string_split 3, string_replace_fn 5; `(var x)`: def_meta 2 |
30+| whole-program abort at run time | 1 | 7 | thrown_test: `error: lower-wasm: Phase-2 constant var` in `_main`, no summary |
31+| harness / driver (`--test` mode, `run-tests.sh`) | 5 | 41 | quality.* not on backend `-source-paths` (35 deftests, `compile: unable to load namespace`); macro-state cascade (try_finally 6, `compile: unresolved symbol <deftest>`); no-ns files (top_level_do, harness_load_only: 0 deftests); plus chunked_seq (passes only with an ns-named copy) |
32+| wrong value (no trap) | 1 | 1 | file_var: `*file*` reads nil (`string?` false) |
33+
34+(129 deftests lost = 70 + 10 + 7 + 41 + 1; clojure_math also hits `+ on a non-Int operand (numeric tower is Phase 2)` once, behind the missing twins.)
35+
36+By error event (158 FAIL/ERROR lines in the backend runs): 129 `nil is not a function`, 20 `Phase-2 constant Regex`,
37+6 `Phase-2 constant var`, 1 `*file*`-related assertion false, 1 `ends-with? expected non-nil string` (cascade from nil `*file*`),
38+1 numeric-tower trap. There are no `thrown?`/`are`/`with-redefs`/`binding` harness gaps in this corpus:
39+`select-core-tests.sh` excludes `with-redefs`/`binding`, no file uses `are`, and `thrown?` appears only in thrown_test, which
40+aborts earlier on `(var x)`.
41+
42+## Top 10 blockers, ranked by deftests unblocked
43+
44+"Alone" = deftests that would pass once only this is fixed (assumes nothing else hides behind it; the rest are upper bounds).
45+Owner: backend = `src/`, rt = `rt/`, harness = `checks/run-tests.sh` / `src/testshim.lg` / driver `--test`.
46+Repros are plain lg, run with `WASM_RUN=checks/wasm-run.sh checks/oracle.sh r.lg`; each printed `MISMATCH` in this run (native result shown).

57+| 8 | `clojure.walk` twin missing (prewalk postwalk keywordize-keys ...) | 6 (4 alone; walk-on-maps also needs `sorted-map`, map-entry?-predicate needs `map-entry?`) | rt | port walk.lg | `(ns r (:require [clojure.walk :as w]))` `(println (w/postwalk #(if (number? %) (inc %) %) [1 [2]]))` -> `[2 [3]]` |
58+| 9 | a user `defmacro` whose body touches a program-level `def` (atom) fails at native compile time; the rest of the file is dropped and `_main` still calls every deftest, so the whole file is lost | 6 (try_finally, all) | backend driver (+shim: epilogue should skip undefined deftests) | evaluate program `def`s natively before expanding macros, or stub the failing form | `(def n (atom 0))` `(defmacro cnt [] (swap! n inc) nil)` `(defn a [] (cnt) 1)` `(println (a))` -> `1`; wasm `Executing macro #'user/cnt ... swap expected Atom`. In a test file: `run-tests.sh` prints `compile: error: ir/build: unresolved symbol b` |
59+| 10 | `core/meta` unlinked although `rt/wasm/core.lg:888` defines `meta` (no `:twin` marker, not in `extra-twins`) | 3 alone (update_keys_vals 2, set-with-meta); feeds def_meta and gold return_hint_metadata | rt | add the `:twin` marker or an `extra-twins` row | `(println (meta (with-meta [1] {:a 1})))` -> `{:a 1}` |
60+
61+Tail (12 deftests): `disj`, `disj!`, `dissoc!` 3 (`(println (disj #{1 2} 1) (persistent! (disj! (transient #{1 2}) 1)) (persistent! (dissoc! (transient {:a 1 :b 2}) :a)))` -> `#{2} #{2} {:b 2}`);
62+`map-entry?` 2 (`(println (map-entry? (first {:a 1})))` -> `true`); `clojure.math` twin 2 (`m/round m/sqrt m/PI ...`; `(ns r (:require [clojure.math :as m]))` `(println (m/round 2.7) (m/sqrt 16) m/PI)` -> `3 4.0 3.141592653589793`);
63+`sorted-map`/`sorted-set` 1 (`(println (sorted-map :b 1 :a 2))` -> `{:a 2, :b 1}`); `with-out-str` 1 (`(println (with-out-str (pr {:b 1})))` -> `{:b 1}`);

65+Harness-only, 0 deftests: files without an `ns` form (top_level_do_test, harness_load_only_test: `(assert (= 2 (+ 1 1)))` alone gives `native run printed no summary: ... unable to load namespace`);
66+ns/file-name mismatch (chunked_seq_test, 11 deftests pass once the native side can load it).
67+
68+Reading the ranking against the gate: pure rt twins (zip, data, set, walk, meta, the tail) account for about 62 deftests, so rt work alone reaches roughly 195/273 (71%).

@@ -0,0 +1,78 @@
1+# corpus/depth — D89: does xsofy's stack fit under JSPI?
2+
3+**Verdict: fits.** xsofy's deepest call stack, counted in lg fn frames, is
4+**20** (as of 2026-10-01, xsofy canonical checkout, lg 4e769212). The browser
5+budget D89 measured is about 5,000 frames of the smallest boxed shape
6+(Chromium 148: 5,000 pass, 7,000 fail; node 25 without flags the same, with
7+node-host's flags 1,000,000). The margin is two orders of magnitude even
8+after the allowances below.
9+
10+## Method
11+
12+`measure.lg` wraps core's `fn` macro (and labels `defn`/`defn-` bodies with
13+the var name) before xsofy loads, so every fn body xsofy compiles counts a
14+frame on entry and uncounts it in a `finally`. This includes anonymous
15+fns, named-fn self-recursion, letfn and `lazy-seq`/`for` thunks, which a
16+var proxy would miss. A fn-level `recur` stays a loop. The world must not
17+change: `measure.lg load corpus/dump-world.lg 1 200` and the plain
18+`dump-world.lg 1 200` print byte-identical dumps (20,831 bytes, checked with
19+`cmp`).
20+
21+Run: `lg -source-paths ~/projects-new/3p/xsofy corpus/depth/measure.lg depth 20 200`
22+(about 12 min). Raw output: `results-2026-10-01.txt`. Coverage: 20 seeds × 200
23+turns × three fixtures (bench/native.lg's `:wait`, `:autoex`, `:descend`), each
24+starting with `make-world 79 30 seed` (so world generation is included). Every
25+turn also runs `render-full` and `render-dirty` on the new world, with
26+`term/size` pinned to 100×36 and output discarded, and 0 render errors.
27+
28+## Results
29+
30+| fixture | min / median / max deepest stack per seed |
31+|---|---|
32+| wait | 16 / 18 / 19 |
33+| autoex | 16 / 18 / 20 |
34+| descend | 16 / 18 / 19 |
35+
36+The deepest chain (autoex, seed 16) is `update-world → autoexplore-step →
37+player-move → update-fov → compute-fov → cast-octant ×12 → blocked? →
38+transparent? → in-grid?`.
39+
40+Top 10 fn bodies by the deepest stack position reached: `terrain/in-grid?` 20,
41+`terrain/tget` 20, `hash/valid-codepoint!` 19, `terrain/transparent?` 19,
42+`fov/blocked?` 18, `fov/cast-octant` 18, `hash/conj-codepoint->utf8` 18,
43+`hash/conj-utf8-char` 17, `hash/u64-shr` 17, `hash/conj-int->8-be` 16.
44+The render path never gets into the top 20.
45+
46+**One non-tail recursion matters: `fov/cast-octant`** (recursive
47+shadowcasting), which reached 13 simultaneous frames. It is bounded by the FOV
48+radius, because each recursive call advances `row` and stops at
49+`row > radius` (fov.lg:23). The player's radius is `view-radius` 12
50+(world.lg:59), NPC perception defaults to 12 (percept.lg:35), and bestiary
51+light radii go up to 20. Everything else nests at most twice (`deep-merge`
52+over a nested map, `ai`, `damage-entity`, `encode-salt-into`).
53+
54+**Lazy realisation chains:** none of any depth. `lazy-seq` thunks from xsofy
55+code are counted above. xsofy's own `lazy-seq` uses are in `check.lg` (the
56+property-test library, which is not on the game path), and every `concat` is
57+realised at once (`vec`, `set`, `distinct`). No `reduce concat`
58+accumulation exists.
59+
60+## Not counted, and the allowance for it
61+
62+- Frames inside let-go natives and pre-compiled core fns (`map`, `reduce`,
63+ `update`, `swap!`, `sort-by`, ...). In wasm these become runtime frames
64+ (`wasm.seq`/`wasm.core` helpers, `$rt_invoke*`) between user frames, a few
65+ per HOF callback.
66+- The game-loop shell above `update-world`: `-main → game-loop →
67+ play/run-play-loop → ui/run-loop → step`, about 10 frames.
68+- Frame size. xsofy fns have more locals than D89's `down`, so each V8 frame
69+ is larger.
70+
71+A pessimistic allowance multiplies the 20 user frames by 5 for runtime
72+helpers, adds 10 × 5 for the shell, and assumes frames 10× the size of `down`.
73+That is 150 "big" frames against a budget of about 500 such frames. It still
74+fits, and the first thing that could break it would be a much larger FOV
75+radius, which grows linearly and visibly.
76+
77+D89's fix-in-the-backend clause (loops or an explicit stack) is not needed for
78+P4.1.

@@ -0,0 +1,105 @@
1+# let-go value hashing: port spec
2+
3+Source: `~/projects-new/3p/let-go` at `4e769212`; paths below are under
4+`pkg/vm/` unless marked. All arithmetic is wrapping `uint32` unless a step
5+says `uint64`. `rotl32(x,r) = (x<<r)|(x>>(32-r))`. Test vectors:
6+`vectors.tsv` (regenerate with `go run . > vectors.tsv`). These algorithms
7+are **not** Clojure/JVM-compatible, despite comments saying "matching
8+Clojure"; port these, not Clojure's.
9+
10+## Entry point
11+
12+`HashValue(v)` (hash.go:19) → `hashValue` (hash.go:23): if `v` implements
13+`Hashable` (has `Hash() uint32`, hash.go:15) use that, else `computeHash`
14+(hash.go:31): `NIL` → 0, anything else → FNV-1a over the bytes of
15+`v.String()`. The lg builtin `hash` is `int64(HashValue(x))`
16+(rt/lang.go:8886-8890), so lg sees the uint32 as a **non-negative** int.
17+
18+## Primitives (hash.go)
19+
20+| name | definition |
21+|---|---|
22+| `hashString(s)` :48 | FNV-1a 32 over the UTF-8 **bytes**: `h=2166136261; for each byte b: h^=b; h*=16777619` (constants :9-10). `hashBytes` :38 is identical over a `[]byte`. |
23+| `mixK1(k)` :81 | `k*=0xcc9e2d51; k=rotl32(k,15); k*=0x1b873593` |
24+| `mixH1(h,k)` :88 | `h^=k; h=rotl32(h,13); h=h*5+0xe6546b64` |
25+| `mixFinishLen(h,len)` :131 | `h^=len; h^=h>>16; h*=0x85ebca6b; h^=h>>13; h*=0xc2b2ae35; h^=h>>16` (Murmur3 fmix32). Note fmix32(0)=0. |
26+| `mixFinish(h)` :127 | `mixFinishLen(h,0)` |
27+| `hashUnencodedChars(s)` :67 | seed `h=0`; n = **byte** length. For each byte pair `(s[i-1],s[i])`, i=1,3,5,…: `k = s[i-1] \| s[i]<<16`; `h=mixH1(h,mixK1(k))`. If n is odd, the last byte: `h ^= mixK1(s[n-1])` (no mixH1). Return `mixFinishLen(h, 2*n)`. |
28+| `hashUint64(v)` :94 | in **uint64**: `v^=v>>33; v*=0xff51afd7ed558ccd; v^=v>>33; v*=0xc4ceb9fe1a85ec53; v^=v>>33`; return low 32 bits. |
29+| `hashOrdered(seq)` :108 | `h=1; for s=seq; s!=nil; s=s.Next(): h=31*h+hashValue(s.First())`; return `mixFinish(h)`. No length mixed in. |
30+| `hashUnordered` :118 | sum then mixFinish. **Dead code**: no callers in pkg/. |
31+
32+`hashUnencodedChars` really is byte-wise: it indexes `s[i]` (Go string
33+indexing = bytes) and passes `2*len(s)` with `len` in bytes (:67-78; the
34+comment at :57-66 says so). Non-ASCII therefore hashes its UTF-8 bytes
35+paired two at a time, *not* runes or UTF-16 units; `héllo` is 6 bytes, an
36+even count, so it has no tail step. A wasm port can hash the raw UTF-8 bytes
37+in memory without decoding.
38+
39+## Per-type dispatch
40+
41+| value | Hash | file:line | caches? |
42+|---|---|---|---|
43+| nil | not Hashable → 0 | hash.go:32-33 | n/a |
44+| Boolean | true→1, false→0 (raw, not mixed) | bool.go:31 | no |
45+| Int (int64) | `hashUint64(uint64(n))` | int.go:58 | no |
46+| Float, Float32 | `hashUint64(IEEE-754 float64 bits)`; no -0/NaN normalisation | float.go:41, :46 | no |
47+| Char (rune) | `hashUint64(uint64(rune))` | char.go:38 | no |
48+| String | `hashString` (FNV-1a) | string.go:56 | no |
49+| Symbol | `hashUnencodedChars(name)` | symbol.go:39 | no |
50+| Keyword | `hashUnencodedChars(name) + 0x9e3779b9` | keyword.go:38 | no |
51+| Ratio | `hashUint64(num.Int64())*31 + hashUint64(den.Int64())`, no finaliser; `Int64()` truncates for big parts | ratio.go:62-67 | no |
52+| BigInt | fits int64 → `hashUint64(n)`; else `h=h*31+b` over big-endian magnitude bytes, `h=^h` if negative | bigint.go:73-87 | no |
53+| BigDecimal | `hashUint64(bits(Float64()))`, NaN→0, -0→+0 | bigdecimal.go:108-117 | no |
54+| ArrayVector | own loop: `h=1; h=31*h+hash(e)` per element; `mixFinish` | vector.go:56-62 | no |
55+| PersistentVector | `hashOrdered(v.Seq())`; empty `Seq()` is `EmptyList` | persistent_vector.go:84-86, :262-264 | no |
56+| List | `hashOrdered(l)` | list.go:71-78 | yes (`_hash`, list.go:49-50) |
57+| Cons / ChunkedCons / LazySeq | `hashOrdered`; an empty LazySeq uses `EmptyList` | cons.go:110, chunk.go:221, lazy_seq.go:232-238 | no |
58+| PersistentMap | `h += hash(k) ^ hash(v)` per entry; `mixFinish(h)`; loop stops at `EmptyList` | persistent_map.go:777-798 | yes (:624-625) |
59+| SortedMap | same `k^v` sum | sorted_map.go:359-370 | yes |
60+| PersistentSet | `h += hash(e)`; `mixFinish` | persistent_set.go:69-82 | yes (:18-19) |
61+| SortedSet | same | sorted_set.go:77 | yes |
62+| MapEntry | `ArrayVector{k,v}.Hash()` | persistent_map.go:107-109 | no |
63+| PersistentQueue | empty → 0, else `hashOrdered` | persistent_queue.go:153-158 | no |
64+| Record | `mixFinish(Σ hash(fieldName)^hash(v) + extra.Hash())` | record.go:142-151 | no |
65+| Atom, DTypeInstance | identity (pointer): `hashString(%p)`, `mixFinish(uintptr)` | atom.go:230, deftype.go:154 | no |
66+| Boxed | `hashString(String())` | boxed.go:60-67 | yes |
67+| UUID / Instant | `hashString(val)` / `hashUint64(UnixMilli)` | uuid.go:88, instant.go:86 | no |
68+| legacy `vm.Map` | **not Hashable** → FNV of `String()`, which follows Go map order | map.go (no Hash) | no |
69+
70+The reader produces ArrayVector, List, PersistentMap (its `Type()` reports
71+`let-go.lang.Map`, persistent_map.go:801) and PersistentSet. A vector with
72+metadata becomes a PersistentVector (vector.go WithMeta). Keyword and symbol
73+strings carry no colon; the namespace is part of the hashed string
74+(`:foo/bar` hashes `"foo/bar"`, keyword.go:48-49).
75+
76+## Surprises (all reproduced by rows in vectors.tsv)
77+
78+1. **`hashOrdered` counts `EmptyList` as one `nil` element.** `EmptyList.First()`
79+ is `NIL` and the loop only stops on Go `nil` (list.go:106-109, :122-125). So
80+ `()`, `(nil)`, `[nil]` and an empty PersistentVector all hash 1257683291,
81+ while an empty ArrayVector hashes `mixFinish(1)` = 1364076727. Map and set
82+ loops guard `s != EmptyList` (persistent_map.go:784), so they don't have this.
83+2. **Equal values with different hashes.** `(= [] ())` and
84+ `(= [] (with-meta [] {:a 1}))` are true but the hashes differ (item 1), so
85+ `(contains? #{[]} ())` is false in lg 4e769212. Likewise `(= 0.0 -0.0)` is
86+ true but the Float hashes differ (float.go:41 has no -0 fold, unlike
87+ BigDecimal). `(get {0.0 :z} -0.0)` finds `:z` in a small map but returns
88+ nil once the map holds 101 entries. These are let-go bugs; the port must
89+ reproduce them bit-for-bit anyway.
90+3. **Maps whose every key equals its value hash to 0**, same as `{}`, `#{}`,
91+ nil, false, `0` and `0.0`: `k^v` cancels (persistent_map.go:794) and
92+ fmix32(0)=0.
93+4. **Cross-type collisions by construction.** Int, Char, Float and in-range
94+ BigInt all go through `hashUint64` on a raw 64-bit pattern: `97` = `\a`,
95+ `1` = `1N`, `MinInt64` = `-0.0` (both are bit pattern `0x8000…0`), `0` =
96+ `0.0`. `0.1M` = `0.1`, `1.5M` = `1.5`. Keyword = symbol + 0x9e3779b9, for
97+ every name (checked on all 29 pairs).
98+5. Booleans hash to the raw values 1 and 0; `true` collides with nothing in
99+ the table, but `false` = nil.
100+6. Every Hashable type agrees with `HashValue`: gen.go aborts if any row's
101+ `Hash()` differs, and none does. The lg `hash` builtin equals `HashValue`
102+ on all rows (`checks/hash-parity.sh --self`).
103+7. Hash depends on the runtime type, not the EDN text: `[]` is two rows
104+ (`vector`, `pvector`) with different hashes. The check passes `kind` to the
105+ wasm hook for this reason.
