1+# let-go map/set iteration order: port spec
2+
3+Source: `~/projects-new/3p/let-go` at `4e769212`; paths are under `pkg/vm/`
4+unless marked. Hashing is `../hash/SPEC.md`; everything here assumes the
5+port's `hashValue` is bit-exact (D19), because past 8 entries order is a
6+function of key hashes.
7+
8+## Two representations behind one type
9+
10+`PersistentMap` (persistent_map.go:619-626) is either
11+
12+- **ordered mode**: `root == nil`, entries in `okvs` (alternating k/v) in
13+ insertion order, linear-scan lookup (`ordered()` :629, `okvsIndex` :633);
14+- **HAMT mode**: `root != nil`, `okvs == nil`.
15+
16+`arrayMapMaxEntries = 8` (:601). Rules, all in `Assoc`/`Dissoc` (:865-931):
17+
18+| operation | effect on order |
19+|---|---|
20+| assoc new key, count < 8, ordered | appended at the end (:882-885) |
21+| assoc existing key (any mode) | value replaced in place, position kept (:870-878); same value returns the same map |
22+| assoc new key, count == 8, ordered | **promote**: `promoteWithAssoc` (:682-700) pushes the 8 entries, in insertion order, then the new one into a fresh HAMT transient (`forceHAMT`). From then on order is hash order. |
23+| dissoc, ordered | entry removed, the rest keep their order (:904-915) |
24+| dissoc, HAMT, entries remain | **no demotion**: stays HAMT even at 1 entry (:928-930) |
25+| dissoc, HAMT, last entry | becomes the empty *ordered* map (:922-927), so regrowing behaves like `{}` |
26+| `nil` key | allowed (`key == nil` at :866 is Go nil, not lg `nil`) |
27+
28+Every map constructor goes through these: the reader (`compiler/reader.go:860`,
29+`NewArrayMap`), compiled map literals (compiler.go:657-675 emits a call to
30+`array-map` with the read-time map's entries in its `Seq` order), `array-map`
31+(`NewArrayMap` :743-771, a transient) and **`hash-map`**
32+(rt/lang.go:5580-5585 → `NewPersistentMap` :723-735, repeated `Assoc`).
33+Unlike Clojure, `hash-map` with ≤ 8 entries is insertion-ordered too.
34+`into`, `group-by`, `frequencies` use transients (core.lg:1512-1520,
35+1725-1732, 1764-1769); `zipmap`, `select-keys` use `assoc` (core.lg:1714,
36+1665); `merge` is `conj` of each later map, which assocs that map's entries
37+in its own `seq` order (persistent_map.go:833-850, core.lg:1553-1560).
38+
39+**Transients** (transient.go:22-207) have the same two modes: ordered while
40+`count < 8` on insert (:96-99), `forceHAMT` on the 9th distinct key
41+(:45-63, okvs pushed in insertion order), `dissoc!` in ordered mode keeps
42+order (:123-128), no demotion, and `persistent!` of an ordered transient hands
43+over the slice unchanged (:198-201). A HAMT transient drained to 0 keeps
44+`t.hamt` set (`Dissoc`, :119-140, never clears it). `persistent!` right after
45+the drain yields `root == nil`, i.e. the empty ordered map; but keys `assoc!`ed
46+into the same transient after the drain go into a fresh HAMT root (:103-111),
47+so the result stays hash-ordered even at 8 keys or fewer (D49; corpus row
48+`transient-drain-regrow`). Otherwise transient and persistent paths produce
49+identical order (corpus rows `transient`, `transient-dissoc`).
50+
51+## Sets are always hash-ordered
52+
53+`PersistentSet` wraps a `PersistentMap` with each element mapped to itself
54+(persistent_set.go:15-20), but its empty impl is HAMT-mode (`emptySetImpl`,
55+:29, `root: &hmapBitmapNode{}`), every constructor seeds from it
56+(`NewPersistentSet` :34-43; `hash-set` = `NewSet`, set.go:197; `set` and
57+`into #{}` use a transient that is forced to HAMT, transient.go:459-473),
58+`disj` to empty lands back on `emptySetImpl` (:128-133) and so does
59+`persistent!` of an empty transient set (transient.go:513-517). So a set of
60+any size, including `#{:z :y :x}`, iterates in hash order; insertion order
61+only matters inside a collision bucket. `seq` of a set is the backing map's
62+keys in node order (:174-200).
63+
64+## The HAMT
65+
66+- Branching factor 32: `hmapShift = 5`, `hmapMask = 0x1f` (:16-19). The digit
67+ at depth d is `(hash >> 5d) & 31`, **least-significant digit first**
68+ (`hmapMaskFn` :125). Depths 0..6 (the last digit has 2 bits).
69+- **Only two node kinds**: `hmapBitmapNode` (:139-145) and
70+ `hmapCollisionNode` (:489-493). There is no Clojure-style `ArrayNode`; a
71+ bitmap node holds up to 32 slots.
72+- A bitmap node's array holds one pair per set bit, ordered by bit position:
73+ index = `popcount(bitmap & (bit-1))` (`hmapIndex` :133). A pair is either
74+ `[key, val]` (a leaf) or `[nil, child]` (:141-144). New entries are spliced
75+ in at their index (:222-236; transient :406-438).
76+- Two keys whose digits agree at this depth are pushed down together by
77+ `createNode` (:473-485) into a child one level deeper; equal full 32-bit
78+ hashes make a collision node instead.
79+- **seq**: `nodeSeq` (:277-293) walks slots 0..31 in order; a leaf emits its
80+ entry, a child is walked recursively in place (depth-first). `each`
81+ (:295-311) is the same walk. Since a slot holds a leaf *or* a child, never
82+ both, there is no inline-vs-child precedence beyond slot index.
83+
84+**Closed form** (no collisions): HAMT order is ascending order of
85+`rk(h) = Σ_{d=0..6} ((h >> 5d) & 31) · 32^(6-d)`, i.e. lexicographic on the
86+5-bit digits from the least significant end. Verified against native lg on
87+ints (−500..499), 1000 multiples of 4294967311, 10000 entity keywords, 3000
88+multi-byte strings, 1920 `[x y]` vectors and a reversed 5000-int build, for
89+both maps and sets. The tree shape depends on history (dissoc never collapses
90+a single-entry child), but order does not, except for the two cases below.
91+
92+### Collision buckets (insertion-ordered, history-dependent)
93+
94+`hmapCollisionNode` keeps an insertion-ordered array:
95+
96+- created by `createNode` as `[existing, new]` (:474-480, callers :216-219,
97+ :399-402);
98+- a new colliding key is **appended** (:527-533);
99+- `dissoc` from a bucket of ≥ 3 removes in place, order kept (:563-567).
100+
101+So `(-> m (assoc 97 :i) (assoc \a :c))` walks `97 \a` and the reverse build
102+walks `\a 97`.
103+
104+### Bug that changes order and membership: bucket 2 → 1
105+
106+`dissoc` from a 2-entry bucket rebuilds the survivor as
107+`(&hmapBitmapNode{}).assoc(0, n.hash, …)` (:552-562): **shift 0, whatever
108+depth the bucket sits at** (always ≥ 1). The survivor is still walked by
109+`seq`, but `get`/`contains?` look it up with the digit for the real depth and
110+miss whenever `(h >> 5d) & 31 ≠ h & 31`. A later `assoc` of either colliding
111+key goes into a different slot of that node, so the map can then hold the
112+**same key twice**. Native lg, for the 97/`\a` pair (digits 23 at depth 0, 11
113+at depth 1) in a 9-keyword map:
114+
115+ (dissoc a \a) → seq has 97, (get c 97) = nil, count 10
116+ (assoc c 97 :again) → seq has [97 :again] [97 :int], count 11
117+ (= c (dissoc a \a)) → false
118+ sets: (conj s 97) after the same disj → 97 twice
119+
120+`collide-map.lg` pins these (`bucket-*`, `set-bucket-dissoc` rows). Per D19
121+the port reproduces it; this is a let-go bug to raise upstream after the
122+campaign. Reachability in xsofy needs two distinct live keys with equal
123+32-bit hashes in one >8-entry map followed by a dissoc of one: for the
124+1920-cell `[x y]` maps that is ≈ 1920²/2³³ ≈ 0.04% per full map.
125+
126+## Reading paths all agree
127+
128+`seq` builds a `MapSeq` over a materialised entry slice (:1002-1023,
129+map.go:110-150). `keys`/`vals` are `(map first m)`/`(map second m)` over
130+`seq` (core.lg:1679-1685), `reduce-kv` reduces the seq (core.lg:337-341),
131+`doseq` expands to a seq walk (core.lg:1892), printing walks `entries()`
132+(:804-819). So xsofy's entity walks, e.g. `(doseq [[k v] (or (:entities world) {})] …)`
133+(world.lg:565) and `(vals (:entities w))` (render.lg:421, spell.lg:72), see
134+exactly `seq` order. Every map program prints a `views` row asserting
135+`keys = doseq = seq = reduce-kv = vals` order; all are `true` natively.
136+
137+xsofy's entity ids are keywords `:<prefix>-<n>` (det.lg:154-163): a floor
138+with ≤ 8 entities iterates in `assoc` order, above 8 in the keyword-hash
139+order (`hashUnencodedChars(name) + 0x9e3779b9`). Gas and FOV maps are keyed
140+by `[x y]` ArrayVectors (ordered hash, hash SPEC). `entity-*.lg` and
141+`vec-*.lg` cover both.
142+
143+## Equality and hash ignore order
144+
145+`Equals` (:1027-1047) checks counts, then that every entry of one map is
146+found with an equiv value in the other, mode-agnostic. `Hash` (:777-799) is
147+`mixFinish(Σ hash(k) ^ hash(v))` (D19); sets `mixFinish(Σ hash(e))`
148+(persistent_set.go:69-82). Neither depends on order, so `=`/`hash` cannot
149+catch an order bug: the corpus prints keys.
150+
151+## sorted-map, for contrast
152+
153+`SortedMap` (sorted_map.go:302-311) orders by comparator (`DefaultCompare`),
154+not by hash or insertion; `seq` at :495. Not covered here.
155+
156+## What a port cannot see unless it mirrors it
157+
158+1. **Hashes** (D19). Order above 8 entries, and for every set, is a pure
159+ function of the 32-bit hashes except in collision buckets.
160+2. **The mode boundary**: 8, the no-demotion rule, drain-to-empty → ordered
161+ (but not inside one transient, D49), sets never ordered. A port that copies Clojure (sets ordered? no; hash-map
162+ always hashed) or JS `Map` (insertion order always) diverges at size 9 or
163+ at size 1 for sets.
164+3. **Collision-bucket history** and the shift-0 rebuild. "Sort by `rk(h)`"
165+ is not enough: the port must implement the node algorithms literally,
166+ including `createNode`'s `[existing, new]` order and the bug.
167+4. **Go map iteration (random per run)** reaches a `PersistentMap` only by
168+ assoc'ing out of a Go map: `json/read-json` (rt/json.go:39-48),
169+ transit JSON objects (rt/transit.go:319-331), bencode dicts
170+ (rt/bencode.go:134-142), boxing a Go map (value.go:254-275) and
171+ `MapFromGoMap` (map.go:227). With ≤ 8 keys these produce a
172+ run-to-run-random insertion order in native lg itself
173+ (`(json/read-json "{\"z\":1,\"y\":2,\"x\":3,\"w\":4}")` printed two
174+ different orders in three runs). Above 8 the HAMT hides it except in
175+ collision buckets. None is on xsofy's path and none is in the corpus; a
176+ port must not "fix" them into a deterministic order and then expect a
177+ byte match, and the oracle cannot test them.
178+
179+## The corpus
180+
181+`gen.lg` writes 14 programs, `<kind>-{map,set}.lg`, kinds `int` (small,
182+negative, > 2³²), `kw` (plain and namespaced), `entity` (xsofy ids), `str`
183+(ASCII, 2-, 3- and 4-byte UTF-8), `vec` (`[x y]`), `mixed` (nil, booleans,
184+ints, keywords, strings, chars, vectors, floats) and `collide`. Sizes
185+0–9, 16, 33, 100, 1000, 10000. Insertion order is a Fisher-Yates shuffle
186+driven by `s' = (1103515245·s + 12345) mod 2³¹`, seed `n + 7`.
187+
188+Map paths: `literal` (quoted constant), `literal-dyn` (runtime values, so
189+the compiler's `array-map` call), `assoc`, `into`, `zipmap`, `transient`,
190+`hash-map`, `array-map`, `update` (re-assoc every key), `dissoc-half`,
191+`assoc-back`, `transient-dissoc`, `merge` (two halves), `drain-regrow`,
192+`transient-drain-regrow` (drain and regrow 6 keys inside one transient), plus
193+`views`. Set paths: `literal`, `literal-dyn`, `conj`, `set`, `into`,
194+`hash-set`, `transient`, `disj-half`, `conj-back`, `transient-disj`,
195+`drain-regrow`, `map-keys`.
196+
197+A row is `<path> <n> <count> <keys>`; above 100 keys, `<keys>` is the first
198+16, the last 16 and `Σ` checksum `a ← (a·1000003 + idx(k) + 1) mod
199+(2³¹−1)` over the keys' generation indices, in seq order.
200+
201+Colliding keys (distinct, unequal, same hash; `collide-*.lg`):
202+`97`/`\a`/`4.8e-322`/`"xe2tiazy"` (one 4-way bucket: Int, Char, Float bits
203+97, and an FNV-1a preimage), `"snpfo"`/`"s6rja"`, `:kby0z`/`:kcxik`,
204+`'kby0z`/`'kcxik`, `[97]`/`[\a]`, `4611686018427387904`/`2.0`: 11 pairs in
205+6 buckets. `1`/`1N` hash alike but are `=`, so they are one key, not a
206+collision.
207+
208+Regenerate and check, from `dev/lower-wasm/`:
209+
210+ checks/map-order.sh --update # programs + .expected
211+ checks/map-order.sh --native # regen to scratch, require byte-identical programs and .expected
212+ checks/map-order.sh # the P2.4 row (backend + let-go test)
213+
214+`SKIP` keeps `gen.lg` out of `run-corpus.sh`.

1+# opmatrix: generated op-matrix corpus (P1.1)
2+
3+Every `.lg` here is generated; don't edit by hand. Regenerate, from `dev/lower-wasm/`:
4+
5+ ~/projects-new/3p/lg-bin/lg-4e76921230 corpus/gen-opmatrix.lg corpus/opmatrix/
6+ checks/run-corpus.sh --update-expected corpus/opmatrix
7+
8+There is one program per IR builtin op from the `builtin-ops` table in let-go's
9+`pkg/rt/core/ir/build.lg`. That table has 23 ops: `+ - * quot / bit-and bit-or bit-xor
10+bit-and-not bit-shift-left bit-shift-right unsigned-bit-shift-right
11+unchecked-add unchecked-subtract unchecked-multiply < <= > >= = inc dec bit-not`.
12+Two more programs cover unary `-` (`neg`) and unary `/` (`recip`), because build.lg
13+lowers those to distinct shapes (`sub 0 x`, `div 1 x`). A binary op whose program
14+would run past about 400 lines is split into `-1` and `-2` parts.
15+`not`, `zero?`, `pos?`, `neg?`, `even?` and `odd?` are left out: they are plain
16+core defns that compile to `:call`, not to a compare op.
17+
18+Operands: 0, ±1, ±2, ±7, ±2^31, 2^32, 2^62, MaxInt64, MinInt64, 3037000499 and
19+3037000500. Shift counts: 0 1 31 32 63 64 -1.
20+
21+Each application appears twice in the same program:
22+
23+- `typed` uses literal operands, so typeinfer types the op `:int` (unboxed path).
24+- `boxed` routes operands through `(defn id [x] x)`, so the op is `:unknown`.
25+
26+Each application runs in its own `try`, so a throwing case prints
27+`<mode> <op> <a> [<b>] => error: <ex-message>` and the program continues. Every
28+program exits 0.
29+
30+## .expected and what the check is
31+
32+`oracle.sh` is the match relation. It reruns native lg on every invocation and
33+never reads `.expected`. `<prog>.lg.expected` is a committed snapshot of native
34+lg's stdout, and it is still checked. Before calling the oracle,
35+`checks/run-corpus.sh` diffs native stdout against the snapshot and reports
36+`STALE-EXPECTED` (exit 1) on any difference. That catches two things the oracle
37+cannot: a hand-edited snapshot, and an lg that changed behaviour under the
38+corpus. In the second case the oracle would just track the new behaviour and
39+keep matching. The snapshot check also runs when the backend runner is missing.
40+Falsified on 2026-09-30: hand-editing one line of `quot-2.lg.expected` gave
41+`STALE-EXPECTED`, exit 1.
42+
43+Native behaviours worth knowing (lg 4e769212, typed and boxed agree on every line):
44+
45+- `(quot MinInt64 -1)` returns MinInt64 with no error. Clojure throws.
46+- `(- MinInt64)` returns MinInt64 with no error, while `(- MinInt64 1)` and
47+ `(dec MinInt64)` throw `integer overflow`.
48+- `(/ MinInt64 -1)` returns the bigint `9223372036854775808N`. Other int/int
49+ `/` results are ints or ratios (`1/2`, `-7/2`).
50+- Shift counts of 64 or more, and negative counts, follow Go rather than Java's
51+ 6-bit mask: `(bit-shift-left 1 64)` is 0, `(bit-shift-left 1 -1)` is 0,
52+ `(bit-shift-right -7 64)` is -1, and `(unsigned-bit-shift-right -1 64)` is 0.
53+ None of them throw.
54+- There are two error texts: `ExecutionError: integer overflow` (from
55+ `+ - * inc dec`) and a bare `divide by zero` (from `quot`, `/` and unary `/`).

1+# Check/gate wall-time report (2026-10-01, 11:10–12:00 PDT)
2+
3+Read-only investigation of why verification is slow on this campaign and what to
4+change. Nothing under `src/`, `rt/` or `checks/` was edited; every measurement ran
5+in a scratch export of HEAD `6f107d7` (the live tree was mid-edit and its driver
6+failed to load for part of the hour). Load averages are quoted with every number
7+because they dominate: the same check varied **5.8×** with load alone during this
8+hour. Snippets live in `$SCRATCH` =
9+`/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-matt-projects-new-3p-joint-xsofy/fca6f592-886f-4b90-9538-46a9d7127210/scratchpad/perf/`.
10+
11+## Headline
12+
13+1. **The machine is oversubscribed, and macOS load average overstates it.** At the
14+ moment load read 32, there were 5 `lg` processes and 1 headless-Chromium GPU
15+ process at ~100% CPU each: ~6 cores of real demand on 8 cores (4 P-cores). Each
16+ `lg` is a Go binary with 8 runnable GC threads, so three agents' gates read as
17+ load 25–47. Real CPU cost of a check is stable (driver: 11.5 s CPU at load 6,
18+ 13.4 s CPU at load 16) while wall is not (8.1 s → 26 s). More parallelism per
19+ script without a machine-wide cap makes this worse, not better.
20+2. **Agent wall time ≠ machine time.** 6.1 h of 13.7 h was agents polling in
21+ `until … sleep` loops; no script change recovers that, only the harness pattern
22+ (§5). The remaining 7.6 h of machine-bound time splits roughly: oracle compiles
23+ (the driver is >98% of an oracle program's time; wasm-tools 0.15 s, node 0.2 s,
24+ native lg 0.03 s), the census, the native tier, and the rtlib rebuilds that
25+ every scratch tree copy pays separately (six `.rtlib` copies exist under the
26+ scratchpad right now, 45–175 s each to build).
27+3. `fseventsd` at 98% did not reproduce (0–8% live over 3 samples; 3% lifetime
28+ average). Spotlight does not index `dev/lower-wasm` or `/private/tmp` (mdfind
29+ returns 0 items for both). The churn that exists is agents' tree copies in the
30+ scratchpad (671 files written in 15 min by one agent's `cp -r`), not the checks.
31+
32+## Recommendation table
33+
34+| # | Change | Wall saving per typical item | Per campaign-hour | Fidelity risk | Cost | Verdict |
35+|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
36+| 1a | `run-corpus.sh` parallel, **P=3**, per-program captured output, serial summary (`$SCRATCH/run-corpus-par.sh`) | corpus/wasm 14 programs: median 202 s → 96 s (2.1×; 229 → 85 s in the quieter rep); P1 gate's 126 oracle programs ≈ 17 min → ~8 min | ~10–15 min/h of the oracle-bound share | **none** — output byte-identical at P=1..4 (md5 equal across all 8 runs); rtlib build is atomic (tmp+rename) and pre-warmed once | small | **adopt** |
37+| 1b | Machine-wide slot pool for heavy steps (`$SCRATCH/sem.sh`, `LW_SLOTS=4`) wrapped around oracle/census/native workers, shared by all agents | converts 3–6× load slowdowns into queueing: native tier 525 s @ load 29–47 vs 90 s @ load 10 | largest machine-side lever; est. 20–40% of machine-bound time while ≥2 agents gate | **none** (ordering/timeouts only; dead-holder reclaim) | small | **adopt** (prerequisite for 1a/6/7 being net positive) |
38+| 1c | `gate.sh` rows concurrently, -j2, logs kept per row (`$SCRATCH/gate-par.sh`) | gate 1: rows mostly oracle-bound → ~1.6× on top of 1a; also no "rerun to see why it failed" | 5 min/h | **none** (same rows, same exit rule; output kept, not discarded) | small | adopt after 1a+1b |
39+| 2 | `checks/affected.sh`: diff → minimal row set (`$SCRATCH/affected.sh`) | corpus/checks/host-only items (7 of 29): 1–4 rows instead of a phase gate; src-only items skip the native tier (120–525 s); rt-only items already skip the census (its mtime key reads only `src/`) | 3–8 min/h | **low** — static table; a missed input = a stale row, so gates stay full | small | **adopt** as advisory (implementer runs affected rows; gates unchanged) |
40+| 3 | `checks/attest` records; orchestrator trusts slow rows for the same tree hash (`$SCRATCH/attest.sh`) | skips the second run of the native tier (2–9 min) on the 12 rt items and of run-tests/world-parity/browser-boot later; oracle rows stay rerun (cheap at P=3) | 2–5 min/h | **medium** — forgeable in principle; mitigated by orchestrator-computed tree hash + lg hash + fast rows always rerun + spot-check of one sub-unit | medium | **defer** until 1a–1c land; adopt only for the slow rows |
41+| 4 | fsevents/Spotlight: `.metadata_never_index`, relocate caches | not measurable now (daemon at 0–8%) | ~0 | none | small | **reject** as a perf fix; keep the hygiene items (shared rtlib dir, mktemp leak) |
42+| 4b | Shared content-addressed rtlib dir (`LW_RTLIB_DIR`, e.g. `/tmp/lw-rtlib`) so tree copies reuse one build | 45–175 s per agent per tree copy (6 copies exist today) | 3–5 min/h | **none** — the key is a hash of the exact sources | small (one `def` + `mkdir`) | **adopt** (orchestrator edit to `src/lower_wasm.lg` line 2995) |
43+| 5 | Polling → `run_in_background` + completion notification; AGENTS.md rule 8 text below | 6.1 h of 13.7 h agent wall (45%) | 27 min/h | none | none | **adopt** |
44+| 6 | Census per-file sharded, P=4 (LPT by TSV `ms`), content-hash key instead of mtime | fresh census 23.7 min of unit time → ~6 min (xsofy 3.4 + legmacs 2.5 LPT bound; per-process floor 2–3 s); paid on each of the 10 src items | ~6 min/h | **none** (compile-only, per-unit, TSV rows merged in idx order; summary unchanged) | medium | **adopt** |
45+| 7 | Native tier per test file, `xargs -P 4` | measured 182 s at P=4 (load 25) vs 525 s one-process (load 29–47) and 349 s per-file sum; LPT bound ≈ 95 s (max file seq 86 s); startup floor 2.0 s × 11 files = 6% overhead | 3–6 min/h | **none** — per-file pass sums equal the one-process run (34 281 = 34 281); the deftest-count guard becomes per file | small | **adopt** |
46+| 8 | `GOMAXPROCS=2/4` on lg | no signal (12.6–30 s all settings, interleaved ×3 at load 26–47) | 0 | none | none | **reject** |
47+
48+"Typical item" = one row run by the implementer + the orchestrator's rerun + a
49+phase gate when the row is in a gated phase. Campaign-hour figures assume the
50+measured mix (31 items in 13.7 h of tool wall) and are estimates; the per-item
51+columns are measured unless marked LPT (bound from per-unit times).
52+
53+## Measurements
54+
55+All in the HEAD export unless noted. `lg-4e76921230`. Load = 1-min average at start.
56+
57+**Oracle program breakdown** (vectors.lg / maps.lg):
58+
59+| step | wall | CPU | load |
60+|---|---|---|---|
61+| driver, rtlib cold (first run builds it) | 45.4 s | 60.8 s | 5.5 |
62+| driver, rtlib warm | 8.1 s | 11.5 s | 5.8 |
63+| driver, rtlib warm | 26.0 s | 13.4 s | 15.7 |
64+| wasm-tools parse (1.6 MB wat → 281 KB) | 0.15 s | | 15.7 |
65+| node run | 0.21 s | | 15.7 |
66+| native lg | 0.03 s | | |
67+
68+**rtlib build race**: `.rtlib` removed, three drivers started together: all three
69+exit 0 after **175 s** (vs 45 s for one), identical `.wat` md5, one
70+`rtlib-cf5351a4.edn` left (load 5.9 → 23.9). The write is `spit tmp` +
71+`os/rename`, so concurrent builders cannot corrupt the file; the prune only
72+removes files with *other* keys. Cost is CPU only — which is why every parallel
73+script must warm the cache once before fanning out (both scratch scripts do).
74+
75+**corpus/wasm (14 programs), `run-corpus-par.sh`, outputs md5-identical across all runs**:
76+
77+| P | rep 1 wall (load at start) | rep 2 wall (load) |
78+|---|---|---|
79+| 1 | 229 s (21.3) | 175 s (31.3) |
80+| 2 | 90 s (18.1) | 102 s (21.2) |
81+| 3 | 85 s (18.5) | 106 s (26.4) |
82+| 4 | 76 s (19.6) | 131 s (17.7; overlapped the native-tier P=4 run below) |
83+
84+Medians: P=1 202 s, P=2 96 s, P=3 96 s, P=4 104 s (rep 2 of P=4 contaminated).
85+Gains stop at P=2–3 because other agents held 3–5 lg processes throughout (each
86+driver is ~1.4 cores of CPU); P=3 is the cap this report recommends for a shared
87+8-core laptop, with the pool (1b) making the cap global rather than per script.
88+
89+**Native tier (D81)**, default tier, HEAD export:
90+
91+| file | wall | passes |
92+|---|---|---|
93+| seq_test | 86.1 s | 1 642 |
94+| reader_test | 73.8 s | 69 |
95+| phm_test | 71.4 s | 6 558 |
96+| phs_test | 37.0 s | 3 131 |
97+| xsofy_natives_test | 24.3 s | 9 350 |
98+| pvec_test | 18.1 s | 29 |
99+| vkind_test | 18.0 s | 124 |
100+| str_test | 10.6 s | 2 249 |
101+| core_test | 8.6 s | 10 693 |
102+| term_test | 0.8 s | 155 |
103+| intrinsics_test | 0.1 s | 281 |
104+| **sum (load 12→29)** | **349 s** | **34 281** |
105+| one process, as `run-intrinsics-native.sh` (load 29→47) | **525 s** | 34 281 |
106+| D81's figure (load 10) | 90 s | |
107+| runtime load + one ns (per-process floor) | 2.0 s | |
108+
109+Time is not where the assertions are: reader (69 passes, 74 s) and seq (1 642,
110+86 s) dominate, so a per-file split is bounded by the biggest file (~86 s), not by
111+count. Measured per-file at `xargs -P 4` (load 24.7 → 21.6, overlapping one
112+other corpus run): **182 s** wall, 11/11 files OK, 34 281 passes — against 525 s
113+for the one-process run at load 29–47 and 349 s for the per-file sum at load
114+12–29. The LPT bound (~95 s) needs a quieter machine; the win on this one is
115+~2–3×.
116+
117+**Census** (from the committed TSVs' `ms` column, i.e. the 10:16/10:26 run):
118+xsofy 1 064 units, 825.5 s (13.8 min), largest file world.lg 64 s, largest unit
119+7.0 s; legmacs 816 units, 592.3 s (9.9 min), largest commands.lg 68 s. legmacs'
120+wall (10:16:30 → 10:26:28) equals its unit sum, so per-process startup is noise.
121+LPT over files at P=4: xsofy 207 s, legmacs 149 s → **~6 min vs ~24 min**. One
122+file alone (`census.lg … main.lg`) costs unit-sum + 2.3 s; at load 29–34 that run
123+took 164 s for 161 s of units that the cached TSV had recorded as 25 s — the same
124+6× load effect. Invalidation: the mtime test covers `src/*.lg` + the two census
125+scripts + the corpus files; `rt/` never invalidates it (good), but any `touch` or
126+reverted edit of `src/` does, and a tree copy resets mtimes (bad: content-hash the
127+inputs like the rtlib key does).
128+
129+**Item → inputs → rows** (`affected.sh --all` is the table). Applied to the 29
130+non-doc commits of `dev/lower-wasm`: 10 touched `src/` (every oracle row + census
131++ bench-fib), 12 touched `rt/` but not `src/` (every oracle row + native tier +
132+twins + review2; **not** census, refuse or bench-fib: `fib` links no runtime, 1.3 KB
133+shaken), 7 touched only `corpus/`, `checks/` or `host/` (1–4 rows; `1b822bf`,
134+`oracle.sh` itself, is the honest outlier at 19). Total 533 row-runs if every
135+affected row were run, against 29 × 28 = 812 for "run everything" and against the
136+actual practice of one row + an occasional gate.
137+
138+**Churn (15-min window, 11:16–11:31)**: `dev/lower-wasm` 9 files (6 `rt/`, 3
139+`corpus/`); scratchpad 691 files, of which 671 were one agent's tree copy
140+(`p213/lw/corpus`, 574 `.lg`/`.expected`); `$TMPDIR` 33 files (27 Chromium
141+profile). `$TMPDIR` also holds 281 leaked `tmp.*` dirs (31 from the last 12 h,
142+438 MB total) from `KEEP=1` or killed oracle runs. Time Machine includes
143+`~/projects-new` and excludes `/private/tmp`; the `.rtlib` under the live tree is
144+therefore backed up (4.3 MB rewritten on every key change), the scratch ones not.
145+
146+## Ready-to-apply snippets (all in `$SCRATCH`)
147+
148+- `run-corpus-par.sh` — drop-in for `checks/run-corpus.sh` (same flags minus
149+ `--update-expected`, plus `-j N`; default 3). Pre-warms the rtlib, fans out with
150+ `xargs -0 -P`, prints the summary in sorted order. Verified: 8 runs, 4 values
151+ of P, one md5.
152+- `sem.sh` — `checks/sem.sh <cmd>`: `mkdir`-based slot pool at `/tmp/lw-sem`,
153+ `LW_SLOTS=4`, dead-pid reclaim, bounded wait. Verified: two 2 s sleeps under
154+ `LW_SLOTS=1` take 4 s and leave no slot behind. Wrap the per-program worker in
155+ `run-corpus-par.sh`, the census shards and the native-tier files with it.
156+- `gate-par.sh` — `gate.sh` with `-j`, per-row logs under `checks/.gate/<phase>/`,
157+ one rtlib warm-up. Same row set and exit rule.
158+- `affected.sh` — static id → inputs table (`--all` prints it); no args = `git
159+ diff HEAD` + untracked under `dev/lower-wasm`. Verified against the samples in
160+ the table above and all 29 commits.
161+- `attest.sh` — records and `--verify`; the spot-check hook is a stub by design
162+ (one line per row kind), since the verdict is defer.
163+- 4b is a one-line change for the orchestrator, not a script: in
164+ `src/lower_wasm.lg` replace
165+ `(def rtlib-dir (str lw-rt/src-dir "/.rtlib"))` with
166+ `(def rtlib-dir (let [d (os/getenv "LW_RTLIB_DIR")] (if (seq d) d (str lw-rt/src-dir "/.rtlib"))))`
167+ and export `LW_RTLIB_DIR=/tmp/lw-rtlib` from `checks/*.sh`. Content-addressed, so
168+ sharing across tree copies cannot serve a stale library.
169+- 6 and 7 are edits to `checks/census.sh` and `checks/run-intrinsics-native.sh`:
170+ census — split the file list into 4 LPT bins by the previous TSV's per-file
171+ `ms` (fall back to round-robin), run 4 `census.lg` processes under `sem.sh`
172+ writing `<c>.raw.N.tsv`, concatenate in idx order (pass a per-shard idx
173+ offset or renumber), then the existing validate + summary steps; native tier —
174+ replace the single runner call with
175+ `for f in corpus/intrinsics/*_test.lg; do printf '%s\0' "$f"; done | xargs -0 -P 4 -n1 sh -c '… intrinsics-native-runner.lg "$(grep -c "^(deftest " "$1")" "<ns of $1>" > out/$b'`
176+ and sum/compare afterwards (the count guard is then per file, which is stricter,
177+ not looser).
178+
179+## Text for AGENTS.md rule 8 (proposed; not applied)
180+
181+> 8. **Never poll.** The harness caps a foreground command at 10 minutes, and a
182+> check that can take longer (the native tier, a census, a phase gate, world
183+> parity, browser boot) must not be waited on with `until … sleep` loops: across
184+> 31 agent runs on 2026-10-01 those loops were 6.1 of 13.7 hours of tool time,
185+> most of it idle. Start the long check once with `run_in_background: true` and
186+> a `timeout` sized to the check (gate: 3 600 000 ms), capture its output to a
187+> file, and **stop**: do other work or end your turn. The harness delivers a
188+> completion notification with the exit code; act on that. If you must check
189+> progress, `Read` the output file once — do not loop on it. Where a `Monitor`
190+> tool exists, prefer it over any `sleep`. Never background anything that
191+> outlives you (rule 6 still holds): the background job ends with your run.
192+
193+## Appendix: fidelity notes per change
194+
195+- **1a/1c (parallel corpus/gate)**: `oracle.sh` and `wasm-run.sh` each `mktemp -d`
196+ per invocation and share nothing else; `run-corpus.sh`'s only shared file is its
197+ own `$t/native.out`, which the parallel twin makes per-program. The STALE-EXPECTED
198+ check runs native lg per program and is unaffected. The one shared mutable
199+ resource is `src/.rtlib`, covered above (atomic, idempotent, pre-warmed).
200+ `--both` (`run-tests.sh`) was carried over untested here because the HEAD tree
201+ has no `_test.lg` in an oracle dir; it uses the same per-program scratch.
202+- **1b (pool)**: a pool wait that times out runs the command anyway and says so;
203+ a crashed holder's slot is reclaimed on the next acquire. A smaller `LW_SLOTS`
204+ cannot change any result, only when it arrives.
205+- **2 (affected)**: the table is deliberately coarse (prefixes) and errs toward
206+ running more; the risk is an input added to a check without a table edit, which
207+ is why gates ignore it.
208+- **3 (attest)**: the forgery surface is the record file; the orchestrator never
209+ reads the tree hash from it, it recomputes, so a record can only lie about the
210+ *result* for a tree it genuinely names. Always rerunning fast rows (everything
211+ but census, native tier, run-tests, world-parity, browser-boot) and spot-checking
212+ one sub-unit of a slow row bounds a lie to "one slow row, until the next gate".
213+- **6 (census shards)**: `census.lg` holds no cross-file state except the `idx`
214+ counter and the `corpus-nses` set (filled from each file's `ns` form as it is
215+ read). The set decides `unbound-var` vs `ok` by whether an extern's namespace is
216+ in the corpus, so each shard must be given the full ns list up front (read all
217+ `ns` forms first, lower only its share) or the buckets drift. That is the one
218+ real change in the shard edit.
219+- **7 (native tier per file)**: `test/run-all-tests` with the ns regex is per
220+ invocation already; the files share only `rt/`. Per-file counts: 14/12/11/8/4/
221+ 7/11/20/8/2/17 = 114, equal to the one-process `tests=114`.

1+# Phase 1 adversarial review (2026-10-01)
2+
3+Reviewer's brief: break "the backend is correct on the Phase 1 language subset".
4+Every row was run with `WASM_RUN=checks/wasm-run.sh checks/oracle.sh <file>`
5+against a snapshot of `src/` at HEAD 4e203f4. Two implementers were editing
6+`src/` during the review and the working tree stopped compiling even
7+`corpus/closure/closures.lg` partway through (`unknown type $Str`,
8+`CompileError`), so results come from HEAD rather than the moving tree. Native lg
9+is `lg-4e76921230`.
10+
11+- `probes/` holds every program in the table, as run.
12+- `bug-NN-*.lg` are the MISMATCH programs (native and wasm output in the header).
13+- `gap-NN-*.lg` are Phase-2 constructs that fail without a named error.
14+
15+P1.7 (2026-10-01) moved every bug/gap program, header kept plus one
16+`;; P1.7:` disposition line, into `fixed/` (MATCHes; `.expected` from native,
17+none where native's report embeds an address, D55) or `refused/` (named
18+error, checked by `checks/refuse.sh`; `;; refuse-runtime:` marks the one
19+refusal that can only happen at run time). `fixed/p17-*.lg` are shapes next
20+to each bug that P1.7 also checks against native. Row: `checks/run.sh P1.7`.
21+
22+Classes: MATCH; MISMATCH = inside the Phase 1 scope and native != wasm;
23+NAMED-LIMIT = refused or thrown with a `lower-wasm: ...` message, or covered by
24+a DECISIONS entry (D33 stack bound, D42, D52, D63 unbound-var, D65);
25+GAP = outside Phase 1 and not reported as a named limit; NOT-COMPARABLE =
26+native does not terminate.
27+
28+Counts (148 programs, as of 2026-10-01): 78 MATCH, 33 MISMATCH, 28 NAMED-LIMIT, 7 GAP, 2 NOT-COMPARABLE.
29+

35+| bug-03 | wrong value | LICM hoists `+` and `quot` out of a zero-trip loop: wasm throws `:ovf`/`divide by zero` where native returns 0 | q01 | do not hoist trapping ops past the loop guard | FIXED: LICM hoists no op that may raise (pin on `ir.passes.licm/pure-op?`); upstream finding |
36+| bug-04 | wrong value | D35's unary-minus rewrite ignores lexical shadowing: `(let [- inc] (- x))` gives -5 instead of 6 | p14 | skip the rewrite when `-` is locally bound (track locals or rewrite after build) | FIXED: the rewrite tracks locals named `-` |
37+| bug-05 | wrong value | `(defn inc ..)` / `(defn + ..)` in `user`: native keeps compiling calls as the core op (prints 2, 7); wasm calls the user defn (101, 12). A native quirk, but the oracle follows native | p16 p17 | reproduce (a D16-style quirk) or refuse by name; record in DECISIONS | REFUSED: `lower-wasm: redefining core op <name> is not supported` (native's opcode set) |
38+| bug-06 | wrong value | var used before its `def`: native fails `Can't resolve y`, wasm prints `nil` and exits 0 (the driver interns every def up front) | p67 (p85 is the defn-body variant) | intern defs in order, or refuse a forward reference | FIXED: every form is compiled natively at its position; native's message ends `_main` there |

47+
48+| # | what | programs | P1.7 disposition |
49+|---|---|---|---|

D63 promises `lower-wasm: Phase-2 constant vector`, but only `[]` gets it | p00d p48 | MATCH as is since the runtime is compiled in (D75-D78) |
51+| gap-02 | `$rt_print` and `$rt_report` fall through to the Int unbox for `$Fn`, `$Atom` and `$Err`. `(println (fn [] 1))`, `(println (atom 1))`, `(println e)` on a caught exception, and an uncaught `(throw (fn ..))` all trap `illegal cast`, which is uncatchable. Printing them is Phase 2 (D53), but they fail without a name | p57 p58 q06 q07 q14 | native print for atoms, ex-info and a caught runtime error (`#error {:type ..}`); an uncaught fn reports `<fn 0x0>`; printing a fn is REFUSED at run time (native prints an address) |

53+## Named limits worth a DECISIONS note
54+
55+- D63's runtime surface is the bulk of NAMED-LIMIT here: `not`, `str`, `nil?`, `some?`, `string?`, `rem`, `mod`, `max`/`min`/`abs`, `not=`, `identical?` and `unchecked-inc`/`-dec`/`-negate` all report native's own `TypeError: nil is not a function `. A reader cannot tell that apart from a real native bug.
56+- `=` throws the named error on any non-Int pair (keyword, nil, bool, string) unless it is constant-folded or part of a 3+ arm keyword `:switch`. A 2-arm `(if (= k :a) ..)` throws. D65 documents only the keyword-cond-in-loop case.
57+- D33: named-fn closures (`(fn self [n] ..)`, which go through an atom) overflow between 1e5 and 1e6 frames, def'd fns and boxed returns between 1e6 and 3e6. Native handles 3e6.
58+- `letfn` is refused as `unsupported variadic fn (& args)`, which names the wrong construct.

1+# review2: differential fuzz of the Phase 2 runtime (rt/wasm/*.lg)
2+
3+Adversarial review of the claim "rt/wasm/*.lg behaves identically to native let-go on the
4+Phase 2 surface", run under native lg (`lg-4e76921230`) with the reference intrinsics. Nothing
5+in `src/`, `rt/` or `checks/` was touched. Run from `dev/lower-wasm/`.
6+
7+## Counts (2026-10-01, rt/ at 28f7c6d)
8+
9+- **2300 seeds** run (`[1000,3300)`), 5-40 steps each, 8 shards; ~25 min wall on a host at load
10+ 15-44 from other sessions (per-shard 560-700 s for 400 seeds unloaded-equivalent; logs in `runs/`).
11+- Plus `seams.lg`: 256 targeted rows, 219 MATCH; every DIFF is accounted for below.
12+- **105 distinct raw signatures** (`[op field native-class runtime-class]`) in the final runs, plus
13+ ~3,000 tallied hits on signatures filtered once reported. Hand triage folds them into
14+ **16 distinct runtime bugs**, 3 declared/known differences, and 3 harness artifacts.
15+- 19,858 more steps were the README's known follow-up (a static-text `wasm/trap` where native raises
16+ a catchable error with the same text); 1,564 of those also differ in text because native embeds a
17+ type name (D47). Tallied, not counted as bugs.
18+
19+## Method
20+
21+`fuzz.lg` keeps a pool of `[native runtime]` pairs. A program is a vector of steps: builders
22+(`:vec-n` at 0/1/2/31/32/33/64/65/1055/1056/1057/1100, `:map-n`/`:set-n` crossing 8/9 with int,
23+keyword, string, colliding (maporder SPEC M3) and mixed keys in a seeded shuffle, `:tmap-n`
24+transients with assoc!/dissoc! churn, `:list-n`, 140 leaves covering i31/i64 bounds, -0.0, NaN,
25+±Inf, subnormals, every escape, multi-byte text, chars, keywords/symbols with and without ns) and
26+~100 ops over the twins (`tools/twin-manifest.lg`). After every step both results are compared on
27+pr-str, str, print-str, hash, count, type, meta and a structural bridge; when a step throws, both
28+must throw and messages are compared (heap addresses normalised). Lazy chains use runtime ports of
29+core.lg's `take`/`filter`/`concat`/`into` built on the runtime's own seq natives. Pool refs are
30+taken mod the pool size and the shrinker renumbers them when it deletes a step, so minimal programs
31+stay meaningful.
32+
33+```
34+lg -source-paths rt corpus/review2/fuzz.lg 1000 1400 # a shard (FUZZ_NOSHRINK=1 to skip shrinking)
35+lg -source-paths rt corpus/review2/fuzz.lg --replay '[[:vec-n 2] [:seq 0]]'
36+lg -source-paths rt corpus/review2/fuzz.lg --shrink '<prog>' '<sig>'
37+lg -source-paths rt corpus/review2/fuzz.lg --eval corpus/review2/seams.lg
38+FUZZ_NOFOUND=1 ... # turns off the filters for the bugs below, so the fuzzer re-finds them
39+```
40+
41+Each `bug-NN-*.lg` runs standalone (`lg -source-paths rt corpus/review2/bug-NN-....lg`) and prints
42+the native line and the runtime line; its header carries both outputs and the implicated function.
43+
44+## Distinct bugs, ranked
45+
46+Rank order: silent wrong value > wrong error > crash/trap > limit that should be parity.
47+"Hits" counts fuzz steps across all runs, filtered ones included.
48+
49+| # | rank | file | what | implicated | hits |
50+|---|---|---|---|---|---|
51+| 01 | silent | `bug-01-empty-vector-hash.lg` | `(hash [])` is 1257683291 (the `()` hash), native 1364076727; every set or 9+-key map holding `[]` orders differently. H1 is therefore **not mirrored**: runtime `(contains? #{[]} ())` is true, native false | `wasm.seq/hash*` kind 11 via `vec-seq` → EmptyList | 395 |
52+| 08 | silent | `bug-08-vector-seq-hash.lg` | `(hash (seq [1 2]))`, `(hash (rest v))`: runtime hashes FNV of `"(seq [1 2])"`, native FNV of `"(1 2)"`; only vectors conj'd past 32 match | `wasm.seq/vec-seq` (always PVecSeq), `hash*` kind 10 | 20+ |
53+| 02 | silent | `bug-02-lazy-error-not-cached.lg` | a lazy seq whose thunk threw re-runs it on the next access and can return values; native caches the error. `(realized? s)` after the throw: native true, runtime false. **S2 seam open** | `wasm.seq/lazy-step` | 525 |
54+| 09 | silent | `bug-09-pvec-repeat-print-mode.lg` | a meta'd (or >32-conj'd) vector and a Repeat print elements via `String()` natively in every mode: pr-str loses nested map commas, print-str keeps strings/chars quoted. The runtime honours the mode. **D67 seam fails for these two kinds** | wasm.str printer, kinds 11 (with meta) and 9 | 190 |
55+| 03 | silent | `bug-03-pvecseq-print-type.lg` | seq of a >32-conj'd vector prints `(0 1 …)` and types PersistentList; native prints `(seq [whole vector])`, type Sequence. The runtime's hash of the same value already uses the `(seq [` form, so its own pr-str and hash disagree | wasm.str (no kind 10 arm), `wasm.core/type-id` | 245 |
56+| 14 | silent | `bug-14-sort-accepts-non-collections.lg` | `(sort (repeat 3 2))`, `(sort (seq (map inc (range 3))))` return sorted lists; native throws "sort expected a Collection" | `wasm.core` `sortable?` accepts kinds 6 and 9 | 2 |
57+| 16 | silent (stand-in) | `bug-16-computed-nan-hash.lg` | `(hash (- ##Inf ##Inf))` hashes like `##NaN`; native bits differ (0x7FF8…0 vs Go's 0x7FF8…1). Likely vanishes with the real `f64-bits` (D28); re-check then | `wasm.seq/float-bits` | 1 |
58+| 13 | silent (native quirk) | `bug-13-repeat-type-of-type.lg` | `(type (type (repeat 2 1)))` is `let-go.lang.Repeat` natively, Type in the runtime. Mirror-or-document call, like H1/M1 | `wasm.core/type-of` | 3 |
59+| 04 | wrong error | `bug-04-transient-map-not-seqable.lg` | a transient map is seqable natively (`seq`, `first`, `reduce`, `into`, `apply`, `nth` with default all work); the runtime raises "don't know how to create ISeq from …TransientMap" | `wasm.core` foreign-seq hook (ckind 32) | 475 |
60+| 11 | wrong error | `bug-11-foreign-nonseqable-error.lg` | seq natives on a type value, TransientSet or TransientVector raise one generic message where native names the native (`first expected Seq`, `seq expected Seqable`, …); `(nth (type 1) 0 :nf)` raises where native returns `:nf`; `(apply f 5)` says "apply expected Seq" vs native "seq expected Seqable" | `wasm.core` foreign-seq hook, `apply*` | 200 |
61+| 15 | wrong error | `bug-15-assoc-failed-message-commas.lg` | "assoc failed for key K" embeds `(pr-str K)`; native embeds K's String() (no map commas) | `wasm.core` assoc1/dissoc1 | 1 |
62+| 07 | trap | `bug-07-nested-lazy-rethrow-traps.lg` | re-reading a lazy seq whose **nested** thunk threw traps "cast failure, expected struct Fn, got null" (native returns `()`); reached by `(concat () transient-map)` printed twice | `wasm.seq/lazy-step` clears the fn slot before `seq-view` can throw | 301 |
63+| 06 | trap | `bug-06-hash-meta-named-traps.lg` | hash of a meta'd keyword/symbol, or of a type value, traps; a 9+-key map keyed by a meta'd symbol traps on assoc. Native's meta'd hash differs from the bare name's, so delegating is not enough | `wasm.core` foreign-hash (ckind 35, 36) | 507 |
64+| 05 | trap | `bug-05-print-transient-map-set-traps.lg` | pr-str/str/print-str of a transient map or set traps; native prints `<transient-map count=N>` (transient vectors already work) | `wasm.core` print-foreign | 217 |
65+| 10 | trap | `bug-10-hash-atom-volatile-fn-traps.lg` | hash of an atom, volatile or fn traps, so does any collection holding one when hashed or put in a set | `wasm.seq/hash*` `:else` | 26 |
66+| 12 | unprefixed limit | `bug-12-case-mapping-non-ascii-traps.lg` | upper/lower-case of any non-ASCII string traps, even `"日本"` which has no case; `(int ##NaN)` traps too. Neither is parity nor a `lower-wasm:` named limit | `wasm.str` map-ascii, `int` | 13 |
67+
68+Not bugs, but recorded:
69+
70+- **R5 open (known)**: map/set seq hashes still ordered in the runtime (450139980 vs 21852162);
71+ 150 top-level hits plus nested ones (`[:cons :hash]`, `[:nest :hash]`, `[:take-rep :hash]`).
72+- **D69 declared**: `type` of a >32-conj'd vector reports ArrayVector (1,039 hits), and native
73+ messages that embed `PersistentVector` read `ArrayVector` (248). Bugs 03, 08 and 09 are the
74+ same unrecorded ArrayVector/PersistentVector split leaking into hash and print, where D69 does not
75+ cover it.
76+- **Named limits that fire as declared** (all `lower-wasm:`-prefixed, so not silent): >4-arg calls
77+ (D52, 65), float `quot`/`mod` (27; D15's float cases are named limits, verified), with-meta on a
78+ transient (16) or atom (3). `/` has no runtime twin at all (ratios, D15), so it was not fuzzed.
79+- **Harness artifacts, excluded**: the bridge's own `with-meta` on a keyword makes a value equal
80+ only to itself (49); heap addresses in printed atoms/volatiles (180); boundary closures hand a
81+ native fn a list where native passes a Repeat (5); `disj` is not a twin (7).
82+- **Native findings met on the way (not runtime bugs)**: R8's stamped empty-list meta shows up
83+ through `pop`/`rest`/`range` returning `()` (955 tallied). An exception thrown while native `=`
84+ realises a lazy seq escapes `try`/`catch` in some positions at 4e769212, and so does one from a
85+ `try` inside a vector literal; the harness works around both (comments in `fuzz.lg`).
86+ `(lazy-seq (lazy-seq (throw …)))` reads as `()` on the second access natively (bug-07 header).
87+
88+## Seams that held
89+
90+- **M1** bucket 2→1: all five colliding pairs (`97/\a`, string, keyword, vector, `2^62/2.0`) in a
91+ 9-key map: seq, `get` miss and re-assoc duplicate count all match.
92+- **D49** transient drain-regrow stays HAMT-ordered; drain-persist-regrow gives the ordered map.
93+- **D46** string index semantics: `subs`/`nth`/`get`/`count`/`seq`/`index-of`/`last-index-of` over
94+ ASCII, 2-, 3- and 4-byte text and NUL agree on value and on which calls throw (the throws are
95+ traps where native raises: the known follow-up).
96+- **D67** print modes on scalars, maps, sets, lists, entries and ArrayVectors at any nesting
97+ (the failures are bug-09's two kinds only).
98+- **D69** metadata kept by conj/assoc/dissoc/disj/pop and dropped by rest/next/seq/into/persistent!/
99+ vec/subvec on vectors, maps, sets and lists; meta'd keyword `=` and printing; `with-meta` on a
100+ scalar is the scalar.
101+- **H2** `-0.0` vs `0.0` keys at ≤8 and >8 keys; NaN keys miss; `nil`/`()` collapse to one key (D50).
102+- **S1** Range/Repeat FNV hashes; hash/`=` agreement everywhere outside bugs 01/08/16 and R5.
103+- Transients: use-after-persistent!, interleaved assoc!/dissoc!/conj!, count on all three kinds.
104+- `reduce` with `reduced` at random points over vectors, lists, lazy and chunked seqs, maps, sets.
105+- `compare` across kinds, int/float arithmetic incl. overflow and MinInt64 edges, `quot`/`mod` on
106+ ints, `read-string` round trips of every generated value incl. NaN, -0.0, escapes and colliders
107+ (no mismatch in 2300 seeds), keyword/symbol/name/namespace construction, `split`/`trim`/
108+ `replace`/`parse-long`.
109+
110+## First three to hand the implementer
111+
112+1. `bug-01-empty-vector-hash.lg`: `[]` is the most common value in xsofy state, and it silently
113+ reorders any set or large map that holds it.
114+2. `bug-08-vector-seq-hash.lg`: every `(seq v)`/`(rest v)` of an ordinary vector hashes wrong;
115+ pairs with 03/09 as one decision about recording ArrayVector vs PersistentVector.
116+3. `bug-02-lazy-error-not-cached.lg` (with `bug-07`): one function, `lazy-step`, gives a silent
117+ re-run in the flat case and an uncatchable trap in the nested case.

1+# corpus/wasm: P2.1 differential oracle programs (D75)
2+
3+Plain lg programs, one per runtime area. Each prints one labelled line per probe. Native lg
4+runs let-go's own Go natives. The backend side compiles the program plus `rt/wasm` through
5+`src/driver.lg`. Match means `checks/oracle.sh`. `.expected` files are native snapshots (D13).
6+
7+```
8+checks/run-corpus.sh corpus/wasm # the 14 programs
9+checks/run-corpus.sh corpus/wasm/pending # the backlog (13 files after P2.12)
10+checks/run-corpus.sh corpus/wasm/pending/variadic # P2.12's row (9 programs)
11+checks/run-corpus.sh --update-expected corpus/wasm corpus/wasm/pending corpus/wasm/pending/variadic
12+```
13+
14+## P2.12 status (2026-10-01)
15+
16+Variadics (D83) are in `src/`: user `& rest` fns (closures, defns, multi-arity with a variadic
17+arm, destructured rest, recur), core.lg's variadic arities, `apply` over any count, and n-ary
18+natives as values. `pending/variadic/` holds the five variadic files that were in `pending/`
19+(apply-over-4, core-variadic-closures, letfn, variadic-core, variadic-user) plus four new
20+programs: user-variadic, apply-spread (0/1/5/50/1000 elements), hof-chains, coll-extra-args.
21+All nine MATCH. The directory keeps its name because items.tsv's P2.12 row names it.
22+
23+`merge-with` MATCHes and is folded back into maps.lg. The main programs are 14/14 on the tree
24+with P2.13's rt (13/14, R5 only, on the rt before it).
25+Not covered: `%&` (native lg rejects it: `Can't resolve %&`), and a variadic fn wrapped by
26+`with-meta` (rt's wrapper copies the fixed code slots only, so its variadic arity is lost).
27+
28+## P2.11 status (2026-10-01)
29+
30+Backend fixes for F1, F2, F4/F8/F9, F5, F7, review2 bug-16 (the `##NaN` literal's payload)
31+and constfold's `(* x 0)` identity on floats are in `src/`. On the tree as it stands,
32+**10/14** programs MATCH. The four that still fail are runtime-side, and `src/` cannot fix them:
33+
34+- F3 (maps.lg `eq`, sets.lg `eq-vec-vs-list-member`, hashing.lg `agree-nested`): native's
35+ map/set equality is `valueEquiv`, which is asymmetric. A vector or map on the left decides by
36+ its own Go `Equals`, so it equals only its own kind. The runtime's `kequiv` uses plain `=`.
37+ The README's earlier "native-tier run gives false" was wrong: the runtime under native lg
38+ returns `true` too. The fix is rt patch A in the P2.11 report.

115+ float-in-fns, ifn-callables, hof-wrong-arity, typed-param-float, negate-float).
116+
117+## New failures (not in corpus/review or corpus/review2), ranked
118+
119+Silent wrong value > wrong error > crash/trap > compile error.
120+
121+**F1 (silent). Two closures capturing same-named locals in different scopes share the capture.**
122+The second closure reads the first one's final loop value. Renaming the second `i` to `j` fixes it.
123+```clojure
124+(def fs (loop [i 0 acc []] (if (= i 4) acc (recur (inc i) (conj acc (fn [] (* i 10)))))))
125+(println (mapv (fn [f] (f)) fs)) ; both [0 10 20 30]
126+(def gs (mapv (fn [i] (fn [x] (+ x i))) [0 1 2]))
127+(println (mapv (fn [f] (f 100)) gs)) ; native [100 101 102], backend [104 104 104]
128+```
129+
130+**F2 (silent). The constant pool interns literals by `=`, so the first spelling wins.**
131+`[]` and `'()` collapse into one constant, and so do `0.0` and `-0.0`. This breaks `vector?`,
132+`into '()`, hash and printing.
133+```clojure
134+(println (pr-str [])) (println (pr-str '())) ; backend: [] then [] (reverse order: () ())
135+(println [0.0 -0.0]) ; native [0.0 -0.0], backend [0.0 0.0]
136+```
137+
138+**F3 (silent). Compiled `=` on maps and sets treats vector and list values or members as equal.**
139+Native is strict inside maps and sets. A native-tier run of `wasm.core/=` gives `false`, so the
140+difference is in the compiled path.
141+```clojure
142+(println (= {:a [1]} {:a (list 1)}) (= #{[1]} #{(list 1)})) ; native false false, backend true true
143+```
144+
145+**F4 (trap). `compare` with any float operand recurses until the stack overflows.**
146+That takes down `sort` and `sort-by` on floats, `reduce +`/`*` over floats, `==`, and `=` on
147+boxed NaN/Inf. Native-tier runs of rt/ match (review2), so the likely cause is that the f64
148+`<`/`+` inside wasm.str/num-cmp and the numeric twins lower to boxed runtime calls that re-enter.
149+```clojure
150+(println (compare 1 2.5)) ; native -1, backend: Maximum call stack size exceeded
151+(println (reduce + [0.5 1])) ; native 1.5, same overflow
152+```
153+
154+**F5 (silent, minor). Vector `=` short-circuits on identical elements.**
155+Native compares vector elements without an identity check. Native lists do take the shortcut.
156+```clojure
157+(def nan ##NaN) (println (= [nan] [nan])) ; native false, backend true
158+```
159+
160+**F6 (trap). Runtime HOF twins reject non-fn callables.**
161+Direct `(:a m)` works, and so does `filter :a`. The xsofy shape `(map :id ents)` traps.
162+```clojure
163+(map :a [{:a 1}]) ; backend: wasm trap: map expected Fn (also some #{3}, mapv :a, map {..}, map [..])
164+```
165+
166+**F7 (trap). A wrong-arity closure invoked by a `reduce` or lazy `map` twin dereferences a null.**
167+The twin calls the missing `$Code` slot directly. Direct calls, `apply` and `mapv` raise native's
168+catchable arity error.
169+```clojure
170+(try (reduce (fn [a] a) [1 2]) (catch Exception e :caught)) ; backend: dereferencing a null pointer
171+```
172+
173+**F8 (trap). `max`/`min` with a float operand: `illegal cast`.** Floats reaching closures or fn
174+params via a HOF also trap (`(mapv (fn [x] (< x 0.0)) [-1.5])`, `((fn [k] (fn [x] (* k x))) 2.5)`).
175+```clojure
176+(println (max 1 2.5)) ; native 2.5, backend: illegal cast
177+```
178+
179+**F9 (compile error). Float literal where typeinfer chose i64:**
180+`unsupported coercion {:from :float, :to :int}`, which fails the whole program. It is the
181+compile-time sibling of review bug-01.
182+```clojure
183+(println (- 1.5)) ; unary minus on a float literal
184+(defn lt [a b] (< a b)) (println (lt 1.5 2.5)) ; float args to a param typed by <
185+```
186+
187+Also seen, lower impact: `(println (+ a 0.5))` with `a` a boxed float throws `lower-wasm:
188+printing this value needs the runtime` (pr-str of the same value works). review2 bug-16 has
189+flipped direction: the backend now hashes the `##NaN` literal like the computed NaN, where
190+review2 saw the opposite.
191+
192+## Known bugs carried by review-shapes.lg (status 07:28)
193+
194+The following now MATCH on the current tree: review2 bug-01, 02, 03, 04, 08, 09, 11 (first
195+and nth), 13, 14 and 15; review bug-07 at 1e5 frames. Still MISMATCH: review2 bug-16 and R5,
196+review bug-02 (DCE drops the checked `+`, both shapes), review bug-03 (LICM gives `divide by
197+zero` for a zero-trip loop) and review bug-04 (shadowed unary `-`). pending/review-traps.lg
198+holds review2 bug-11's `(apply + 5)` trap and review bug-08's compile failure.

1+# corpus/xsofy — P3.2: xsofy's world through the backend
2+
3+`checks/world-parity.sh [--keys wait|autoex|descend|deep|<str>] [N] [turns]`
4+compiles `corpus/dump-world.lg` once (xsofy on `-source-paths`, read from
5+`LG_ARGS` by `checks/wasm-run.sh`) and compares its dump with native lg per
6+seed through `checks/oracle.sh`. Results as of 2026-10-01 (lg 4e769212, xsofy
7+0c38395):
8+
9+| run | result |
10+|---|---|
11+| 20 seeds × 60 turns, wait | 20/20 MATCH |
12+| 5 seeds × 200 turns, autoex (`x` then waits) | 5/5 MATCH |
13+| 5 seeds × 200 turns, descend (`>` then waits) | 5/5 MATCH |
14+| seeds 7, 9, 10 × 200 turns, deep (98 × `x`, then `>`) | 3/3 MATCH, all reach floor 2 |
15+
16+measure.lg's autoex and descend fixtures never leave floor 1 (`>` only routes
17+to stairs already in `:memory`, and with waits after it nothing walks there),
18+so `deep` is the fixture that covers `change-floor` and a second floor.
19+Autoexplore kills the player on every seed 1–5 before turn 200, so death is
20+covered too.
21+
22+## Root causes found (each has a repro here; native output in its header)
23+
24+| repro | cause | fixed in |
25+|---|---|---|
26+| repro-01 | `term/size` is nil off a TTY natively; run.mjs said 80×24, so each descend drew the title card (ANSI) on stdout | run.mjs reports (-1,-1) = no terminal; `lw-ext/term-size-v` |
27+| repro-02 | a library def's Var is bound at compile time; lg's `vector?`/`string?` see through a Var, so the `:def` target looked like a vector literal | `typed-aux?`, `template?`, `string-const?`, `symbol-const?` exclude Vars |
28+| repro-02 | `^:private` reads as a `(with-meta name ..)` def name, which ir.build evaluates | driver drops the name's meta for library defs |
29+| repro-02 | `binding` of a program dynamic var (xsofy.opcontext/*op-context*) | saved/restored var-table global (`push-var!`/`pop-var!`) |
30+| repro-04 | typeinfer's self-call test matches by name: string/ends-with? → core/ends-with? was typed :int | `self-call?` false on a same-named foreign call (UPSTREAM) |
31+| repro-05 | unbound natives on the path: core/long, ints, re-find, string/join and ends-with? (string.lg is lg code), *assert*, *out*/*err*, push-binding!, let-go.core/now (trapped at ui load) | lw_ext fills, string.lg compiled like core.lg, var constants |
32+| repro-06 | os/args was nil, so the dump ignored its seed | `env.argc`/`env.arg` imports (proposed) |
33+| (census) | `validate after licm` on bfs-path (reached by descend) | rebuild without licm on that error (UPSTREAM) |
34+
35+## P4: xsofy's real entry in the browser (2026-10-01)
36+
37+`host/build-xsofy-module.sh` compiles `main.lg` itself (`-source-paths` =
38+xsofy, D114), wasm-opt -O3, cached by content. Checks:
39+
40+| check | what |
41+|---|---|
42+| `checks/browser-boot.sh --xsofy` | term-demo.lg under node-host == native lg on a 100x30 pty; the module in the real shell reaches the title card and the map, ?seed= honoured, xsofy/startup + xsofy/stats received |
43+| `checks/lane5.sh` | settle-based probe walk (`browser-boot.mjs --settle-walk`: `zz-determinism-probe.mjs`'s `l l j j h k l j` at seed 424242, each key sent after the previous turn finished): `document.body.innerText` byte-identical to the stock-Go lane (`lg -w` at 4e769212 + the same injected shell). The held-key burst walk is printed too but is informational only |
44+| `checks/size-boot.sh` | bundle bytes and boot times vs the stock and TinyGo lanes, written to `size-boot.md` |
45+
46+Lane 5's gate is settle-based because fixed spacing is load-dependent: the original probe sent a key every 400 ms, and under load 15-45 whether a key landed mid-turn changed the dump from run to run (one run probe IDENTICAL / held DIFFER, the next the reverse). The stock-Go lane is the sensitive one (its turns took 200-2000 ms at that load, the emitted lane 30-180 ms); both lanes coalesce identical queued keys (D98), so a late `l` after `l` is merged into one step. Measured 2026-10-01 at load 17-22: the 400 ms walk gave the stock lane a final turn counter of 5-8 for the same 8 keys (4 of 5 runs differed from the emitted lane, which always reached 8). The settle walk sends a key only after the game's `xsofy/stats` event for the previous one and 3 x 100 ms of unchanged xterm rows (>= 200 ms; a wait over 5 s is a harness failure, exit 2, not a lane mismatch), and logs the turn counter per key. The held-key bursts coalesce by design, depend on timing in both lanes, and so cannot be a byte-identity gate; `lane5.sh` prints them as informational, and the deterministic property (a burst is ONE read) stays gated by `checks/browser-boot.sh`'s `held` assertion.
47+
48+| repro | cause | fixed in |
49+|---|---|---|
50+| repro-07 | n-ary `dissoc` (4 keys) fell through to `$rt_invoke5`: FATAL ERROR on the first map frame | `seq-variant-table` → `lw-ext/dissoc-n` |
51+| repro-08 | `(.Sub (now) epoch)` (ui/millis): `core/.` was a nil slot, the title card's first tick died | `lw-ext/dot-v` (Int `Sub`; other interop a named error) |
52+| repro-09 | `os/os-name` unbound; the wasm lane says "js" (by design differs from native "darwin") | `lw-ext/os-name-v` |
53+| repro-10 | `core/char?` unbound (reached through `long-v`) | `lw-ext/char-v` |
54+| repro-11 | `js/emit` / `js/url-param` never reached the host: no title bar, ?seed= ignored | `host-emit` / `host-url-param` intrinsics (`env.emit`, `env.url_param`, D100), `json-str` |
55+
56+`js/emit`/`js/url-param` are routed to `src/lw_ext.lg` only while
57+`rt/wasm/host.lg` lacks `host-emit`; `rt-host-emit.patch` here moves the two
58+intrinsics and the JSON encoder (runtime dialect) into `wasm.host`, after
59+which lw_rt stops routing and the runtime twins are used as they are.

1+# lower-wasm host ABI (P4.0, proposed as D88)
2+
3+Each lower-wasm module talks to its host only through the imports and exports
4+listed here. `lg-wasm-host.js` implements them for browsers and Node,
5+`node-host.mjs` wraps it for the command line, and `wasmtime-adapter.wat`
6+implements the same set on WASI preview1 for wasmtime (which has no
7+`emit`/`url_param`/`argc`/`arg`: it runs only the P4.0 smoke modules). As of
8+2026-10-01 (P4.1-backend) the backend emits every import marked "emitted",
9+each only when the program reaches it (imports are tree-shaken); `getenv` is
10+still "defined".
11+
12+## Exports (module side)
13+
14+| export | type | meaning |
15+|---|---|---|
16+| start function (`_rt_init`) | — | builds runtime globals during instantiation; must not block |
17+| `lw main` | `() -> anyref` | runs the program's top-level forms; the host calls it once, through `WebAssembly.promising` when JSPI is present |
18+| `lw mem` | memory | linear memory, owned by the module (D5: strings are GC byte arrays; linear memory is only the copy area for crossing the boundary) |
19+| `lw lgex` | tag | the lg exception tag; an uncaught lg throw leaves `lw main` as this |
20+| `lw report` | `(eqref) -> ()` | formats an uncaught exception value through `print_*` |
21+| `lw trap` | `() -> i32` | 1 if a `wasm/trap` set a message (it prints it), else 0 |
22+
23+Export names contain a space so no lg symbol can collide with them (P1.7 bug-09).
24+
25+## Imports
26+
27+"Suspends" means the import is a `WebAssembly.Suspending` in JS hosts: the
28+wasm stack parks until the returned Promise settles, and the JS event loop
29+keeps running in the meantime. wasmtime has no JSPI, so there these imports
30+simply block the thread.
31+
32+| import | signature | suspends | status | semantics |
33+|---|---|---|---|---|
34+| `env.print_i64` | `(i64) -> ()` | no | emitted | decimal text of the value to the current output fd |
35+| `env.print_str` | `(ptr i32, len i32) -> ()` | no | emitted | UTF-8 bytes `[ptr, ptr+len)` to the current output fd |
36+| `env.print_nl` | `() -> ()` | no | emitted | `"\n"` to the current output fd |
37+| `env.write` | `(fd i32, ptr i32, len i32) -> i32` | no | emitted | bytes to fd 1 (program stdout) or fd 2 (stderr); returns `len`. The runtime copies the bytes to address 32 first (`rt_host_write`) |
38+| `env.sleep` | `(ms i64) -> ()` | **yes** | emitted | resumes after `ms` milliseconds (`setTimeout`); `ms <= 0` resumes on the next macrotask. Reached from `(<!! (timeout ms))` via `wasm.host/take!!` (D6, D87) |
39+| `env.nanotime` | `() -> i64` | no | emitted | monotonic ns (`performance.now()*1e6` in JS hosts, `CLOCK_MONOTONIC` under WASI); only differences mean anything |
40+| `env.getenv` | `(name_ptr i32, name_len i32, buf i32, cap i32) -> i32` | no | defined | copies the value into `[buf, buf+cap)` and returns its byte length; returns `> cap` (nothing copied, retry with a bigger buffer) or `-1` when unset. The backend still lowers `host-getenv` to nil |
41+| `env.emit` | `(name_ptr i32, name_len i32, json_ptr i32, json_len i32) -> ()` | no | emitted (P4.1) | `js/emit`: the event name and the data as JSON text, let-go's `_lgEmit(name, dataJson)` shape; the JSON is byte-identical to let-go's (`fromValue` + `encoding/json`: sorted keys, HTML escaping). The browser host parses the JSON and fires the `window` CustomEvent the shell listens for (`xsofy/startup` sets the title and quest, `xsofy/stats`, `xsofy/replay-dump`, …); node and run.mjs drop it. xsofy calls `js/emit` 10 times |
42+| `env.url_param` | `(name_ptr i32, name_len i32, buf i32, cap i32) -> i32` | no | emitted (P4.1) | `js/url-param`: getenv's contract over the page's query string; `-1` when absent or off-browser (native returns nil). xsofy reads `?seed=` and friends through it (6 calls) |
43+| `env.argc` | `() -> i32` | no | emitted (P3.2, D115) | `os/args` length; JS hosts take `argv` (default `['lg']`) |
44+| `env.arg` | `(i i32, buf i32, cap i32) -> i32` | no | emitted (P3.2, D115) | argument `i`, getenv's copy contract |
45+| `term.read_key` | `(buf i32, cap i32) -> i32` | **yes** | emitted (D104) | waits for the next key and copies its UTF-8 bytes (one `sendInput` call = one key, ≤ 16 bytes, as in let-go's SAB ring) into `[buf, buf+cap)`; returns the byte count, **0 = end of input** (`read-key` → nil). Coalesces (D98, below). The runtime builds the lg String |
46+| `term.key_pending` | `() -> i32` | no | emitted (D104) | 1 if a key is queued, else 0 (`key-pending?`) |
47+| `term.size` | `() -> (i32 i32)` | no | emitted (D104) | `cols rows` as a multi-value result (`term/size` → `[cols rows]`); default 80×24 |
48+| `term.write` | `(ptr i32, len i32) -> i32` | no | defined | same stream as `env.write` fd 1. let-go's `term/write` is `(write *out* s)`, so the runtime may use either; this exists so a terminal host can tell term output apart if it ever needs to |
49+
50+**Not imports, and why:**
51+- **Colour and cursor** (`term/set-fg`, `set-bg`, `move-cursor`, `clear`, `bold`, …):
52+ let-go's wasm build already writes these as ANSI escapes to `*out*`
53+ (`pkg/rt/term_wasm.go`, `WriteToOut`), and xterm interprets them. They belong
54+ in the runtime as string builders over `env.write`. `xsofy-shell.html` takes
55+ nothing from `LetGoHost` beyond the text stream.
56+- **`set_size`** goes from host to module, so it is not an import. It is
57+ `LetGoHost.setSize(c, r)` → `host.setSize`, which updates the state that
58+ `term.size` reads.
59+- **`term/flush`**: `env.write` is unbuffered on every host, so the runtime can
60+ implement flush as a no-op.
61+
62+## Who owns what
63+
64+- **Module:** linear memory and everything in it. Address 0 holds an active
65+ data segment (`"niltruefalse…"`) that `print_str` reads, so low addresses are
66+ **not** free scratch (the first wasmtime adapter assumed they were and
67+ garbled `true`). Strings bound for `env.write` are copied to 32 and up.
68+- **Host:** reads `[ptr, ptr+len)` synchronously inside the call and copies it
69+ out (the module reuses the area right away). For `read_key` the host writes
70+ into `buf` **after** resuming, so it re-reads `mem.buffer`, since memory may
71+ have grown while the stack was parked. Text decoding is per fd and streaming
72+ (`TextDecoder {stream:true}`), so a UTF-8 sequence split across two writes
73+ still decodes.
74+- **Input queue:** belongs to the host. Keys sent before `lw main` starts are
75+ dropped, and at most 8 keys queue (the rest are dropped). Both match let-go's
76+ ring; `node-host` lifts the cap for piped input.
77+
78+## Key coalescing (D98)
79+
80+`term.read_key` is the consumer half of let-go's `HostKeySource.ReadKey`
81+(`pkg/rt/keysource_js_wasm.go:78-127`), and `sendInput` the producer half
82+(`lg-host-core.js` `_lgKey`):
83+
84+- `sendInput` refuses an empty key, a key over 16 UTF-8 bytes, and a key past
85+ the 8-slot capacity (returns `false`, as `_lgKey` does).
86+- `read_key` takes the head key. If its length is outside 1..16 it is drained
87+ alone and the read returns 0 (nil). Otherwise every following queued key
88+ with the same bytes is drained with it: a held key that outruns the program
89+ is one read, not a backlog. Distinct keys are never merged.
90+- `sendInput` always queues and then wakes a parked `read_key`, which resumes
91+ in a later microtask and reads the queue itself. Keys sent in one task (an
92+ auto-repeat burst) are therefore all queued by the time it looks, which is
93+ what makes them coalesce even when the program was already waiting. Handing
94+ the first key straight to the waiter, as P4.0 did, would make a burst into
95+ two reads.
96+
97+`node-host` turns coalescing **off** unless given `--coalesce`, so scripted
98+and piped input still reaches the program key for key. The wasmtime adapter
99+reads stdin and does not coalesce (it has no queue to look ahead in).
100+
101+## Errors (identical to src/run.mjs, D12)
102+
103+If `lw main` rejects, the host switches the current output fd to 2 and prints
104+`error: `. If the exception carries `lw lgex`, `lw report(arg0)` prints the
105+message. Otherwise, if `lw trap()` is 1, the module has already printed it.
106+Failing both, the host prints the JS error message. A newline follows, and the
107+result is `{code: 1, error: <that line>}`. A trap in the start function
108+surfaces from `instantiate` and gets the same `error:` line. node-host matches
109+run.mjs byte for byte on `corpus/control/uncaught{,-value,-raw}.lg`. Under
110+wasmtime an uncaught lg exception exits 1 with wasmtime's "thrown Wasm
111+exception" backtrace instead; the adapter does not format it.
112+
113+## Browser surface: `window.LetGoHost`
114+
115+`index.html` defines let-go's surface with the same shape as
116+`lg-host-core.js`: `onReady(cb)`, `onOutput(cb)`, `onEmit(cb)`,
117+`sendInput(str)`, `setSize(c, r)`. It is a classic script that runs before any
118+shell code and buffers output and the ready signal until a shell registers.
119+`index.html` reports ready mode **`'jspi'`**. `xsofy-shell-adapter.js`, the
120+surface the real shell runs on, reports **`'worker'`** (D90). The reason is
121+the shell's own gate: `xsofy-shell.html` calls `setSize`, registers
122+`term.onResize` and wires `term.onData` → `sendInput` only inside
123+`if (mode === 'worker')`. In `'main'` (let-go's output-only mode) and in any
124+other value it shows output but never sends a key or a size. `'worker'` names
125+let-go's worker + SAB-ring mechanism, which this host does not use; what the
126+shell actually needs to know is "input is live", and that is true here.
127+Reporting `'worker'` keeps the shell byte-identical to upstream (changing its
128+gate would be an xsofy PR). With `'jspi'` the `--xsofy-shell` check fails
129+boot, size, held and quit (falsified 2026-10-01).
130+
131+## xsofy-shell.html on this host (P4.1)
132+
133+`host/build-xsofy-serve.sh <dir> [modules…]` builds a serve directory:
134+`host/xsofy.html` (let-go's `-w-shell none` frame: `#status`, `#app`, then a
135+classic `<script src="xsofy-shell-adapter.js">`) with the shell injected by
136+the workspace's own `local-scripts/inject-shell.sh` (sentinel-wrapped, before
137+the body close tag; the shell is copied byte for byte). The adapter defines
138+`window.LetGoHost` synchronously, so it exists when the shell binds at parse
139+time, then dynamic-imports `lg-wasm-host.js`.
140+
141+What the shell expects at boot, and who provides it:
142+
143+| shell expects | provided by |
144+|---|---|
145+| `window.LetGoHost` with `onReady/onOutput/sendInput/setSize` before its own script runs | adapter (classic script ahead of the injection point) |
146+| `#app` (xterm mount) and optionally `#status` (hidden on ready) | `xsofy.html`, same ids as let-go's `host.html` |
147+| `onReady(mode)` with `mode === 'worker'` to wire input and size | adapter reports `'worker'` (above) |
148+| output buffered until it registers `onOutput` | adapter buffers; the shell buffers again until xterm opens |
149+| xterm 5.5 + addon-fit from cdn.jsdelivr.net | network; nothing local |
150+| Fairfax HD (inlined base64 in the shell), loaded before `term.open` | the shell itself; `?font=system` skips it |
151+| `build-info.json` next to the page (optional; 404 = ad-hoc bundle) | absent |
152+| `xsofy/startup`, `xsofy/stats`, `xsofy/term-size`, `xsofy/perf`, `xsofy/replay-dump` window events (title, quest, stats, replay link) | `env.emit` → `onEmit` default → `CustomEvent` (P4.1: the emitted xsofy fires them) |
153+| nothing printed at boot: the title bar shows `—` until `xsofy/startup` arrives; the terminal shows whatever the program writes | — |
154+
155+The adapter starts `lw main` only after the shell's first `setSize` (or 2 s
156+without one). The shell calls `setSize` after awaiting its font and opening
157+xterm, roughly 150–180 ms after load in headless Chromium; a module that
158+starts sooner reads the 80×24 default instead of the real grid. let-go's lane
159+has the same race but hides it behind its slower boot.
160+
161+## COI: not needed
162+
163+let-go's `read-key` needs a SharedArrayBuffer ring, hence COOP/COEP (the
164+workspace CLAUDE.md, "Serving a WASM bundle requires cross-origin isolation").
165+With JSPI, a blocked `read_key` is a parked wasm stack waiting on a Promise
166+that `sendInput` resolves on the same thread, so no shared memory is involved.
167+Evidence from `checks/browser-boot.sh` (Chromium 148, 2026-10-01): served by
168+plain `python3 -m http.server`, the page reports `crossOriginIsolated=false`
169+and `SharedArrayBuffer` undefined, yet hello still matches native lg and the
170+keys probe echoes `a b q`. Served by `coi-serve.py`, both are true and the
171+results are identical. The JSPI lane can therefore deploy without the COI
172+service-worker fallback. That fallback is also unreliable under headless
173+automation (CLAUDE.md), so dropping it simplifies P4.1–P4.3.
174+
175+## Stack depth under JSPI (a P4.1 risk)
176+
177+Closed by D99: xsofy's deepest stack is 20 lg frames, well inside the
178+browser budget measured below.
179+
180+A promising export runs on a V8 secondary stack sized by
181+`--wasm-stack-switching-stack-size`, 984 kB by default. A worker's
182+`resourceLimits.stackSizeMb` (run.mjs's D33 mechanism) does not reach that
183+stack. Measured with a non-tail boxed `(+ 1 (down (- n 1)))`:
184+
185+| host | deepest passing | first failing |
186+|---|---|---|
187+| Chromium 148, page (flags impossible) | 5,000 | 7,000 |
188+| node 25, defaults or in a worker with 256 MB | 5,000 | 10,000 |
189+| node 25 main thread, `--stack-size=262000 --wasm-stack-switching-stack-size=262144` | 1,000,000 | — (3M fails, as it does under run.mjs) |
190+| wasmtime 47, `-W max-wasm-stack=268435456` | 1,000,000 | — |
191+
192+So node-host runs on the main thread and re-execs itself with those two
193+flags. In a browser the limit is fixed at about 5–7k frames of this shape.
194+Native lg grows its stacks into the millions. Before P4.1, check whether
195+xsofy's deepest recursion (map generation, FOV) fits. If it does not, the
196+fix belongs in the backend (loops for self-recursion, or an explicit stack),
197+not in the host.
