@@ -0,0 +1,88 @@
1+# wasm.intrinsics (P2.1, native half, 2026-09-30)
2+
3+The var set the wasm runtime is written against (plan D4). Source of truth is
4+the metadata on each `^:intrinsic` defn in `intrinsics.lg` (`:wasm`, `:type`);
5+`intrinsics_test.lg`'s `intrinsic-coverage` test fails if an intrinsic lacks
6+either key or is not exercised by that file. Check: `checks/run-intrinsics-native.sh`.
7+
8+**Types.** Every operand and result is an lg typeinfer type: `:int` = i64,
9+`:float` = f64, `:bool` = i32, `:any` = `(ref null eq)`. i32 and i8 exist only
10+as field/element storage; the backend inserts `i32.wrap_i64` /
11+`i64.extend_i32_*` inside the intrinsic's expansion, so runtime lg never sees
12+an i32. `decl` is a var defined by a declaration form, resolved statically.
13+
14+**Declarations** (top-level `def`s the backend reads as a data table, emitted
15+as ONE `(rec ...)` group so same-shaped types stay distinct for `ref.test`):
16+`(defstruct Name [t ...])` with `t` in `:i64 :f64 :i32 :ref :funcref` or
17+`[:mut t]`; `(defarray Name t)` (elements always mutable); `(deffunc Name [t ...] t)`;
18+built-in `Bytes` = `(array (mut i8))`.
19+
20+Used by: **P** = `pvec.lg`, **H** = HAMT (P2.4), **C** = closures/arity dispatch (P1.3),
21+**V** = value model, hash, strings (P2.2/P2.6), **IO** = host boundary. All are used by the test file.
22+
23+| name | arity | wasm | type | used by |
24+|---|---|---|---|---|
25+| `new` | 1–8 | struct.new | [decl fields…] → :any | P H C V |
26+| `get` | 3 | ref.cast; struct.get (i32: extend_s) | [decl const :any] → field | P H C V |
27+| `set!` | 4 | ref.cast; struct.set (mut fields only) | [decl const :any T] → nil | H (transient edit), V (hash cache) |
28+| `is?` | 2 | ref.test | [decl :any] → :bool | H (node kind), V (type dispatch) |
29+| `as` | 2 | ref.cast (non-null) | [decl :any] → :any | H V |
30+| `array-new` | 3 | array.new | [decl :int T] → :any | P H C |
31+| `aget` / `aset!` | 3 / 4 | array.get / array.set | [decl :any :int (T)] | P H C |
32+| `alen` | 1 | array.len; extend_u | [:any] → :int | P H V |
33+| `array-copy` | 6 | array.copy (memmove) | [decl dst di src si n] → nil | P H V |
34+| `ref-eq` | 2 | ref.eq | [:any :any] → :bool | H (identity fast path, transient owner) V |
35+| `null` / `null?` | 0 / 1 | ref.null none / ref.is_null | | P H |
36+| `i31` / `i31?` / `i31-get` | 1 | ref.i31 / ref.test i31 / i31.get_s | | V (D2 hybrid box), P test |
37+| `i64-add` `-sub` `-mul` | 2 | i64.add/sub/mul (wrap) | [:int :int] → :int | V (murmur3, hash mixing) |
38+| `i64-shl` `-shr-s` `-shr-u` | 2 | i64.shl/shr_s/shr_u (count mod 64) | [:int :int] → :int | H (bitpos) V |
39+| `i64-lt-u` | 2 | i64.lt_u | → :bool | V (uint32 hash compare) |
40+| `i64-clz` `-ctz` `-popcnt` | 1 | i64.clz/ctz/popcnt | → :int | H (popcnt = bitmap index) |
41+| `i32-wrap` | 1 | extend_i32_s(wrap_i64) | → :int | V (32-bit murmur3 in i64) |
42+| `i64-extend-i32-u` | 1 | extend_i32_u(wrap_i64) | → :int | H V (hash as uint32) |
43+| `i64-to-f64` / `f64-to-i64` | 1 | f64.convert_i64_s / i64.trunc_f64_s (traps) | | V (`double`, `long`) |
44+| `f64-neg` | 1 | f64.neg (sign bit only, NaN included) | [:float] → :float | V (`neg1`: unary `-` on a Float, P2.13) |
45+| `bytes-new` `bget` `bset!` | 1/2/3 | array.new_default / get_u / set ($Bytes) | | V (strings, D5) IO |
46+| `bytes-of-string` | 1 | array.new_data (literal only) | [:string] → :any | V IO |
47+| `string-of-bytes` | 1 | none (identity) | [:any] → :string | reference/test boundary only |
48+| `host-write` `host-sleep` `host-nanotime` `host-getenv` | 2/1/0/1 | call $env.* | | IO (D6, D11's `env.write`) |
49+| `trap` | 1 | unreachable | [:string] → :bottom | P V |
50+| `funcref` / `call-ref` | 2 / 2–7 | ref.func / call_ref $Sig (7 = `$Code4`: closure + 4 args, P2.7) | | C |
51+
52+43 intrinsics, 3 declaration macros, 1 built-in type, as of 2026-10-01 (`f64-neg` added
53+by P2.13: `(* -1.0 x)` may return either NaN sign in wasm, Go's `-x` flips it; lg's own
54+unary `-` on a Float is Go's `-x`, so it is the reference, and native `hash` sees the bit).
55+`new` gained its 7-field arity on 2026-10-01 for D52's `$Fn`.
56+
57+**Reference semantics.** Wrapping arithmetic, shift counts mod 64, packed-i8
58+truncation in `bset!`, and memmove `array-copy` match wasm exactly (measured on
59+lg 4e769212: `unchecked-add` wraps; lg's own shifts follow Go, so the reference
60+masks the count; `(long ##NaN)` is 0 and `(long 1e19)` saturates, so
61+`f64-to-i64` checks the trap cases itself). The reference is *stricter* than
62+wasm where wasm is silent and a correct runtime never relies on it: an
63+out-of-range `i31` traps (wasm drops the top bit), an index ≥ 2^32 traps (wasm
64+would wrap it to i32 and may land in bounds), a raw lg value in a `:ref` slot
65+or an out-of-range value in an `:i32` slot throws. One exception (P2.10): a
66+native exception may sit in a `:ref` slot, as the stand-in for the payload a
67+wasm `catch` binds, which is always a `(ref null eq)` (a LazySeq caches the
68+error its thunk threw). Host calls are
69+deterministic: a virtual clock advanced only by `host-sleep`, env from
70+`*host-env*`.
71+
72+**Not intrinsics, on purpose.** No `wasm/throw`/`wasm/try`: the runtime throws
73+catchable errors with lg's own `try` and `core/throw` (P1.2's `:try`) once
74+`ex-info` exists (P2.7); internal invariants use `trap`, which is uncatchable
75+in wasm too. No `blen` (`alen` takes `Bytes`) and no `i64-extend-i32-s` (it is
76+`i32-wrap`).
77+
78+**HAMT (P2.4) needs, and has:** BitmapIndexedNode `[:i64 bitmap, [:mut :ref] edit, :ref arr]`,
79+ArrayNode `[[:mut :i64] cnt, [:mut :ref] edit, :ref arr]`, HashCollisionNode
80+`[:i64 hash, [:mut :i64] cnt, [:mut :ref] edit, :ref arr]` (`defstruct`/`new`/`get`/`set!`);
81+node kind dispatch (`is?`/`as`); `bitpos = 1 << ((h >>> shift) & 31)` (IR shifts or `i64-shl`/`i64-shr-u`);
82+`index = popcnt(bitmap & (bit - 1))` (`i64-popcnt`); hash as uint32 (`i64-extend-i32-u`);
83+insert/remove by allocate-and-copy-twice (`array-new`, `array-copy`); key compare via
84+the runtime's `=` with a `ref-eq` fast path; transient ownership by `ref-eq` on the edit token.
85+Covered. **Gap for P2.2:** hashing a float needs its IEEE bits (`i64.reinterpret_f64`),
86+which this set lacks and which native lg offers no non-interop way to compute; add
87+`f64-bits` there, with its reference implementation, when P2.2 needs it. Until then
88+`wasm.seq/float-bits` computes the bits with float arithmetic (STR.md, Floats).

@@ -0,0 +1,197 @@
1+# wasm.reader (P3.0, 2026-10-01)
2+
3+`read-string` for data, in the runtime dialect (`reader.lg`, ns
4+`wasm.reader`, loaded after `core.lg`). D70: let-go's `edn.lg` wraps a Go
5+native, so there is no lg reader to compile; this is a port of the Go one.
6+Ground truth is let-go 4e769212 built with go1.27.1. Citations are
7+`~/projects-new/3p/let-go/pkg/compiler/reader.go` unless stated.
8+
9+xsofy calls `core/read-string` (not `edn/read-string`) at `xsofy/seed.lg:27`
10+and `xsofy/console.lg:94`. That native is `newDataReaderWithResolvers` +
11+`ReadSkipNoValue` (`eval.go:241`): the first form, data semantics
12+(metadata attached, real sets, duplicate keys rejected, `#_` splices
13+nothing), leading comments and discards skipped, the rest of the input
14+ignored.
15+
16+## API
17+
18+| fn | args | result |
19+|---|---|---|
20+| `read-string` `^{:twin "core/read-string"}` | a Str | the first form; raises on error |
21+| `read-string*` | a Str, a boxed rune index | `[form end]`, end the rune index after what was consumed; positions in messages count from `start`, as reading `(subs s start)` would |
22+
23+A non-string argument raises `read-string: expected String, got <%T>` with
24+Go's type name for the kinds the runtime has (`*vm.Nil`, `vm.Int`,
25+`vm.ArrayVector`, `*vm.List`, `*vm.PersistentMap`, …; `eval.go:247`).
26+
27+## Shape
28+
29+One reader state per call: `RS` (bytes, length, byte position, rune
30+position, line, column) and `Aux` (lastCol, lastRune, lastSize, the error
31+chain, the caused-by-EOF flag, a Void marker, the `:line`/`:column`
32+keywords). `new` takes at most 7 fields, hence two structs. No runtime
33+global. Read functions return a value, the Void marker (comment, discard),
34+or the state itself on failure, which mirrors Go's `(Value, error)` returns
35+without try/catch and lets `#_` swallow a non-EOF error as
36+`readFormComment` does (`:1962`). `next!`/`unread!` track line and column in
37+runes as `next`/`unread` do (`:151`, `:167`), so positions in messages match
38+without a rescan. Input is UTF-8 bytes decoded by `wasm.seq/decode-at`
39+(invalid bytes are U+FFFD of width 1, as `bufio.ReadRune`).
40+
41+## Token table
42+
43+First rune after whitespace (`unicode.IsSpace` or `,`), as `Read` (`:260`)
44+dispatches it:
45+
46+| first rune | reads as | notes |
47+|---|---|---|
48+| a Unicode digit (Nd) | number token → the number cascade below | `٣` starts a number and is `invalid number: ٣` |
49+| `+` `-` then a digit | number | `+` or `-` at end of input is an EOF error, not a symbol |
50+| `(` | list, with position meta `{:line L :column C}` | `meta` reads FormSource (`lang.go:3456`) |
51+| `[` | vector (no meta) | |
52+| `{` | map: even count, no duplicate keys (`=`), built on a transient as `NewArrayMap` | order: array-map ≤ 8, HAMT past (D29) |
53+| `#{` | set, conj in order, duplicate element is an error | |
54+| `"` | string, escapes `\t \r \n \b \f \\ \" \uXXXX` (surrogate pairs combined) | |
55+| `\` | char: one rune, `space tab backspace newline formfeed return`, `uXXXX`, `oNNN` | `%x`/`%o` scan quirks below |
56+| `'` `@` `~` `~@` | `(quote x)` `(deref x)` `(unquote x)` `(unquote-splicing x)` | no meta |
57+| `#'` | `(var sym)`; any other form is `invalid var quote` | |
58+| `#_` | discard the next form | |
59+| `;` | comment to end of line | |
60+| `##` | `##Inf` `##-Inf` `##NaN` | |
61+| `^` | metadata on the next form | data mode: attached to lists, vectors, maps, sets; any other form reads as `(with-meta form m)` with a symbol tag quoted (`:1617`) |
62+| `) ] }` | `unmatched delimiter c` | |
63+| `` ` `` `#(` `#"` `#?` `#letter` | named limits (below) | |
64+| anything else | a token up to whitespace or a terminating macro (`( ) [ ] { } " \ ; @ ` ~ ^`) | `nil` `true` `false`; `:…` keyword; else symbol |
65+
66+Symbols are not validated (`a/b/c`, `/`, `clojure.core//`, `a:b`, `a#b`,
67+`a'b` all read). Keywords reject an empty part, a leading or trailing `:`
68+or `::` inside a part (`hasInvalidKeywordColon`, `:324`); `:/` is the
69+keyword `/`.
70+
71+## Numbers
72+
73+`readNumber` (`:638`) collects the token and tries, in order, Go parsers
74+whose own syntax decides the result. The cascade is reproduced step by step
75+because each step's quirks are observable:
76+
77+| step | parser | findings (native, measured) |
78+|---|---|---|
79+| `…N` / `…n` | `big.Int.SetString(s, 10)` | `1N` is a BigInt even when small; `1.5N`, `0x10N` fall through to `invalid number` |
80+| `…M` / `…m` | `big.Float.Parse(s, 10)` | accepts `p` exponents: `1p3M` is `8.0M` |
81+| `0x…` (after an optional `-`) | `big.Int.SetString(hex, 16)` | the hex part takes its own sign: `0x-5` is -5, `-0x-5` is 5; `+0x1F` is invalid; past int64 → BigInt, but `-0x8000000000000000` is an Int |
82+| `0[0-7]…` | `ParseInt(s[1:], 8)` | `017` is 15; `018` and `08` are DECIMAL 18 and 8 (octal fails, decimal wins); octal overflow ends up a decimal BigInt |
83+| `NrDDD` | `Atoi(N)` in 2..36, `ParseInt(DDD, N)` | both take a sign: `+2r101` 5, `2r-101` -5, `-2r-101` 5; overflow is `invalid number`, never BigInt |
84+| `N/D` | `ParseInt` both, `big.Rat` | an Int when D divides N (`4/2` is 2, `4/-2` is -2); `1/2` a Ratio; `1/0` invalid; `MinInt64/-1` a BigInt |
85+| decimal | `ParseInt(s, 10)` | past int64 → BigInt |
86+| float | `ParseFloat(s, 64)` | underscores between digits are legal: `1_000` is the FLOAT 1000.0; hex floats `0x1p-2`; `1.` and `1.e5` read; overflow (`1e309`, `1.7976931348623159e308`) is `invalid number`; underflow is 0.0 |
87+
88+Floats: readFloat's syntax check with `underscoreOK`
89+(`internal/strconv/atof.go:182`, `atoi.go:252`), then `decimal.set` and
90+`decimal.floatBits` (`atof.go:80`, `:322`) over the same multiprecision
91+decimal str.lg's formatter ports (800 digits, `trunc` flag, 59-bit shift
92+chunks). Go's fast paths (exact, Eisel-Lemire, uscale) all return the
93+correctly rounded double, so the exact slow path is the whole algorithm.
94+`floatBits` yields a 53-bit mantissa and a binary exponent; the double is
95+`f64(mant) * 2^(exp-52)`, scaled in exact power-of-two steps (every
96+intermediate has at most 53 significant bits and an exponent at or above
97+the result's, so no step rounds). No `f64-from-bits` intrinsic is needed.
98+
99+## Error messages
100+
101+Every failure is a `ReaderError` (`errors.go:37`): `Syntax error reading
102+source at (<read-string>:L:C).\n<msg>`, L and C 1-based and counted in runes
103+at the moment of failure. Each `Wrap` appends `\n\tcaused by <inner>`
104+(`errors.AddCause`), so the chain depth is part of the message:
105+`(1` and `""` carry two `unexpected error` layers over `EOF`, each enclosing
106+collection adds one. The chain is kept as a vector of layers and joined once
107+when raised. Static messages, all compared exactly by the test:
108+
109+| message | site |
110+|---|---|
111+| `unexpected error` (wrapping EOF or an inner error) | eatWhitespace `:210`, Read `:263-291`, readToken, readString `:443-448`, readChar `:582`, collections `:762-894` |
112+| `invalid token: <tok>` | interpretToken `:345-375` |
113+| `unpaired high surrogate \uXXXX`, `invalid low surrogate \uXXXX`, `unpaired low surrogate \uXXXX` | readString `:479-494` |
114+| `unknown escape sequence \c` | `:499` |
115+| `invalid escape sequence \u<digits read>` | readHexEscape `:554`, `:561` |
116+| `invalid char constant \<tok>` | readChar `:635` |
117+| `invalid number: <tok>` | readNumber `:750` |
118+| `map literal must contain even number of forms` | `:847` |
119+| `duplicate key in map literal: <key.String()>` | `:855` |
120+| `Duplicate key: <elem>` | readSet `:905` |
121+| `reading quoted form`, `reading deref form`, `reading unquote prefix`, `reading unquoted form`, `reading quoted var`, `invalid var quote` | `:915-1186` |
122+| `reading meta` (drops the inner chain), `unsupported meta form` | readMeta `:1620-1683` |
123+| `reading symbolic value`, `unknown symbolic value: ##<tok>` | `:1705-1720` |
124+| `reading hash macro`, `invalid hash macro` | `:1727`, `:1737` |
125+| `unmatched delimiter c` | `:1883` |
126+
127+Messages that embed a value use `wasm.str/value-string` (Value.String()),
128+so `duplicate key in map literal: "a"` and `Duplicate key: \a` match too.
129+
130+## Named limits
131+
132+Raised catchable (wasm.core/raise) with `lower-wasm: read-string: …`,
133+not trapped, because the input is user data and xsofy's console catches
134+read errors. Each names what native would return:
135+
136+| input | native | why not here |
137+|---|---|---|
138+| `1N`, past-int64 integers, hex past int64, `MinInt64/-1` | BigInt | no BigInt box |
139+| `1/2` | Ratio | no Ratio box |
140+| `1.5M` | BigDecimal | no BigDecimal box |
141+| `0x1p-2` | Float | hex floats: rare, need a hex mantissa path (the decimal type only takes decimal digits) |
142+| `::k`, `::alias/k` (after the validity checks) | `:<current-ns>/k` | needs `*ns*` / the alias table |
143+| `` `x `` | syntax-quoted form | resolves symbols against `*ns*` |
144+| `#(…)` | `(fn* [%1] …)` | code, not data |
145+| `#"re"` | Regex | no Regex box |
146+| `#?(…)` | the `:lg`/`:default` branch | reader conditionals |
147+| `#inst`, `#uuid`, `#foo` | Instant/UUID, or the bare value when no reader is registered | tagged literals / `*data-readers*` |
148+| `^m ;c`, `';c`, … | `(with-meta <VOID> m)`, `(quote <VOID>)` | Go's VOID sentinel is not a value here |
149+
150+The test admits a limit only when native's answer shows the named thing
151+(a BigInt in the result, `#?` in the input, …). As of 2026-10-01 the corpus
152+hits 28 limits in 951 inputs.
153+
154+## Divergences (known, not tested as matches)
155+
156+- An empty list read gets position meta like any list. Native stamps it on
157+ the process-global `EmptyList` singleton (`FormSource.Set` keys by
158+ pointer, `vm/source.go:278`), so `(meta ())` anywhere returns the last
159+ read's position: an upstream bug, not reproduced. The test drops
160+ `:line`/`:column` from empty lists on both sides.
161+- Position meta lives in the list's meta field (D69), so `conj` keeps it;
162+ native's FormSource is keyed by the `*List` pointer and a conj'd list has
163+ none.
164+- A named limit inside `#_` raises; native reads the discarded form and
165+ drops it (`#_ 1N 5` is 5 natively).
166+- `\u-8000000000000000` (a char whose `%x` scan yields MinInt64) is
167+ rejected; native reads `\u0000` via `rune(hexi)` truncation. Every other
168+ truncation is reproduced (`က00041` is `\A`, `\u-041` is rune -65).
169+- Invalid UTF-8 input is decoded exactly as Go does but untested: native lg
170+ strings cannot be built with invalid bytes from the test.
171+
172+## Dedupe (proposed, not applied: other rt files are frozen for P3.0)
173+
174+reader.lg duplicates str.lg's private multiprecision decimal (`dec-trim!`,
175+`right-shift!`, `left-shift!`, `dec-shift!`, `should-round-up?`) and a
176+small byte buffer with `encode-rune!`. Making those public in str.lg
177+(`defn-` to `defn`) lets reader.lg drop ~110 lines. core.lg's
178+`read-string` stub (core.lg:1005, a trap) should go once reader.lg is in
179+the load order; until then `tools/twin-manifest.lg` lists both claims.
180+
181+## Checks
182+
183+`corpus/intrinsics/reader_test.lg` via `checks/run-intrinsics-native.sh`
184+(7 deftests, ~11 s under the reference intrinsics on 2026-10-01):
185+
186+- `edn-corpus`: every line of `corpus/edn/cases.txt` (951 as of
187+ 2026-10-01; regenerate with `lg corpus/edn/gen.lg`): pr-str equal (the
188+ runtime printer against native's, so map/set order and float digits too),
189+ metadata of every nested collection equal, or the same error message.
190+- `floats-round-trip-bits`: the 278 finite lines of
191+ `corpus/floats/pr-str.expected` read to the same IEEE bits.
192+- `floats-decimal-sweep`: long decimal strings (17-25 digits, exponents
193+ -345..334) bit for bit; 100 by default, 1000 with `SLOW=1` (~40 s).
194+- `argument-errors`, `read-string-star`, `xsofy-call-sites`, `dialect`.
195+
196+Falsified 2026-10-01: writing `h + 1` for a `\uXXXX` escape turns
197+`edn-corpus` red with 144 mismatches.

1+# rt/wasm — the wasm runtime in the runtime dialect
2+
3+Thirteen namespaces that load together under native lg as one runtime (P2.9, P3.1),
4+with the reference `wasm.intrinsics` standing in for the wasm instructions.
5+Ground truth is let-go 4e769212. Each file's header states its dialect; the
6+`dialect` deftest of its test file enforces it.
7+
8+## Load order and link step
9+
10+| order | file | ns | requires | owns |
11+|---|---|---|---|---|
12+| 1 | `intrinsics.lg` | `wasm.intrinsics` | | the 43 intrinsics, `defstruct`/`defarray`/`deffunc`, `Bytes` (INTRINSICS.md) |
13+| 2 | `pvec.lg` | `wasm.pvec` | 1 | the persistent vector, `Node` arrays |
14+| 3 | `seq.lg` | `wasm.seq` | 1 2 | the value model: every box struct, `Fn` (D52), `kind`, `equiv?`, `hash`; seq kinds, chunking, laziness, the seq natives; strings as collections; `float-bits`; the foreign-kind hook slots (SEQ.md) |
15+| 4 | `str.lg` | `wasm.str` | 1 2 3 | building the scalar boxes, keyword/symbol interning, `str`/`pr-str`/`print-str`, float formatting, the string natives, `compare` (STR.md) |
16+| 5 | `phm.lg` | `wasm.phm` | 1 2 3 | the persistent/transient map (array-map + HAMT), map hooks (slot 0) |
17+| 6 | `phs.lg` | `wasm.phs` | 1 2 3 5 | the persistent/transient set, set hooks (slot 1) |
18+| 7 | `arrays.lg` | `wasm.arrays` | 1-4 | let-go's typed arrays (`int-array` `byte-array` `aget` `aset` `alength` `aclone` `bytes`), the `Arr` struct, and the count/seq/print/get view wasm.core routes to it (kind 37) |
19+| 8 | `core.lg` | `wasm.core` | 1-7 | the generic dispatchers (`assoc` `get` `conj` `nth` `peek` `pop` `transient` ...), numbers as values, `compare`, atom/volatile, meta, exceptions, `apply*`, `sort`, `type`; the link step `install!` |
20+| 9 | `reader.lg` | `wasm.reader` | 1-8 | `read-string` for data (EDN subset of let-go's data reader) and `read-string*`; per-call state, no global (READER.md) |
21+| 10 | `math.lg` | `wasm.math` | 1 3 4 8 | `/` `rem`, the bit ops and unchecked arithmetic as values, `float` `float?` `int?` `bigint?` `rand-int`, math/abs sqrt exp pow (Go's portable float algorithms, i.e. lg's wasm build) |
22+| 11 | `xxhash.lg` | `wasm.xxhash` | 1 3 4 7 | `xxh3/HashSeed` and `xxh3/Hash`: XXH3-64 as github.com/zeebo/xxh3 v1.1.0 computes it |
23+| 12 | `host.lg` | `wasm.host` | 1 3 4 7 8 | `println` `print` `pr` `prn`, IO handles (`write!` `flush!` `close!`, `out-handle`/`err-handle` for `*out*`/`*err*`), the clocks, timeout channels (`async/timeout`, `async/<!!` = sleep), `js/emit` `js/url-param` |
24+| 13 | `lang.lg` | `wasm.lang` | 1-4 8 | `iterate`, `transformer-seq*` (`sequence` with a transducer), `->AssertionError` (`assert`) |
25+| 14 | `term.lg` | `wasm.term` | 1-4 8 | the `term/*` natives as term_wasm.go defines them: ANSI escapes on fd 1, `read-key` / `key-pending?` / `size` over three term intrinsics (`term-read-key` `term-key-pending` `term-size`, D88 imports) defined there, not in `intrinsics.lg` |
26+
27+`seq.lg` requires neither `str.lg` nor the collections, so the value model
28+has no cycle: anything that must dispatch on a box lives in seq.lg, and the
29+collections reach seq.lg's generic natives through hooks. The link step is
30+one call, `(wasm.core/install!)`: maps (slot 0) and sets (slot 1) through
31+`wasm.phs/install-hooks!`, wasm.core's own foreign values (transients, types,
32+meta'd keywords/symbols) in the generic slot 2, which foreign values are
33+seqable (`wasm.seq/set-seqable-hook!`: maps, sets, transient maps; for the
34+others first/rest/seq/reduce/map raise their own message), the printer
35+wasm.str uses for
36+foreign values (`set-print-hook!`, called with a mode: 0 `Value.String()`,
37+1 `pr-str`, 2 `print-str`; a map's String() has no commas, its pr-str does),
38+and the printer seq.lg hashes Range/Repeat/PVecSeq elements with
39+(`wasm.seq/set-print-hook!`, given `wasm.str/value-string`), and the type
40+namer wasm.arrays and wasm.seq use in their messages for foreign values
41+(`wasm.arrays/set-type-name-hook!`, `wasm.seq/set-type-name-hook!`: both load
42+before wasm.core, so they cannot call `type-name`).
43+
44+File names must match `[a-z_]+\.lg`: `src/lw_rt.lg` reads this table
45+with that pattern, and a row it cannot match is silently not loaded by the
46+backend (why the XXH3 file is `xxhash.lg`).
47+
48+Runtime globals (D39), one per namespace that has state: `wasm.seq/hooks`
49+(three Handler slots, the hashing printer, the seqable and ifn hooks, the type namer), `wasm.str/globals` (intern
50+table, its count, the print hook), `wasm.core/globals` (gensym counter,
51+interned types), `wasm.arrays/globals` (the type-name hook),
52+`wasm.math/globals` (rand-int's xorshift state), `wasm.xxhash/globals` (the
53+default secret, built on first use) and `wasm.host/globals` (the stdout and
54+stderr handles).
55+
56+## Kind table (`wasm.seq/kind`, the one dispatch point)
57+
58+| # | kind | struct (in seq.lg unless noted) |
59+|---|---|---|
60+| 0 | nil | ref.null |
61+| 1 | int | i31 when it fits 31 bits signed, else `Int` (D41) |
62+| 2 | EmptyList | `List` with count 0 |
63+| 3 | List | `List` |
64+| 4 | Cons | `Cons` |
65+| 5 | LazySeq | `LazySeq` |
66+| 6 | ChunkedCons | `ChunkedCons` |
67+| 7 | Range | `Range` |
68+| 8 | InfiniteRange | `InfiniteRange` |
69+| 9 | Repeat | `Repeat` |
70+| 10 | PVecSeq | `PVecSeq` (vec, i, chunk length): PersistentVectorSeq or ArrayVectorSeq, by the vector's pkind |
71+| 11 | PVec | `wasm.pvec/PVec` (pkind 0 ArrayVector, 1 PersistentVector, D73) |
72+| 12 | ArrayChunk | `ArrayChunk` |
73+| 13 | ChunkBuffer | `ChunkBuffer` |
74+| 14 | Reduced | `Reduced` |
75+| 15 | Bool | `Bool` |
76+| 16 | Fn | `Fn` (D52: code 0-2, env, code 3-4, `FnInfo`) |
77+| 17 | Str | `Str` (UTF-8 bytes, cached hash) |
78+| 18 | foreign | anything else: `wasm.phm/HMap`, `wasm.phs/HSet`, ... via hooks |
79+| 19 | Char | `Char` |
80+| 20 | Kw | `Kw` (interned by wasm.str) |
81+| 21 | Sym | `Sym` (interned by wasm.str) |
82+| 22 | Float | `Float` |
83+| 23 | MapEntry | `MapEntry` (key, val): what a map's seq yields; = and hash as the 2-vector, but a Seq, and the only thing `key`/`val` accept |
84+| 24 | Atom | `Atom` (the backend's `$Atom`: one mutable slot) |
85+| 25 | Volatile | `Volatile` (same shape) |
86+| 26 | Err | `Err` (the backend's `$Err` plus a cause: kind 0 ex-info / 1 raw / 2 caught, msg, caught msg, data, cause) |
87+| 27 | MapSeq/SetSeq | `ArrSeq` (arr, i, flavour 0 MapSeq / 1 SetSeq; P2.13, R5): the seq of a map, a set or a transient map, built by phm/phs's seq hooks. PersistentList type, sequential `=`, counted, not chunked; hashes by FNV of String() (no `Hash()`); `conj` on it is native's recovered panic `interface conversion: vm.Seq is *vm.Cons, not *vm.List` |

89+wasm.core refines kind 18 with `ckind`: 30 map, 31 set, 32 TransientMap
90+(phm's `HTransient`), 33 TransientSet (`TSet`), 34 TransientVector (`TVec`),
91+35 a `type` value (`TypeVal`), 36 a keyword/symbol with meta (`MetaNamed`),
92+37 a typed array (`wasm.arrays/Arr`; also its `type` id). Values of the
93+namespaces loaded after wasm.core stay plain kind 18 (wasm.host's `Handle`
94+and `Chan`): they have no `type` name or printed form yet.
95+
96+Equality and hash of every kind follow corpus/hash/SPEC.md (D19). Kind 18
97+dispatches through per-kind Handlers, slot 0 maps, 1 sets, 2 a generic
98+fallback (SEQ.md, "Composition hooks").

100+## Vector kinds (D73)
101+
102+A `PVec` records which Go type native lg would hold. Measured against
103+`lg-4e76921230`; `corpus/intrinsics/vkind_test.lg` checks every row's type,
104+hash, printed forms and seq view at sizes 0, 1, 31, 32, 33 (and 1057: four
105+producers by default, all under `SLOW=1`):
106+
107+| producer | native type |
108+|---|---|
109+| literal, `vector`, `(conj)`, `vec` of anything, `subvec`, `read-string`, `assoc`/`pop` of an ArrayVector | ArrayVector at any size |
110+| `conj` (and `assoc` at the end) onto an ArrayVector | ArrayVector while the result has <= 32 elements, then PersistentVector |
111+| `conj`/`assoc`/`pop` of a PersistentVector (down to empty) | PersistentVector, meta kept |
112+| `with-meta` (meta nil included) | PersistentVector |
113+| `persistent!` (so `into []`, `mapv`, `filterv`, even `into` onto a meta'd vector) | ArrayVector up to 32, else PersistentVector, never meta |
114+| `sort`, `reverse`, `keys`, `vals`, `rseq` | lists |
115+
116+What follows from the kind: an empty ArrayVector hashes mixFinish(1)
117+(1364076727), an empty PersistentVector as `()` (H1); a PersistentVector,
118+its seq and a Repeat print their elements through `Value.String()` in every
119+mode; the seq of a PersistentVector is `Sequence`, prints and hashes as
120+`(seq [whole vector])` and chunks by 32-wide leaf, while the seq of an
121+ArrayVector is `PersistentList`, prints from i and chunks 1, 2, 4, ...;
122+`type` and the messages that name a type follow.
123+
124+`wasm.pvec/varray` turns a trie built by `vconj` into an ArrayVector of any
125+size. **Backend note:** vector constants and `vector` calls are built as a
126+`vconj` chain from `empty-vec` (src/lower_wasm.lg:637, :665, :2107); past 32
127+elements that is now a PersistentVector, where native's literal is an
128+ArrayVector. Wrapping the chain in `wasm.pvec/varray` restores parity.
129+
130+## Hashing values with no value hash
131+
132+Atoms, volatiles and fns hash by pointer natively (a volatile by FNV of a
133+String() that embeds its address). The runtime has no address and no
134+per-object id slot (the `$Atom` and `$Fn` layouts are the backend's, D52/D53),
135+so each of the three kinds hashes to one constant: consistent with identity
136+equality and stable within a run, but not distinct between objects (a set of
137+atoms degrades to one collision node). Exceptions, type values, transients
138+and meta'd keywords/symbols are not Hashable natively either; they hash by
139+FNV-1a of their String(), here as there.
140+
141+## Declared differences (P2.10)
142+
143+- `(hash x)` of a NaN produced by arithmetic: native sees the hardware's
144+ default NaN (0x7FF8000000000000) while `##NaN` is Go's `math.NaN()`
145+ (0x7FF8000000000001). The reference `float-bits` cannot see NaN payloads
146+ and gives every NaN the latter; the real `f64-bits` intrinsic (D28) gives
147+ the engine's bits, and the backend then has to emit `##NaN` as
148+ `nan:0x8000000000001`.
149+- `upper-case`/`lower-case` map ASCII and Latin-1 and pass caseless scripts
150+ through (CJK, kana, Hangul, Indic, Hebrew/Arabic, symbols, emoji); other
151+ cased text is a `lower-wasm:` named limit (Unicode case tables not ported).
152+ `(int ##NaN)` is a named limit (Go leaves it platform-defined).
153+- The Repeat type's own type is the Repeat type natively
154+ (`(type (type (repeat 1 1)))`): mirrored, like H1/M1.
155+
156+## Declared differences (P3.1)
157+
158+Measured against `lg-4e76921230`; `corpus/intrinsics/xsofy_natives_test.lg`
159+checks everything else live.
160+
161+- Arrays: `(seq arr)` is built when called, so a later `aset` is not seen
162+ through it (native's TypedArraySeq reads as it walks); only int and byte
163+ arrays exist (`double-array`, `object-array`, and `conj`/`empty` on an
164+ array, which make an object-array, are absent); calling an array as a fn
165+ is not routed.
166+- `float` is a Float holding float64(float32(x)): native's Float32 shares
167+ its type name, printed form, hash and `=`, but `(compare (float 1) 1.0)`
168+ throws natively.
169+- `/` of two Ints with a non-integral quotient (a Ratio) and
170+ `(/ MinInt64 -1)` (a BigInt) are named limits (D15).
171+- math/exp and math/pow follow Go's portable algorithms, which is what lg
172+ computes on wasm; native arm64 lg differs by 1 ulp on some inputs (fused
173+ multiply-add in exp_arm64.s and in compiled log/pow). Integral-exponent
174+ pow, sqrt, and xsofy's own exp inputs agree exactly.
175+- `rand-int` is a fixed-seed xorshift (native is OS-seeded); the
176+ `System/currentTimeMillis` origin is the host clock's, not the Unix epoch.
177+- `iterate` is a Cons over a LazySeq: `type` says PersistentList where
178+ native says Iterate.
179+- `->AssertionError` is a raw error (kind 1): message and uncaught text
180+ match; its class does not (native prints `#error {:type
181+ java.lang.AssertionError ...}`, and `(catch Exception e)` does not catch
182+ it natively).
183+- `xxh3/HashSeed` takes a byte-array, a String (its Chars truncated to
184+ bytes, as the reflection boundary converts it) or nil, with an Int or nil
185+ seed; other reflection coercions are named limits.
186+- IO: `flush!` is nil (native Syncs the fd, which fails on a pipe);
187+ `js/emit` validates the event name but not the data's JSON conversion;
188+ `js/url-param` is nil, as native off the browser; `let-go.core/now` is a
189+ named limit. Handles and timeout channels have no `type` name or printed
190+ form.
191+
192+## Twin markers
193+
194+Public defns that implement a let-go native carry `^{:twin "core/name"}`
195+(D58); `lg tools/twin-manifest.lg` lists them and
196+`checks/native-twins.sh corpus/natives/natives-shared.txt --exclude 'term/'`
197+scores what the shipped programs reach (MISSING 0 since P2.7). One-kind
198+entries (`massoc`, `vnth`, `sconj`, ...) carry no marker; the dispatching
199+entries do, and where wasm.core's dispatcher supersedes a seq.lg/str.lg one
200+(`conj`, `nth`, `peek`, `pop`, `compare`) the marker moved to wasm.core.
201+`slurp`, `open` and `read-string` are named-limit twins: they claim the
202+native and trap with a `lower-wasm:` message.
203+
204+## Errors
205+
206+Every namespace raises let-go's catchable errors as the backend's exception
207+value, `(throw (wasm/new sq/Err 1 msg cmsg nil nil))`, with native's exact
208+text: the backend lowers #'throw to `throw $lgex`. A native called as a value
209+reports unprefixed messages (msg = cmsg); `inc`/`dec`, being IR-op fns
210+natively, carry the "ExecutionError: " prefix once caught. Under native lg the
211+Err is a wasm ref, so only `catch Throwable` sees it. `wasm/trap` is kept for
212+invariant violations (`wasm.seq:`, `pvec:`, `phm:` prefixes: a hook not linked,
213+a count that disagrees with its walk) and `lower-wasm:` named limits (D74
214+sweep, P2.13). Messages that name a type use `wasm.seq/kind-type-name` for
215+seq.lg's kinds and wasm.core's namer for foreign values (Hooks slot 6,
216+installed by `install!`). Every test file's `res` tags a reference trap
217+`[:trap msg]`, apart from `[:err msg]`, so a trap never matches a catchable
218+native error.
219+
220+## read-string and edn.lg (plan D8)
221+
222+`read-string` is a named limit here. The plan (section 1, item 6) routes it
223+through `pkg/rt/core/edn.lg` compiled by the backend like any program, on the
224+premise that edn.lg is an lg EDN reader. At 4e769212 it is not: edn.lg's
225+`read-string` is one line, `(core/read-data-string s)`, a Go native, so
226+compiling edn.lg buys nothing until there is a reader written in lg. The
227+route that stays inside the campaign's rules is a reader in the runtime
228+dialect (or in plain lg compiled by the backend once top-level defs and
229+`case` chains lower, P1.6) checked against `read-data-string` the way
230+str.lg's printer is checked against `pr-str`; the float-literal half needs
231+the inverse of D45's formatter (Go's strconv parse) in the dialect.
232+
233+## Checks
234+
235+Run from `dev/lower-wasm/`:
236+
237+- `checks/run-intrinsics-native.sh`: every `corpus/intrinsics/*_test.lg`
238+ in one lg process, against native lg's own answers; exit 0 iff all pass
239+ and the test count equals the deftest count. Default tier under 90 s;
240+ `SLOW=1` adds the 10k map/set builds, every map/set path at 1000 keys and
241+ the 1e6 reduce gate (D51). `checks/gate.sh 2` sets `SLOW=1`.
242+- `checks/map-order.sh --native`: the map/set iteration-order corpus
243+ (corpus/maporder) is current against native lg.
244+- `checks/native-twins.sh <reach-list> [--exclude REGEX]`: natives a program
245+ reaches that no runtime defn claims.

1+# wasm.seq (P2.5 runtime half, integrated at P2.9, 2026-10-01)
2+
3+let-go's sequence machinery in the runtime dialect (`seq.lg`, ns `wasm.seq`),
4+checked against native lg by `corpus/intrinsics/seq_test.lg` via
5+`checks/run-intrinsics-native.sh`. Ground truth: let-go 4e769212. Paths are
6+under `pkg/vm/` unless they start with `rt/` (= `pkg/rt/`) or `core.lg`
7+(= `pkg/rt/core/core.lg`).
8+
9+## Kind table (`kind`, the one dispatch point)
10+
11+| # | kind | struct | Go type (`Type()` name) | Seq | Counted | Indexed | chunked | hash |
12+|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
13+| 0 | nil | null | | | 0 | | | 0 |
14+| 1 | int | i31 / `Int` | Int | | | | | hashUint64 |
15+| 2 | EmptyList | `List` count 0 | `*List` (PersistentList), list.go:41 | y | 0 | | | ordered, counts as one nil (H1) |
16+| 3 | List | `List` [first next count] | list.go:44 | y | O(1) | | | ordered (Go caches; we recompute) |
17+| 4 | Cons | `Cons` [first more] | cons.go:12 (PersistentList) | y | walks tail, cons.go:76 | | | ordered |
18+| 5 | LazySeq | `LazySeq` [fn s done err] | lazy_seq.go:16 (PersistentList) | y | walks | | via resolve | ordered; empty = EmptyList, :232 |
19+| 6 | ChunkedCons | `ChunkedCons` [chunk more] | chunk.go:112 (PersistentList) | y | **no** (count throws) | | y | ordered |
20+| 7 | Range | `Range` [start end step] | range.go:28 (Range) | y | O(1), :97 | y | y, 32 | **FNV of String()** |
21+| 8 | InfiniteRange | `InfiniteRange` [start step] | range.go:156 (Range) | y | **no** | | y, 32 | FNV of `"(range ...)"` |
22+| 9 | Repeat | `Repeat` [i val] | repeat.go:22 (Repeat) | y | `i`, **-1** when infinite | | | FNV of String() (`"()"` when infinite) |
23+| 10 | PVecSeq | `PVecSeq` [vec i clen] | of a PersistentVector: persistent_vector.go:183 (Sequence); of an ArrayVector: vector.go:198 (PersistentList) | y | O(1) | y | PV: leaves; AV: 1, 2, 4, ... | PV: FNV of `"(seq [whole vector])"`; AV: FNV of `"(e_i ...)"` |
24+| 11 | PVec | `wasm.pvec/PVec` [... pkind] | ArrayVector (pkind 0) or PersistentVector (1), D73 | | O(1) | y | | ordered over the elements; empty: AV mixFinish(1), PV EmptyList's |
25+| 12 | ArrayChunk | `ArrayChunk` [arr off end] | chunk.go:39 | | y | y | | |
26+| 13 | ChunkBuffer | `ChunkBuffer` [arr n] | chunk.go:225 | | y | | | |
27+| 14 | Reduced | `Reduced` | reduced.go:6 | | | | | |
28+| 15 | Bool | `Bool` | Boolean | | | | | 1/0 |
29+| 16 | Fn | `Fn` (D52's `$Fn`) | | | | | | |
30+| 17 | Str | `Str` [bytes, cached hash] | String | y, List of Chars (string.go:259) | runes | byte-bounded, rune-found | | FNV-1a, cached |
31+| 18 | foreign | anything else | maps, sets, ... | via hook | hook | | | hook |
32+| 19 | Char | `Char` [rune] | Char | | | | | hashUint64(rune) |
33+| 20 | Kw | `Kw` [ns name hash] | Keyword | | | | | stored (symbol hash + 0x9e3779b9) |
34+| 21 | Sym | `Sym` [ns name hash] | Symbol | | | | | stored |
35+| 22 | Float | `Float` [f64] | Float | | | | | hashUint64(float-bits) |
36+| 27 | MapSeq/SetSeq | `ArrSeq` [arr i flavour] | map.go:110 / set.go:131 (PersistentList) | y | O(1) | | | FNV of String() (P2.13, R5) |
37+
38+The boxes of 17 and 19-22 are declared here (D38, D48) and built by
39+wasm.str (`mk-str`, `kw-of-bytes`, ...), which owns interning, printing and
40+the string natives; `kind` tests them right after `Int` because they are the
41+common map keys. `equiv?` compares them before the identity fast path (one
42+NaN box is not `=` to itself): Str by bytes, Char by rune, Float by `==`,
43+Kw/Sym by text; across kinds always false, as native (`(= 1 1.0)` is false).
44+
45+"FNV of String()": Range, InfiniteRange, Repeat and PersistentVectorSeq do
46+not implement `Hashable`, so `HashValue` falls back to FNV-1a over the printed
47+form (hash.go:31). `(hash (range 3))` = 3057436279 while `(hash '(0 1 2))` =
48+3071521495. Reproduced for int/nil elements; other element kinds trap
49+(printing lives in wasm.str, which seq.lg cannot require; see Gaps).
50+
51+## Realisation rules (verified)
52+
53+- A LazySeq's thunk runs once, on the first First/Next/More/Seq/Count; its
54+ value goes through `Sequable.Seq()` (so a nested LazySeq is resolved and an
55+ empty collection becomes nil) and an empty result is cached as nil
56+ (lazy_seq.go:84-150). `realized?` = done or thunk consumed (:38).
57+- A thunk that throws stores its error and every later access rethrows it
58+ without re-running; `realized?` is then true (lazy_seq.go:59-68). When the
59+ thunk returns but realising its value throws (a nested lazy seq), native
60+ keeps nothing and the next access reads `()`: mirrored (P2.10, D74).
61+- `cons`/`rest` never force a lazy tail; `next` does (Cons.Next resolves,
62+ cons.go:49; ChunkedCons.Next, chunk.go:151). `seqOf` returns a LazySeq
63+ unresolved (rt/lang.go:1398); `seq` resolves it (rt/lang.go:2247 via
64+ `Sequable`).
65+- A thunk returning a non-seqable (e.g. `(lazy-seq 5)`) throws "don't know
66+ how to create ISeq from let-go.lang.Int" (lazy_seq.go:127).
67+- `(range n)` with n > 0 is a `Range` (lazy, O(1) count/nth, chunked); with
68+ n <= 0 or step 0 it is `EmptyList`, never an eager vector (range.go:188,
69+ rt/lang.go:5772). `(range)` is an `InfiniteRange`. `(repeat n x)` with
70+ n <= 0 is `EmptyList`; `(repeat x)` is `Repeat` with i = -1
71+ (rt/lang.go:6792).
72+
73+## Chunking rules (verified)
74+
75+- Chunk size is 32 (`rangeChunkSize = nodeCap`, range_chunked.go:11).
76+ Range chunks materialise up to 32 boxed ints; InfiniteRange always 32;
77+ PersistentVectorSeq exposes trie leaves and the tail, windowed at the
78+ current index (persistent_vector_chunked.go:34-82).
79+- Go natives that consume chunks: `map*` single-coll (mapLazy1 maps a whole
80+ chunk per thunk and emits a ChunkedCons, rt/lang.go:1480), `reduce`
81+ (rt/native_prims.go:367; Range takes a no-allocation arithmetic path,
82+ :438), `some` (:612), `nth` on a seq (nthInSeq, rt/lang.go:1453).
83+ `vec` (rt/lang.go:2054) and `count` walk element-wise.
84+- lg-defined core fns that chunk: `filter` (core.lg:523), `take` (whole chunk
85+ when it fits the quota, element-wise after, :574), `keep` (:1587), `dorun`
86+ /`doall` (chunk-next, :2748). `drop`, `concat`, `last`, `take-while` do not.
87+- Measured realisation (native = wasm.seq, both asserted live in the test):
88+ `(doall (take 3 (map f (range))))` 32; `(first (map f (range 100)))` 32;
89+ `(first (map f '(1 2 3)))` 1; `(count (take 33 (map f (range))))` 64;
90+ `(first (filter f (range 100)))` 32; the map-filter gate realises 224.
91+
92+## Generic natives by input
93+
94+| native | nil | pvec | string | map/set (foreign) |
95+|---|---|---|---|---|
96+| `seq` | nil | PVecSeq / nil | List of Chars / nil | hook seq |
97+| `first` `rest` `next` `second` | nil, `()`, nil, nil | via its seq | via its seq | via hook seq |
98+| `count` | 0 | O(1) | runes (lang.go:6105) | hook count |
99+| `nth` | nil / not-found | Indexed path, OOB throws | byte bound, rune walk; past the last rune nil (string.go:276) | seq walk via hook |
100+| `cons` | `(x)` (Cons, more = nil) | Cons onto its seq | Cons onto its seq | Cons onto hook seq |
101+| `conj` | List `(x)` | `vconj` | "conj expected Collection" | trap (owner's job) |
102+| `peek`/`pop` | nil | last / `vpop` | error | error |
103+| `reduce` | init or `(f)` | via chunked seq | via its seq | via hook seq |
104+| `vec` | empty pvec | copy | vector of Chars | via hook seq |
105+| `=` | nil = nil only | PersistentVector.Equals (nilListEquivalent) | bytes | hook equiv |
106+| `hash` | 0 | ordered | FNV-1a, cached | hook hash |
107+
108+Quirks reproduced on purpose (D19 spirit): `(count (seq (map inc (range 3))))`
109+throws (ChunkedCons is not Counted); `(count (repeat x))` = -1; `(peek (cons
110+1 nil))` throws; `(= '(nil) (lazy-seq nil))` is true (the `*List` branch walks
111+b unresolved, lang.go:1140); `(= [nil] [()])` true but `(= '(nil) '(()))`
112+false; `pop` on a Cons/LazySeq counts it first (walks to the end); nth3 on a
113+non-seqable returns not-found while nth2 throws; `(reduce nil :x nil)` = :x.
114+
115+## Composition hooks
116+
117+Kind 18 dispatches through one `Handler` per slot, so registrations never
118+overwrite each other: slot 0 maps (`wasm.phm/install-hooks!`), slot 1 sets
119+(`wasm.phs/install-hooks!`, which also calls phm's), slot 2 the generic
120+fallback (`set-hooks!`, kept for callers written against the single slot).
121+A Handler is `[pred seq count equiv hash]`, each a `Fn`; `(set-kind-hooks!
122+slot pred seq count equiv hash)` registers one, and a null `seq` clears the
123+slot. For a foreign value, `hook` asks slot 0's pred, then slot 1's, then
124+takes slot 2 (whose pred is null, matching everything); with nothing
125+claiming it, the value traps. equiv goes to the handler of whichever side
126+is foreign (a first) and must answer false for cross-kind pairs. Neither
127+runtime imports the other's, and seq.lg imports neither.
128+
129+## Gaps
130+
131+- `map*` covers one collection; the multi-coll path (chunkedHeads) is not
132+ ported. `list`/`conj` are fixed-arity (0-3 / 0-3) pending the backend's
133+ variadic-native convention. Float range bounds trap (`range-int`), as
134+ does any numeric-tower mixing (P2.7).
135+- List hash is recomputed, not cached (observationally identical).
136+- The FNV-of-String() hash of Range/Repeat/PVecSeq over elements that are
137+ not ints or nil traps: printing is wasm.str's, and seq.lg cannot require
138+ it. A print hook in seq.lg (as wasm.str has for foreign values) would
139+ close it.
140+- One runtime global (`hooks`), which the backend does not lower yet (D23).

@@ -0,0 +1,168 @@
1+# wasm.str (P2.6 runtime half, integrated at P2.9, 2026-10-01)
2+
3+Strings, chars, keywords, symbols and floats as values, `str`/`pr-str`/
4+`print-str`, float formatting and the string natives, in the runtime dialect
5+(`str.lg`, ns `wasm.str`). Checked against native lg by
6+`corpus/intrinsics/str_test.lg` via `checks/run-intrinsics-native.sh`. Ground
7+truth: let-go 4e769212 built with go1.27.1. Paths are under
8+`~/projects-new/3p/let-go/pkg/` unless they start with `go:` (Go's
9+`internal/strconv`).
10+
11+## Representation (D38)
12+
13+| box | fields | notes |
14+|---|---|---|
15+| `Str` | bytes (`wasm/Bytes`, UTF-8), `[:mut :i64]` cached hash, -1 = not yet | hash is FNV-1a over the bytes, cached on first `hash` |
16+| `Char` | `:i32` rune | any 0..0x10FFFF, surrogates included (`rt/lang.go:6665`) |
17+| `Kw` | ns bytes or null, name bytes, hash | built from the full `ns/name` text, split at the first `/` unless the text is `/` (`vm/symbol.go:79`); hash = `hashUnencodedChars(text) + 0x9e3779b9`; interned |
18+| `Sym` | same layout, symbol hash | interned in the same table, distinct from a keyword of the same text |
19+| `Float` | `:f64` | |
20+
21+The five structs are declared in wasm.seq beside `Int`/`Bool` (D38, D48),
22+and `sq/kind` numbers them: 17 Str, 19 Char, 20 Kw, 21 Sym, 22 Float (raw
23+`wasm/Bytes` is not a value; it falls to kind 18 and traps without a hook).
24+wasm.seq also owns their equality and hash, the UTF-8 walks (`decode-at`,
25+`rune-count*`), strings as collections, and `float-bits`; wasm.str builds
26+the boxes (`mk-str`, `mk-char`, `box-float`, `kw-of-bytes`, `sym-of-bytes`)
27+and owns interning, printing and the string natives. One runtime global
28+(`globals`, D39): the intern table (open addressing over `pv/Node`, load at
29+most 1/2), its count, and the print hook for foreign values.
30+
31+## Index semantics (measured, lg 4e769212)
32+
33+A let-go `String` is a Go string, so UTF-8 bytes, and its `RawCount()` is the
34+**byte** length (`vm/string.go:46`). The natives disagree on which unit they
35+use, and the port follows each one:
36+
37+| op | unit | source |
38+|---|---|---|
39+| `count` | runes | `CoreCount` special-cases String: `len([]rune(s))` (`rt/lang.go:6105`) |
40+| `seq`/`first`/`rest`/`next` | runes | `String.Seq()` builds a `List` of `Char`s (`vm/string.go:259`) |
41+| `subs` | runes, mapped to byte offsets by walking | `rt/lang.go:3165` |
42+| `index-of`/`last-index-of` | runes | `[]rune` + `runeIndex` (`rt/lang.go:4103`, `:4707`) |
43+| `nth` | **bound by bytes, found by runes** | `Nth` takes the `vm.Indexed` path (`rt/native_prims.go:155`) and checks `i >= RawCount()`; `ValueAtOr` walks runes and returns `NIL` past the last rune (`vm/string.go:276`) |
44+| `compare`, `=`, hash | bytes | `string(a) < string(b)` (`vm/compare.go:69`) |
45+
46+So `(nth "héllo" 5)` and `(nth "héllo" 5 :nf)` are both `nil` (5 is inside
47+the 6 bytes but past the 5 runes), while index 6 throws / returns `:nf`.
48+Reproduced on purpose, in D19's spirit. `compare` is byte order:
49+`(compare "￿" "𝄞")` is -1 where UTF-16 order would give 1. Invalid
50+UTF-8 decodes as U+FFFD of width 1, as `utf8.DecodeRune` (strings built by
51+this runtime are always valid; the decoder is exact anyway).
52+
53+## Printing
54+
55+`str` is `strValue` at the top level (`rt/lang.go:5006`): nil is `""`,
56+strings and chars raw, `##Inf`/`##-Inf` as `Infinity`/`-Infinity`, everything
57+else `Value.String()`. Nested values always print readably (`(str [\a "b"])`
58+is `[\a "b"]`, `(str [##Inf])` is `[+Inf]`). `pr-str` is readable at every
59+depth; `print-str` is raw at every depth (`print_method.go:30`, measured:
60+`(print-str ["a" \b])` is `[a b]`). Multiple args: `str` concatenates,
61+`pr-str`/`print-str` separate with one space. Seq kinds print `( … )`, a
62+pvec `[ … ]`; maps and sets go through the print hook (`set-print-hook!`,
63+owned by phm/phs).
64+
65+String escapes (`String.String()`, `vm/string.go:309`), per rune:
66+
67+| rune | written |
68+|---|---|
69+| `"` `\` | `\"` `\\` |
70+| TAB CR LF BS FF | `\t` `\r` `\n` `\b` `\f` |
71+| other < 0x20, and 0x7F | `\uXXXX`, uppercase hex |
72+| invalid byte | U+FFFD (`WriteRune(RuneError)`) |
73+| everything else (0x80+, U+2028, …) | raw UTF-8 |
74+
75+Chars: `\space` `\newline` `\tab` `\return`, else `\` + the rune's UTF-8
76+(`vm/char.go:50`); a surrogate char encodes as U+FFFD, as Go's
77+`string(rune)`. The test checks every code point below 0x80 alone and inside a
78+string, plus non-ASCII samples.
79+
80+## Floats (plan open question 7: decided)
81+
82+`Float.String()` (`vm/float.go:60`): integral finite values print as
83+`FormatFloat(f, 'f', 1, 64)` (exact integer digits, then `.0`; `1e300` prints
84+all 301 digits), everything else as `FormatFloat(f, 'g', -1, 64)`: shortest
85+round-trip digits, `%e` when the decimal exponent is < -4 or >= 6 (`1e-07`,
86+`1.0000005e+06`), `NaN`, `+Inf`, `-Inf`.
87+
88+Algorithm, all in i64 with no tables: `float-bits` recovers the IEEE bits
89+from the f64 (below), then a literal port of Go's multiprecision `decimal`
90+(`go:decimal.go`: Assign, Shift, Round, RoundUp/Down; 800 digits) produces
91+the exact decimal of `mant * 2^(exp-52)`, and `roundShortest` (Go 1.26
92+`go:ftoa.go:262`, the `bigFtoa` shortest path that Go 1.27's faster
93+`shortFloat` replaced; both yield the unique shortest-then-closest string)
94+cuts it. The integral path skips `roundShortest`. Changes from Go that do not
95+change digits: shifts go 59 bits at a time instead of 60 so `10 * 2^k` fits a
96+signed i64, and `leftShift` writes right to left into scratch instead of
97+using the `leftcheats` table.
98+
99+`float-bits` is a stand-in for the `f64-bits` intrinsic D28 gives P2.2: it
100+scales `|x|` by exact powers of two into `[2^52, 2^53)`, reads the mantissa
101+with `f64-to-i64`, and rebuilds the exponent field (subnormals included). The
102+one thing float arithmetic cannot see is the sign of zero, so `float-bits`
103+uses one division, `(/ 1.0 x)`: the only non-dialect reference in the
104+runtime, whitelisted by name in seq_test's dialect test (`float-bits` moved
105+to `seq.lg` at P2.9, because Float hashing needs it there). NaN maps to Go's `math.NaN()` bit
106+pattern `0x7FF8000000000001` (`(hash ##NaN)` agrees).
107+
108+Proven coverage:
109+- `corpus/floats/pr-str.expected` (281 lines from `gen.lg`: the plan's list,
110+ 200 LCG values in [-1e6, 1e6], 1e-10..1e22, and 31 edge cases: subnormals,
111+ 2^53 neighbours, the %e/%f switches, MaxFloat): **281/281 byte-exact**, and
112+ each line is re-derived live from native lg (stale snapshot fails).
113+ `(str x)` and `(hash x)` also match native for every corpus value; the hash
114+ match checks `float-bits` on all 281.
115+- A random sweep (scratch, not shipped, 2026-10-01): 10,000 doubles
116+ (4,000 17-digit mantissas over decimal exponents -330..306, 3,000 short
117+ decimals, 3,000 values below 1e5 with up to 8 fractional digits),
118+ **0 mismatches** against native `pr-str`; 200 s under the reference
119+ intrinsics, so not in the 30 s test.
120+- `roundShortest`'s `inclusive` flag (boundary included when the mantissa is
121+ even) cannot change a `Float.String()` result: a non-integral double's
122+ rounding boundary has at least 18 significant digits, more than the 17 a
123+ shortest result can have, and integral values take the `'f'` path. A mutant
124+ with `inclusive` forced false passes the corpus, as this predicts; a mutant
125+ that rounds down instead of to nearest fails 48 lines.
126+
127+## Natives
128+
129+Scalar: `str` `pr-str` `print-str` (arities 0-3 and `-seq` forms taking the
130+argument list, until the backend's variadic convention), `float->str`,
131+`name` `namespace` `keyword` (1, 2) `symbol` (1, 2) `char` `int` `compare`
132+`equals`/`equiv?` `hash`. String: `subs` (2, 3) `split` (core/split =
133+`strings.SplitN`, returns a List; clojure.string/split is lg code over it)
134+`includes?` (= string/includes?) `starts-with?` `ends-with?` `index-of`
135+`last-index-of` `trim` (`strings.TrimSpace`, Unicode spaces) `triml`
136+`trimr` (cutset ` \t\n\r`) `upper-case` `lower-case` `string-upper-case`
137+(clojure.string/upper-case: coerces with `str`) `str-replace` (literal
138+match, string or fn replacement; `""` matches before each rune and at the end)
139+`parse-long`. `count` `nth` `seq` `first` `rest` `next` `equiv?` `equals`
140+`hash` remain as names here but are wasm.seq's own natives, which have been
141+string-aware since P2.9.
142+
143+lg-defined fns that reach these through the backend for free:
144+`clojure.string/join`, `split`, `split-lines`, `blank?`, `capitalize`,
145+`replace`, `reverse`, `escape`, `starts-with?`/`ends-with?` wrappers.
146+
147+## Gaps (named, not silent)
148+
149+- Case mapping of non-ASCII text traps (`strings.ToUpper/ToLower` are
150+ Unicode). Regex separators/patterns are not in the value model.
151+- Errors whose let-go message embeds a value or a type name
152+ (`"3000000000 can't be coerced to int"`, `"value out of range for char: -1"`,
153+ `"cannot compare let-go.lang.String and …"`, `"keyword name must be a string,
154+ got …"`) trap with the static part until ex-info exists (P2.7); the test
155+ checks these with `same-err` (both throw). Static messages are compared
156+ exactly.
157+- `(int ##NaN)` traps: Go's `int(math.Trunc(NaN))` is platform-defined.
158+ `(last-index-of s x -5)` traps where native lg panics.
159+- `str-replace-first`, `format`, `println`/`pr` output, `re-*` not done.
160+
161+## seq.lg patch (applied at P2.9)
162+
163+Steps 1-4 of the proposal are in: the structs, the `kind` numbers, the
164+string walks (`string-seq`, `string-nth`, `decode-at`, `rune-count*`) and
165+the scalar cases of `equiv?`/`hash*` live in seq.lg, and `float-bits` moved
166+with them so seq.lg never requires wasm.str. Step 5 stands: `fnv-elem` (the
167+hash of a Range/Repeat/PVecSeq over non-int elements) still needs printing
168+and traps (SEQ.md, Gaps).

1+# tools/ — the native-twin instrument (P2.8)
2+
3+The question these answer: which Go natives does a program reach that the
4+wasm runtime does not provide yet? Four pieces, run from `dev/lower-wasm/`
5+with the pinned lg (`~/projects-new/3p/lg-bin/lg-4e76921230`):
6+
7+| Tool | Output |
8+|---|---|
9+| `lg tools/native-inventory.lg` | `corpus/natives/inventory.tsv`: every native var in a stock lg |
10+| `lg tools/twin-manifest.lg` | the natives the runtime claims (`:twin` markers) |
11+| `lg tools/twin-manifest.lg --propose` | `corpus/natives/manifest-proposed.tsv`: the markers to apply |
12+| `tools/reach.sh <root> <prefix> [ns…]` | a reach list (`corpus/natives/natives-*.txt`) |
13+| `checks/native-twins.sh <reach-list>` | what is missing; exit 0 iff nothing |
14+
15+## Inventory
16+
17+The var list is runtime truth: every public var, in every ns a stock lg
18+loads, whose value is a `NativeFn`. The Go sources supply only `file:line`,
19+arity and registration style, and are read with `git show` at the SHA the
20+binary reports in `lg -version`, so a let-go checkout that has moved on does
21+not skew them. Columns:
22+
23+- `arities`: `2,3` for fixed arities, `>=N` for a variadic Go signature, `?`
24+ when the Go side checks arity at run time (the `func(vs []vm.Value)`
25+ proxies). Most `//lg:native` prims are declared `vs ...vm.Value`, so `>=0`
26+ means "checked inside", not "takes anything".
27+- `registered-via`: `lg:native` (the directive `cmd/lgprimgen` consumes),
28+ `ns.Def`, or `other` (`LookupOrAdd(vm.Symbol(…))` in `compiler/eval.go`,
29+ or an lg-level `(def ref atom)` alias in `pkg/rt/core/*.lg`).
30+- `match`: `exact` when the site's ns and name both agree; `name` when the
31+ Def's ns is computed (`installMathInto(nsName)`, `defStaticNS(nm)`) and
32+ only the name matched; `computed` for the exception-constructor spellings
33+ built by string concatenation. A `name` row can point at the wrong one of
34+ two same-named Defs; the source is then a hint, not proof.
35+- `same-fn-as`: the canonical member when several vars hold the very same
36+ NativeFn (`string/trim` is `core/trim`, `hash/xxh3-64` is `xxh3/Hash`). A
37+ twin for one member covers them all.
38+
39+`corefns/` directives are ranked last: there the generated registrar only
40+records a direct-call descriptor, and the var itself is Def'd in `lang.go`.
41+
42+## Marker convention (proposed decision)
43+
44+A runtime defn that implements a native says so with `:twin` metadata on its
45+name, beside D24's `:intrinsic`/`:wasm`:
46+
47+```clojure
48+(defn ^{:twin "core/first"} first [x] …)
49+(defn ^{:twin ["core/count" "core/hash"]} f [x] …) ; one defn, several natives
50+```
51+
52+The value is the native's `ns/name` spelled with runtime ns names (`core`,
53+`string`, `os`), as in the inventory and the reach lists. The lg reader turns
54+`^{…} name` into `(with-meta name {…})`, which `twin-manifest.lg` reads from
55+source without loading the runtime. The form passes every dialect test
56+unchanged: markers on six defns across pvec/phm/phs/seq/str, including a
57+multi-arity defn and a vector value, gave `checks/run-intrinsics-native.sh`
58+66/66 tests, 0 failures (scratch copy, 2026-10-01). A claim of a name that is
59+not a native in the inventory prints a `WARN` in the twin report.
60+
61+Why metadata rather than a per-file `twins` table: the claim sits on the
62+defn it describes, so renaming or deleting the defn takes the claim with it.
63+
64+## Applying the proposal (P2.9)
65+
66+`manifest-proposed.tsv` name-matches today's public runtime defns to the
67+inventory, with a confidence column:
68+
69+- `high`: same name, one defining file.
70+- `medium`: same name, but the string-kind copy still lives in `str.lg` until
71+ D48 folds it into `seq.lg`; or a renamed entry with the same semantics
72+ (`equals` → `core/=`, which is binary where `=` is variadic).
73+- `low`: a one-kind entry point (`massoc`, `vnth`, `sconj`, …). Mark the
74+ dispatching entry P2.9 builds, not these.
75+
76+Until any marker exists, `checks/native-twins.sh` counts every proposed row,
77+`low` included, under a `PROPOSED MANIFEST` banner; once one marker lands it
78+reads only the markers.
79+
80+## Reach lists
81+
82+`tools/reach.sh` calls `../emit-wasm-probe/reach.lg` in place from a scratch
83+dir of symlinks (reach.lg writes to its cwd and slurps fixtures relative to
84+it). The header gives the invocations that reproduce the probe's xsofy and
85+legmacs lists, and `natives-shared.txt` is their `comm -12`.

1+# WasmGC backend campaign: summary for Matt (internal)
2+
3+Written 2026-10-01 evening, finalised 20:30. **Skunkworks: nothing pushed, no PR, no issue.**
4+Everything is local commits on joint `main` under `dev/lower-wasm/`
5+(≈45 commits since the plan). Ground truth: `dev/lower-wasm/STATUS.md`,
6+`DECISIONS.md` (D1–D120), `checks/items.tsv`, `FINDINGS.md`.
7+
8+## Headline
9+
10+**The plan's finish line is reached.** xsofy's real `main.lg`, compiled by
11+a new WasmGC backend walking let-go's IR, boots in the unmodified
12+`xsofy-shell.html` and renders a byte-identical screen to the stock-Go
13+lane at seed 424242 (settle-based scripted walk, identical on 4 consecutive
14+runs). Measured on the same loaded laptop (2026-10-01):
15+
16+| lane | bundle raw | brotli | time to title | time to map |
17+|---|---|---|---|---|
18+| **emitted WasmGC (lane 5)** | 497 KB | 140 KB | ~5.0 s | ~7.2 s |
19+| stock Go `lg -w` | 9.13 MB | 6.64 MB | ~10.9 s | ~16.4 s |
20+| TinyGo (2026-09-20 memory) | 2.3 MB | 1.27 MB | 8.7 s | 12.6 s |
21+
22+No cross-origin isolation needed (JSPI sleep and read-key instead of the
23+SharedArrayBuffer ring). World generation plus 60 turns is byte-identical to
24+native lg on 20 seeds, plus 200-turn runs with exploration, descent to
25+floor 2 and player death. Module alone: 1.84 MB emitted → 409 KB after
26+wasm-opt → 109 KB brotli. fib(32) runs at 1.37× the hand-written probe
27+with checked arithmetic kept.
28+
29+## Gates
30+
31+| phase | state | evidence |
32+|---|---|---|
33+| 1 backend complete on scalar code | PASSED (D62), review fixes landed (D92–D96) | 7 rows + 148-probe adversarial review, all 11 bugs fixed or refused by name; tail calls via `return_call` |
34+| 2 runtime + collections | PASSED with one named limit (D127): 13/14 rows; core tests **265/273 (97%)** under the backend, 14/14 oracle programs, map-order 14/14, hash parity 0 misses, native tier 116 tests / 37.8k assertions, fuzz 2300 seeds clean; the red row is one `to-array` deftest | `corpus/wasm`, `corpus/review2`, `corpus/core-tests-report.md` |
35+| 3 xsofy headless world-gen | PASSED (D113) | `checks/world-parity.sh 20` 20/20 |
36+| 4 xsofy in the browser | PASSED (D120) | `checks/gate.sh 4`; lane 5 identical |
37+| 5 legmacs | not started, by design | new decision |
38+
39+## What was built (dev/lower-wasm)
40+
41+- `src/`: `lower_wasm.lg` (the backend), `driver.lg` (multi-namespace,
42+ `-source-paths`), `lw_rt.lg` (compiles the runtime through the backend
43+ into a content-addressed rtlib cache, tree-shakes), `lw_ext.lg`,
44+ `testshim.lg`, `run.mjs`.
45+- `rt/wasm/`: the runtime written in the constrained lg dialect over 43
46+ intrinsics: pvec, HAMT map/set mirroring let-go's array-map/HAMT
47+ (iteration order parity incl. its bugs), seqs with chunk parity, strings
48+ with exact Go float formatting, EDN reader, core natives, arrays, math,
49+ canonical XXH3, host/term. Runs natively under reference intrinsics too.
50+- `host/`: browser/node/wasmtime host, JSPI, the import ABI (`ABI.md`),
51+ an adapter that loads the real shell unmodified.
52+- `checks/` + `corpus/`: one match relation (`oracle.sh`), every item a row
53+ with a runnable check, corpora as files (op matrix, hash vectors from
54+ `vm.HashValue`, map-order oracle, 14 oracle programs, world dump), two
55+ adversarial reviews, perf report.
56+
57+## Decisions you should know about
58+
59+- D4/D24: runtime in lg over intrinsics, not deftype, not WAT. It paid off:
60+ the backend compiles its own runtime, and the runtime was tested natively
61+ before the backend could run it.
62+- D19/D30/D79: parity INCLUDING let-go's quirks (hash of `[]` vs `()`,
63+ the collision-bucket dissoc bug, ArrayVector vs PersistentVector rules).
64+- D91: no COI for the JSPI lane. D99: xsofy's deepest stack is 20 frames.
65+- D106: check speedups adopted (slot pool, parallel corpus/census/tier,
66+ no sleep-polling); attestation reuse deferred.
67+- D83/D109: variadics were not optional; landed as a `$FnV` subtype.
68+
69+## Upstream-worthy findings (generic phrasing, not yet filed)
70+
71+`docs/project_incoming/letgo-upstream-findings-from-lower-wasm-2026-10-01.md`
72+plus D94/D101/D116: checked arithmetic marked pure in the op catalog (DCE
73+drops throwing ops, LICM hoists them), constfold identities on non-numbers,
74+`free-vars` scope bug in ir.build (closures capturing same-named locals),
75+name-only self-call typing in typeinfer, LICM validate failures, the
76+collision-bucket dissoc bug, `()`/`[]` hash split, -0.0 hash, the reader's
77+empty-list meta leak, `require` silently truncating on an unclosed form.
78+
79+## Open items and honest gaps
80+
81+- Closed since the draft: P2.14 landed at 265/273; P0.1 landed (checks run
82+ 2–3× faster, byte-identical); P2.GATE recorded (D127).
83+- `with-meta` on a variadic fn drops the variadic arity; identity hash of
84+ atoms/fns is per-kind; printing a fn is refused; `sort` incomparable-pair
85+ error may name a different pair; `*out*` rebinding is lexical.
86+- Perf per turn is 1.3–1.5× native lg on a loaded host; untuned.
87+- Everything was measured on a laptop at load 10–45; absolute times are soft,
88+ byte-identity results are not.
89+
90+## What to decide tomorrow
91+
92+1. Whether and how to surface this upstream (the backend itself is not
93+ secret: structurize's header anticipates it; the public why is size and
94+ speed). The upstream-findings dossier can go first, as plain bugs.
95+2. Phase 5 (legmacs: reflection, live compiler, regex, go blocks) as its
96+ own plan, or not.
97+3. Where the code lives long-term (D7 said out-of-tree first).
